title: Unit Tests: Tutorial Page Rendering Validation
description:
# Unit Tests: Tutorial Page Rendering Validation

## Background
The tutorial system (pkg/ui/tutorial.go) has 17+ content pages. We need tests to ensure:
1. All pages render without errors
2. Markdown formatting works correctly
3. Navigation between pages works
4. Progress tracking persists correctly

## Existing Tests (tutorial_test.go)
- Basic navigation tests
- Scrolling tests
- Some progress tests

## Additional Tests Needed

### Page Rendering:
1. Each page's content string is valid markdown
2. Each page renders through Glamour without error
3. No page exceeds reasonable width (causes wrapping issues)
4. Headers, lists, code blocks render correctly
5. Special characters (backticks, etc.) are escaped properly

### Page Navigation:
1. TOC correctly lists all pages
2. Clicking TOC item navigates to page
3. j/k navigation works in page list
4. Page content scrolls correctly
5. Progress indicator updates

### Progress Persistence:
1. Viewing a page marks it as viewed
2. Progress persists across sessions (mock file system)
3. CompletedOnce flag works correctly
4. LastPageID resume works
5. Corrupted progress file doesn't crash

### Context Filtering:
1. Pages filter correctly by context (list, board, graph, etc.)
2. Filtered view shows only relevant pages
3. Navigation within filtered view works

### Edge Cases:
1. Empty page content
2. Very long page content (scrolling)
3. Page with only code blocks
4. Page with mermaid diagrams
5. Wide terminal vs narrow terminal rendering

## Test Data
Consider test fixtures:
- Minimal page content
- Maximum page content (stress test)
- Various markdown elements

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All pages render without error
- [ ] Navigation tests are comprehensive
- [ ] Progress persistence is tested with mocks
- [ ] Context filtering is tested
- [ ] Edge cases don't cause panics
close_reason: Added 15 comprehensive test functions: all pages render, valid content/structure, line width, narrow/short/minimal terminals, markdown validation, TOC coverage, scrolling, sections, context filtering, Glamour rendering.

title: Unit test: suggest_all.go - Suggestion orchestration
description:
Create comprehensive unit tests for pkg/analysis/suggest_all.go

## File Overview
suggest_all.go orchestrates all suggestion types:
- Calls each individual suggester
- Combines and deduplicates results
- Applies global filtering and ranking

## Test Cases to Implement
1. **Orchestration Tests**
   - Empty graph produces no suggestions
   - Single suggester enabled
   - All suggesters enabled
   - Verify no duplicate suggestions across types

2. **Configuration Tests**
   - Test with each suggester enabled/disabled
   - Test confidence threshold filtering
   - Test maximum suggestions limit
   - Test type filtering

3. **Integration Tests**
   - Small graph with known suggestion opportunities
   - Graph with cycles (should produce cycle suggestions)
   - Graph with similar titles (should produce duplicate suggestions)
   - Graph with unlabeled high-impact items (should produce label suggestions)

4. **Ranking Tests**
   - Verify suggestions sorted by confidence
   - Verify deterministic ordering (stable sort)
   - Test tie-breaking behavior

## Implementation Notes
- Create fixture graphs with known properties
- Test each suggester independently first
- Then test orchestration combinations
- Benchmark full suggestion pipeline
close_reason: Comprehensive unit tests for suggest_all.go implemented: 24 tests covering config, orchestration, filtering, sorting, limits, deduplication, integration, and edge cases. All tests passing.

title: Tree: Integrate with main Model and add E shortcut
description:
## Purpose
Wire the TreeModel into the main Model, enabling users to toggle tree view with the `E` key and ensuring all state management works correctly.

## Integration Points

### 1. View() Dispatch (model.go)
Add case for focusTree in the View() method:

```go
func (m Model) View() string {
    // ... existing cases ...
    
    case focusTree:
        return m.renderTreeView()
    
    // ...
}

func (m Model) renderTreeView() string {
    // Handle split view vs full view based on width
    if m.width > SplitViewThreshold {
        return m.renderTreeSplitView()
    }
    return m.tree.View()
}
```

### 2. Update() Key Handling
Add focusTree case in the key handling switch:

```go
case focusTree:
    switch msg.String() {
    case "j", "down":
        m.tree.MoveDown()
    case "k", "up":
        m.tree.MoveUp()
    case "enter", " ":
        m.tree.ToggleExpand()
    case "l", "right":
        m.tree.ExpandOrMoveToChild()
    case "h", "left":
        m.tree.CollapseOrJumpToParent()
    case "g":
        if m.waitingForG {
            m.tree.JumpToTop()
            m.waitingForG = false
        } else {
            m.waitingForG = true
        }
    case "G":
        m.tree.JumpToBottom()
    case "o":
        m.tree.ExpandAll()
    case "O":
        m.tree.CollapseAll()
    case "E", "esc":
        m.focused = focusList
    case "?":
        m.toggleHelp()
    case "tab":
        m.focused = focusDetail
    }
    
    // Sync detail panel with selection
    if issue := m.tree.SelectedIssue(); issue \!= nil {
        m.updateDetailForIssue(issue)
    }
```

### 3. Keyboard Shortcut to Enter Tree View
In the focusList key handling, add `E`:

```go
case focusList:
    switch msg.String() {
    // ... existing cases ...
    
    case "E":
        // Enter tree view (bv-gllx)
        m.tree.Build(m.getFilteredIssues())
        m.focused = focusTree
    }
```

### 4. Window Resize Handling
Update tree viewport on resize:

```go
case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
    m.width = msg.Width
    m.height = msg.Height
    
    // ... existing resize handling ...
    
    // Update tree viewport dimensions
    m.tree.SetSize(m.width, m.height-headerHeight-footerHeight)
```

### 5. Filter Change Handling
Rebuild tree when filters change:

```go
func (m *Model) applyFilter() {
    // ... existing filter logic ...
    
    // Rebuild tree with new filter (preserves expand state)
    if m.focused == focusTree {
        m.tree.Build(m.getFilteredIssues())
    }
}
```

### 6. Detail Panel Sync
When selection changes in tree, update detail panel:

```go
func (m *Model) updateDetailForIssue(issue *model.Issue) {
    m.selectedIssueID = issue.ID
    m.updateViewportContent()
}
```

### 7. Context Help Integration
Add tree view help to context_help.go:

```go
const contextHelpTree = `## Tree View

**Navigation**
  j/k       Move up/down
  Enter     Expand/collapse
  h/←       Collapse or jump to parent
  l/→       Expand or move to child
  gg/G      Jump to top/bottom

**Expand/Collapse**
  o         Expand all descendants
  O         Collapse all

**Exit**
  E/Esc     Return to list view
  Tab       Toggle detail panel`
```

Update the context map:
```go
var ContextHelpContent = map[Context]string{
    // ... existing ...
    ContextTree: contextHelpTree,
}
```

### 8. Status Bar Updates
Show tree-specific info in status bar:

```go
func (m Model) renderStatusBar() string {
    // ... existing ...
    
    if m.focused == focusTree {
        info = fmt.Sprintf("Tree: %d nodes | %d roots | %d expanded",
            len(m.tree.flatList),
            len(m.tree.roots),
            m.tree.expandedCount())
    }
}
```

## State Synchronization

### Tree ↔ List Selection Sync
When entering tree view:
1. Find currently selected list item in tree
2. Set tree cursor to that node
3. Expand ancestors to make it visible

When exiting tree view:
1. Get currently selected tree node
2. Find that issue in list
3. Set list selection to that index

### Expand State Persistence
Store expanded IDs in Model (not just TreeModel):
```go
type Model struct {
    // ... existing ...
    treeExpandedIDs map[string]bool // Persist across tree rebuilds
}
```

## Error Handling

### Empty Tree
If no issues after filter:
- Show helpful message: "No issues match current filter"
- Allow exiting with E/Esc

### Missing Parents
If parent-child dep references non-existent ID:
- Log warning (debug mode)
- Treat issue as root node
- Do not crash

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `E` key enters tree view from list
- [ ] `E` or `Esc` exits tree view to list
- [ ] All navigation keys work as documented
- [ ] Detail panel syncs with tree selection
- [ ] Filter changes rebuild tree correctly
- [ ] Window resize adjusts tree viewport
- [ ] Context help shows tree shortcuts
- [ ] Status bar shows tree statistics
- [ ] Selection preserved when switching views
close_reason: Integrated TreeModel with main Model: E key toggles tree view, all navigation keys (j/k/h/l/g/G/o/O/ctrl+d/u/enter/tab/E/esc) work, mouse scroll support, detail panel sync via tab. Build and tests pass.

title: Help Modal Tutorial Entry Point (Space key)
description:
# Help Modal Tutorial Entry Point (Space key)

## Background
The **primary discoverable path** to the tutorial is through the help modal. When user presses \`?\`, they see the shortcuts reference. From there, pressing \`Space\` launches the full interactive tutorial.

This is better than relying solely on CapsLock because:
1. **Discoverable** - Help modal can show hint
2. **Reliable** - Space works on all terminals
3. **Progressive** - Natural flow from quick reference to detailed tutorial
4. **Intuitive** - "I need more help" → press Space for more

## User Flow

\`\`\`
User presses ? 
    │
    ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Keyboard Shortcuts                                    │
│  ─────────────────                                     │
│  Navigation                                            │
│    j/k     Move up/down                                │
│    Enter   View details                                │
│    ...                                                 │
│                                                        │
│  Views                                                 │
│    b       Kanban board                                │
│    g       Graph view                                  │
│    ...                                                 │
│                                                        │
│  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│  Space: Interactive Tutorial │ Esc: Close │ ;: Sidebar │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼ (user presses Space)
                    │
            Full Tutorial opens
\`\`\`

## Implementation

### Update Help Modal View
Add footer hint in the help overlay:

\`\`\`go
func (m Model) renderHelp() string {
    // ... existing help content ...
    
    footer := helpFooterStyle.Render(
        "Space: Interactive Tutorial │ Esc: Close │ ;: Toggle Sidebar",
    )
    
    return lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, content, footer)
}
\`\`\`

### Handle Space in Help Modal
\`\`\`go
func (m Model) handleHelpKeys(msg tea.KeyMsg) Model {
    switch msg.String() {
    case " ": // Space
        m.showHelp = false
        m.showTutorial = true
        m.tutorialModel.SetContextMode(false, "") // Full tutorial
        return m
    case "escape", "q", "?":
        m.showHelp = false
        return m
    // ... existing scroll handling ...
    }
    return m
}
\`\`\`

## Visual Design for Hint
- Footer should be subtle but visible
- "Space" highlighted in key style (like other shortcuts)
- "Interactive Tutorial" clearly indicates what happens
- Consistent with overall help modal styling

## Alternative Entry Points (for reference)
After this task, tutorial can be accessed via:
1. \`?\` → \`Space\` (primary, discoverable)
2. \`CapsLock\` (power user shortcut)
3. \`CapsLock\` double-tap (context help)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Help modal footer shows Space hint
- [ ] Space from help modal opens full tutorial
- [ ] Help modal closes when tutorial opens
- [ ] Hint styling is consistent with theme
- [ ] No conflicts with existing help modal keys

## Testing
- Verify Space opens tutorial
- Verify other help modal functionality unaffected
- Verify hint is visible at various terminal sizes

## Dependencies
Depends on: Tutorial Model Infrastructure (needs tutorial to open)
Should coordinate with: CapsLock Key Detection (alternative entry)

title: Implement interactive deployment wizard (--pages flag)
description:
# Implement Interactive Deployment Wizard (--pages flag)

## Context
The deployment wizard is an interactive CLI experience (like mcp_agent_mail's share wizard) that guides users through exporting and deploying their static site.

## Requirements

### New CLI Flag
```go
pagesWizard := flag.Bool("pages", false, "Launch interactive Pages deployment wizard")
```

### Wizard Flow
```
$ bv --pages

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║           bv → Static Site Deployment Wizard                     ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  This wizard will:                                               ║
║    1. Export your issues to a static HTML bundle                 ║
║    2. Preview it locally                                         ║
║    3. Deploy to GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages                 ║
║                                                                   ║
║  Press Ctrl+C anytime to cancel                                  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Step 1: Export Configuration
────────────────────────────
Include closed issues? [y/N]: n
Custom site title (default: "Project Issues"): My Project Dashboard
Custom subtitle: Sprint 42 Status

Step 2: Deployment Target
────────────────────────────
Where do you want to deploy?
  1. GitHub Pages (create new repository)
  2. Cloudflare Pages (fast global CDN)
  3. Export locally only

Choice [1]: 1

Step 3: GitHub Configuration
────────────────────────────
Repository name: my-project-status
Make repository private? [y/N]: n
Repository description: Issue tracker dashboard

Step 4: Prerequisites Check
────────────────────────────
✓ gh CLI installed and authenticated
✓ git configured (user: John Doe <john@example.com>)

Step 5: Export
────────────────────────────
Exporting static site...
  → Loading issues from .beads/beads.jsonl
  → Found 178 issues (85 open, 93 closed)
  → Running graph analysis...
  → Generating triage data...
  → Writing JSON files...
  → Copying viewer assets...
✓ Bundle created: /tmp/bv-pages-abc123

Step 6: Preview
────────────────────────────
Preview the site before deploying? [Y/n]: y
Starting preview server at http://localhost:9000...
Press 'r' to refresh, 'd' to deploy, 'q' to quit

[Browser opens]

Step 7: Deploy
────────────────────────────
Creating GitHub repository...
✓ Created: johnsmith/my-project-status
Pushing to GitHub...
✓ Files pushed to main branch
Enabling GitHub Pages...
✓ Pages enabled

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    Deployment Complete! 🎉                       ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  Repository: https://github.com/johnsmith/my-project-status      ║
║  Live site:  https://johnsmith.github.io/my-project-status/      ║
║                                                                   ║
║  Note: GitHub Pages may take 1-2 minutes to become available     ║
║                                                                   ║
║  To update later:                                                 ║
║    bv --export-pages ./update-bundle                             ║
║    cd ./update-bundle && git add . && git commit && git push     ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### Implementation Structure
```go
// pkg/export/wizard.go

type WizardConfig struct {
    IncludeClosed   bool
    Title           string
    Subtitle        string
    DeployTarget    string // "github", "cloudflare", "local"
    RepoName        string
    RepoPrivate     bool
    RepoDescription string
    OutputPath      string
}

func RunWizard(beadsPath string) error {
    config := &WizardConfig{}
    
    // Step 1: Collect export options
    if err := collectExportOptions(config); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    
    // Step 2: Collect deployment target
    if err := collectDeployTarget(config); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    
    // Step 3: Check prerequisites
    if err := checkPrerequisites(config); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    
    // Step 4: Export bundle
    bundlePath, err := exportBundle(beadsPath, config)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    
    // Step 5: Preview
    if shouldPreview() {
        action := runPreview(bundlePath)
        if action == "quit" {
            return nil
        }
    }
    
    // Step 6: Deploy
    return deploy(bundlePath, config)
}
```

### Terminal UI
Use Go packages for nice TUI:
- `github.com/charmbracelet/huh` for forms (consistent with bubbletea)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` for styling
- Or simpler: `bufio.Scanner` + ANSI colors

### State Persistence
Save wizard config for future runs:
```
~/.config/bv/pages-wizard.json
{
  "last_repo_name": "my-project-status",
  "last_deploy_target": "github",
  "include_closed": false
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] --pages flag launches wizard
- [ ] All steps work interactively
- [ ] Prerequisites check validates tools
- [ ] Preview server works with key controls
- [ ] GitHub deployment creates/updates repo
- [ ] Success message shows correct URLs
- [ ] Config saved for next run
- [ ] Ctrl+C cleanly exits at any step
- [ ] Works in non-TTY with sensible defaults

## Error Handling
- gh not installed: Offer to install (brew) or show manual instructions
- gh not authenticated: Run `gh auth login` inline
- Repo exists: Option to update or choose new name
- Network errors: Clear message with retry option

title: Agent Swarm Protocol: Multi-Agent Coordination
description:
Enable multiple AI agents to work on the same project without conflicts.

## INTEGRATION PRINCIPLES FOR AI AGENTS

### Problem This Solves
Without coordination, multiple agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) will:
- Work on the same issues simultaneously
- Edit the same files causing merge conflicts
- Duplicate effort or produce conflicting changes

### How It Integrates With Existing Commands
This feature AUGMENTS existing commands, doesn't replace them:

1. **--robot-plan** will include a new field:
   ```json
   {
     "tracks": [...],
     "agent_claims": {
       "bv-42": {"agent": "claude-opus-1", "claimed_at": "...", "expires_at": "..."}
     },
     "available_for_claim": ["bv-43", "bv-44"]  // Excludes claimed work
   }
   ```

2. **--robot-priority** will filter out claimed items by default:
   ```json
   {
     "recommendations": [...],  // Only unclaimed items
     "claimed_by_others": 3     // How many filtered out
   }
   ```

### Self-Documenting Output Pattern
Every agent-related robot command MUST include an 'explanation' field:
```json
{
  "command": "--robot-agents",
  "result": {...},
  "explanation": {
    "what": "Shows all agents currently registered on this project",
    "when_to_use": "Before starting work to see who else is active",
    "action": "If you see other agents, use --robot-claim to reserve your work"
  }
}
```

### Claim Expiration
Claims auto-expire after 30 minutes of no heartbeat. This prevents orphaned claims from blocking work.

### File Hints Are Advisory
File reservation hints are NOT locks - they're signals to other agents. An agent seeing a conflict should:
1. Check if the other agent is still active (recent heartbeat)
2. If inactive > 30min, proceed with work
3. If active, choose different work or coordinate

Labels: [agent-swarm coordination]

title: Unified Triage Intelligence
description:
# Unified Triage Intelligence: The Mega Command

**This is THE primary entry point for AI agents using bv.**

## Vision

Instead of agents calling 5-10 different robot commands and mentally merging results, `--robot-triage` provides EVERYTHING an agent needs in ONE call:

- What should I work on? (recommendations)
- Are there fires to put out? (alerts)
- Who else is working? (team awareness)
- Will I conflict with anyone? (file conflicts)
- What's the project health? (stats, graph, labels)
- Any handoffs waiting for me? (collaboration)

## Design Principles

1. **One call = full context** - Agent calls triage once, has everything
2. **Critical first** - Alerts before recommendations
3. **Actionable throughout** - Every section says what to DO
4. **Self-documenting** - Output explains itself
5. **Team-aware** - Multi-agent coordination built-in
6. **Progressive detail** - Summaries by default, deep-dive commands available

## Output Structure (Priority Order)

```
1. meta           - Command info, timestamp, data hash
2. quick_ref      - One-line summary for fast parsing
3. alerts         - Critical issues FIRST (fires before features)
4. top_pick       - THE #1 recommendation with full reasoning
5. your_session   - Your claims, handoffs, context
6. team           - Other agents, conflicts, available tracks
7. recommendations- Next 5 items after top_pick
8. quick_wins     - Low-effort high-impact items
9. blockers       - Items that unblock the most work
10. project_health- Stats, graph health, label health, drift
11. suggestions   - Hygiene hints (missing deps, stale claims)
12. commands      - Exact commands for next steps
```

## Relationship to Other Commands

`--robot-triage` INCLUDES summaries from:
- Agent Swarm (team, your_session, conflicts)
- Proactive Alerts (alerts section)
- Priority scoring (recommendations, top_pick)
- Labels View (project_health.labels)
- Execution Plan (available tracks)
- History (your_session context)
- Drift (project_health.drift)
- Suggestions (suggestions section)

Individual commands remain for DEEP DIVES:
- `--robot-plan` for full execution tracks
- `--robot-insights` for complete graph metrics
- `--robot-agents` for detailed agent activity
- `--robot-alerts` for full alert details
- `--robot-history` for commit correlation

## Companion: --robot-next

For agents that just want ONE answer:
```bash
bv --robot-next  # Returns ONLY top_pick, nothing else
```

## Success Criteria

An AI agent should be able to:
1. Call `--robot-triage` at session start
2. Immediately understand what to work on
3. Know if there are any critical issues
4. See team context without additional calls
5. Get exact commands for next actions

title: Proactive Alerts Engine
description:
Background analysis that surfaces issues PROACTIVELY (not just when asked).

## RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING DRIFT SYSTEM

pkg/drift/drift.go ALREADY implements drift detection with:
- Alert types: new_cycle, pagerank_change, density_growth, blocked_increase
- Severity levels: critical, warning, info
- --check-drift and --robot-drift CLI

THIS FEATURE EXTENDS drift to add:
1. **Velocity anomaly detection** (new - not in drift.go)
2. **Individual issue staleness** (priority.go has staleness but per-issue, not alerting)
3. **Integration with triage** (alerts feed into --robot-triage)

## WHAT'S NEW vs WHAT EXISTS

| Alert Type | Exists? | Location |
|------------|---------|----------|
| new_cycle | YES | pkg/drift/drift.go |
| pagerank_change | YES | pkg/drift/drift.go |
| density_growth | YES | pkg/drift/drift.go |
| blocked_increase | YES | pkg/drift/drift.go |
| velocity_drop | NEW | This feature |
| stale_issue | NEW | This feature (per-issue, not aggregate) |
| abandoned_claim | NEW | Needs agent swarm |

## INTEGRATION PATTERN

Alerts should be INCLUDED in triage output, not a separate command agents must call:

```json
{
  "recommendation": {...},
  "alerts": [
    {
      "type": "velocity_drop",
      "severity": "warning", 
      "label": "database",
      "message": "Velocity dropped 40% this week (was 4/wk, now 2.4/wk)",
      "action": "Consider prioritizing database work or checking for blockers"
    }
  ]
}
```

## CONFIGURATION REUSE

Use existing .bv/drift.yaml for thresholds:
```yaml
# Existing drift thresholds
density_warning_pct: 50
blocked_increase_threshold: 3

# NEW alert thresholds (add to same file)
velocity_drop_threshold: 0.3  # 30% drop triggers warning
stale_days_warning: 14
stale_days_critical: 30
```

## DO NOT CREATE ALERT FATIGUE

Only surface alerts that are ACTIONABLE:
- Don't alert on everything
- Group related alerts
- Provide clear action steps

title: Tree: Implement View() rendering with lipgloss
description:
## Purpose
Render the tree structure as beautiful terminal output using lipgloss styling, matching the existing bv visual language.

## Visual Design Language

### Tree Characters (Box Drawing)
```
│   Vertical line (continuing)
├─  Branch (has siblings below)
└─  Last branch (no siblings below)
▸   Collapsed indicator (has hidden children)
▾   Expanded indicator (children visible)
•   Leaf node (no children)
```

### Complete Example
```
▾ 🎯 P1 EPIC-001 Auth system overhaul
│ ├─ • ✨ P2 FEAT-002 OAuth integration
│ ├─ ▾ ✨ P2 FEAT-003 Session management
│ │   ├─ • 📝 P2 TASK-006 Add session store
│ │   └─ • 📝 P3 TASK-007 Session timeout UI
│ └─ • 🐛 P1 BUG-004 Login race condition
▸ 🎯 P2 EPIC-005 Dashboard redesign (collapsed)
• ✨ P3 FEAT-100 Standalone feature (no children)
```

### Color Scheme (from existing theme)
| Element | Color | Lipgloss |
|---------|-------|----------|
| Tree lines | Muted | theme.Muted |
| Expand/collapse indicator | Secondary | theme.Secondary |
| Issue type icon | By type | Existing icon colors |
| Priority badge | By priority | Existing priority colors |
| Issue ID | Accent | theme.Accent |
| Issue title | Text | theme.Text |
| Selected row | Inverted | theme.SelectedBg |
| Status indicator | By status | Green/yellow/red/gray |

### Icons by Type (match existing)
```go
var typeIcons = map[model.IssueType]string{
    model.TypeEpic:    "🎯",
    model.TypeFeature: "✨",
    model.TypeBug:     "🐛",
    model.TypeTask:    "📝",
    model.TypeChore:   "🔧",
}
```

### Priority Badges
```
P0 = red background, white text
P1 = orange background
P2 = yellow background  
P3 = gray background
P4+ = dim gray
```

## Layout Modes

### Wide Terminal (width > 100)
Split view: Tree (60%) | Detail Panel (40%)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐
│ ▾ 🎯 P1 EPIC-001 Auth overhaul  │ EPIC-001                │
│ │ ├─ ✨ P2 FEAT-002 OAuth       │ ─────────────────────── │
│ │ ├─ ▸ ✨ P2 FEAT-003 Session   │ Auth system overhaul    │
│ │ └─ 🐛 P1 BUG-004 Login bug    │                         │
│ ▸ 🎯 P2 EPIC-005 Dashboard      │ Priority: P1 (High)     │
│                                 │ Type: Epic              │
│                                 │ Status: In Progress     │
│                                 │                         │
│                                 │ **Description**         │
│                                 │ Refactor the entire...  │
├─────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┤
│ E: Exit │ j/k: Navigate │ Enter: Expand │ ?: Help         │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Narrow Terminal (width < 100)
Full-width tree, Tab to toggle detail panel

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▾ 🎯 P1 EPIC-001 Auth system overhaul   │
│ │ ├─ ✨ P2 FEAT-002 OAuth integration   │
│ │ ├─ ▸ ✨ P2 FEAT-003 Session mgmt      │
│ │ └─ 🐛 P1 BUG-004 Login race condition │
│ ▸ 🎯 P2 EPIC-005 Dashboard redesign     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ E: Exit │ Tab: Detail │ Enter: Expand   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Rendering Algorithm

### Per-Node Rendering
```go
func (t *TreeModel) renderNode(node *TreeNode, isLast bool, prefix string) string {
    var sb strings.Builder
    r := t.theme.Renderer
    
    // Tree structure characters
    branch := "├─"
    if isLast {
        branch = "└─"
    }
    
    // Expand/collapse indicator
    var indicator string
    if len(node.Children) > 0 {
        if node.Expanded {
            indicator = "▾"
        } else {
            indicator = "▸"
        }
    } else {
        indicator = "•"
    }
    
    // Build the line
    treeChars := r.NewStyle().Foreground(t.theme.Muted)
    
    sb.WriteString(prefix)
    sb.WriteString(treeChars.Render(branch + " "))
    sb.WriteString(indicator + " ")
    sb.WriteString(renderIssueCompact(node.Issue, t.theme))
    
    return sb.String()
}
```

### Title Truncation
If title exceeds available width:
- Truncate with ellipsis: "Very long title that..."
- Ensure minimum visible: 20 chars before truncation
- Account for tree prefix width at each depth

### Viewport Scrolling
Use bubbles/viewport for:
- Scroll when tree exceeds terminal height
- Show scroll indicators (▲ ▼) at edges
- Ensure selected row is always visible

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tree renders with proper indentation
- [ ] Box-drawing characters align correctly
- [ ] Icons and colors match existing theme
- [ ] Selected row is visually distinct
- [ ] Split view works on wide terminals
- [ ] Truncation handles long titles gracefully
- [ ] Scrolling works for tall trees
- [ ] No visual glitches on resize

title: Define AgentRegistration and WorkClaim data types
description:
Core data types for Agent Swarm Protocol

## Data Model
```go
// .beads/agents.jsonl storage format
type AgentRegistration struct {
    Name        string    `json:"name"`         // "claude-opus-1"
    Model       string    `json:"model"`        // "claude-opus-4"
    Program     string    `json:"program"`      // "claude-code", "cursor", "devin"
    StartedAt   time.Time `json:"started_at"`
    LastSeen    time.Time `json:"last_seen"`
    ClaimedWork []string  `json:"claimed_work"` // bead IDs
    FileHints   []string  `json:"file_hints"`   // files being touched
}

type WorkClaim struct {
    BeadID    string    `json:"bead_id"`
    Agent     string    `json:"agent"`
    ClaimedAt time.Time `json:"claimed_at"`
    ExpiresAt time.Time `json:"expires_at"`  // auto-release after inactivity
    Reason    string    `json:"reason"`      // "implementing", "reviewing", "testing"
}
```

## Storage
- Store in `.beads/agents.jsonl` (same pattern as issues.jsonl)
- One line per agent registration
- WorkClaims embedded in AgentRegistration.ClaimedWork

## Heartbeat Logic
- Agent updates LastSeen on each operation
- Claims auto-expire after 30 minutes of inactivity (configurable)
- Stale agents (LastSeen > 1 hour) marked inactive

## Integration Points
- Triage considers claims (bv-147 ClaimPenalty)
- Graph viz can show claim status
- Alerts when claims conflict or expire

title: Implement work claiming and releasing
description:
Work claiming and releasing mechanism

## Commands
```bash
bv --robot-claim bv-42              # Claim a bead
bv --robot-claim bv-42 bv-43        # Claim multiple beads
bv --robot-release bv-42            # Release a claim
bv --robot-release --all            # Release all claims for this agent
```

## Claim Semantics
- Soft lock (advisory, not enforced)
- Auto-expires after 30 min inactivity (configurable)
- Renewed by heartbeat or explicit --robot-claim
- Other agents see claim but can override with --force

## Conflict Handling
- If already claimed by another agent: return warning, not error
- Include claim holder info so agents can coordinate
- --force flag allows override (for emergencies)

## Output Format (claim)
```json
{
  "explanation": {
    "what": "Work claim result",
    "when_to_use": "Before starting work on an issue",
    "action": "Proceed with work if granted, coordinate if conflict"
  },
  "granted": ["bv-42"],
  "conflicts": [
    {
      "bead_id": "bv-43",
      "holder": "claude-opus-2",
      "claimed_at": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z",
      "expires_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "message": "Claimed 1 of 2 requested beads"
}
```

## Integration with Triage
- Triage scoring (bv-147) applies ClaimPenalty to claimed items
- --robot-triage excludes your own claims from recommendations
- --robot-next never suggests items claimed by others

title: Implement unified scoring algorithm
description:
INCREMENTAL ENHANCEMENT on existing scoring

## What Already Exists (DO NOT DUPLICATE)
- `pkg/analysis/priority.go:ComputeImpactScores()` - composite scoring
- Existing weights: PageRank(30%), Betweenness(30%), BlockerRatio(20%), Staleness(10%), PriorityBoost(10%)
- `pkg/analysis/priority.go:ScoreBreakdown` - individual component tracking

## What This Adds (NEW VALUE)
TRIAGE-specific scoring that EXTENDS base scoring with:
1. Label health factor (from bv-99 labels view) - boost items in unhealthy labels
2. Agent claim factor (from bv-132) - reduce score for claimed items
3. Unblock impact factor - boost items that unblock many others
4. Quick-win factor - boost small items with high impact ratio

## Incremental Implementation (Graceful Degradation)

**Phase 1 (MVP):** Works with existing scoring only
```go
TriageScore = ComputeImpactScores() // 100% weight
```

**Phase 2 (Labels ready):** Add label health
```go
TriageScore = BaseScore*0.7 + LabelHealthBoost*0.15 + UnblockBoost*0.15
```

**Phase 3 (Agent Swarm ready):** Add claim penalty
```go
if claimedByOther { TriageScore *= 0.1 } // Heavily penalize claimed items
```

**Phase 4 (Attention scores ready):** Refine label factor
```go
// Replace simple label health with attention-weighted health
LabelHealthBoost = labelAttentionScore * 0.15
```

## Key Principle
Start simple, enhance incrementally. Never block triage on optional features.

## Output Format
```json
{
  "triage_scores": [{
    "issue_id": "bv-42",
    "base_score": 0.72,
    "triage_score": 0.85,
    "factors_applied": ["base", "label_health", "unblock"],
    "factors_pending": ["claim_penalty", "attention_score"]
  }]
}
```
close_reason: Implemented Phase 1 MVP scoring with unblock boost (15%) and quick-win factor (15%). All 29 triage tests passing. Ready for Phase 2 enhancements.

title: Implement --robot-triage command
description:
# --robot-triage: The Mega Command (Incremental Implementation)

**THE primary entry point for AI agents. One call = everything available.**

## Key Design Principle: Graceful Degradation

The mega-command works with WHATEVER features are available. Sections are included only when their underlying systems are ready:

| Section | Requires | Phase |
|---------|----------|-------|
| meta, quick_ref | Nothing | 1 (MVP) |
| recommendations | ComputeImpactScores() | 1 (MVP) |
| project_health.counts | Basic stats | 1 (MVP) |
| project_health.graph | Analyzer | 1 (MVP) |
| alerts | Proactive Alerts (bv-135) | 2 |
| your_session, team | Agent Swarm (bv-132) | 2 |
| project_health.labels | Labels View (bv-99) | 2 |
| history_hints | History (bv-62) | 3 |
| suggestions | Smart Suggestions (bv-137) | 3 |

**Missing sections return `null` or are omitted entirely.**

## Phase 1 MVP Output (Works Today)

```json
{
  "meta": {"command": "--robot-triage", "generated_at": "...", "data_hash": "..."},
  "quick_ref": {
    "top_pick": "bv-43: Implement auth middleware",
    "actionable_items": 33,
    "status": "ready_to_work"
  },
  "alerts": null,
  "top_pick": {
    "bead_id": "bv-43",
    "title": "Implement auth middleware",
    "score": 94.2,
    "why": ["Highest impact score", "Unblocks 5 items"],
    "claim_command": "bv --robot-claim bv-43"
  },
  "your_session": null,
  "team": null,
  "recommendations": [...],
  "quick_wins": [...],
  "blockers_to_clear": [...],
  "project_health": {
    "counts": {"total": 169, "open": 131, "blocked": 12},
    "graph": {"cycles": 0, "density": 0.15, "health": "good"},
    "labels_attention": null,
    "drift": null
  },
  "suggestions": null,
  "commands": {"claim_top_pick": "bv --robot-claim bv-43", "see_full_plan": "bv --robot-plan"}
}
```

## Full Output (All Features Enabled)

[Previous full specification remains valid - all 12 sections populated]

## Implementation Approach

```go
func ComputeTriage(agentName string) TriageResult {
    result := TriageResult{
        Meta: buildMeta(),
    }
    
    // Phase 1: Always available
    result.Recommendations = computeRecommendations()
    result.TopPick = result.Recommendations[0]
    result.ProjectHealth.Counts = computeCounts()
    result.ProjectHealth.Graph = computeGraphHealth()
    result.QuickWins = findQuickWins()
    result.BlockersToClear = findBlockers()
    
    // Phase 2: If agent swarm available
    if agentSwarmEnabled() {
        result.YourSession = getSessionContext(agentName)
        result.Team = getTeamStatus()
    }
    
    // Phase 2: If alerts available  
    if alertsEnabled() {
        result.Alerts = getAlerts()
    }
    
    // Phase 2: If labels view available
    if labelsEnabled() {
        result.ProjectHealth.LabelsAttention = getLabelHealth()
    }
    
    // Phase 3: If history available
    if historyEnabled() {
        result.HistoryHints = getHistoryHints()
    }
    
    // Phase 3: If suggestions available
    if suggestionsEnabled() {
        result.Suggestions = getSuggestions()
    }
    
    result.QuickRef = buildQuickRef(result)
    result.Commands = buildCommands(result)
    
    return result
}
```

## Usage

```bash
bv --robot-triage                    # Full output (whatever is available)
bv --robot-triage --compact          # Minimal: quick_ref + top_pick + alerts
bv --robot-triage --agent=claude-1   # Include agent-specific context
```

## Companion Command

`bv --robot-next` - Returns ONLY top_pick (~10 lines). Same incremental approach.

title: Implement --robot-next command
description:
# --robot-next: The One-Answer Command

**For when you just need ONE thing to work on. No context, no analysis, just an answer.**

## Usage
```bash
bv --robot-next                    # What should I do next?
bv --robot-next --skip=bv-42       # Skip specific bead
bv --robot-next --agent=claude-1   # Respect agent claims
```

## Output (Minimal by Design)

```json
{
  "next": {
    "bead_id": "bv-43",
    "title": "Implement auth middleware",
    "score": 94.2,
    "why": "Unblocks 5 items, label needs attention",
    "claim": "bv --robot-claim bv-43"
  },
  "alerts": 2,
  "your_claims": 1
}
```

That's it. ~10 lines of JSON.

## When to Use

| Scenario | Use |
|----------|-----|
| Starting fresh session | `--robot-triage` (full context) |
| Mid-session, need quick direction | `--robot-next` |
| Polling frequently | `--robot-next` |
| First time on project | `--robot-triage` |
| Debugging/investigating | `--robot-triage` |

## Behavior

1. Computes full triage internally (same as --robot-triage)
2. Returns ONLY the top_pick + minimal metadata
3. Respects agent claims (excludes items claimed by others)
4. Excludes your own claims (you already have work)
5. Applies --skip filters

## Edge Cases

**No work available:**
```json
{
  "next": null,
  "reason": "all_claimed",
  "suggestion": "Wait for claims to release or help with bv-42 (claimed by cursor-agent)"
}
```

**Critical alerts pending:**
```json
{
  "next": {
    "bead_id": "bv-43",
    "title": "Implement auth middleware",
    "claim": "bv --robot-claim bv-43"
  },
  "alerts": 1,
  "alert_preview": "CRITICAL: Dependency cycle detected",
  "suggestion": "Run bv --robot-triage to see full alert details"
}
```

## Implementation

Internally calls the same triage computation as --robot-triage, then:
```go
func RobotNext(agentName string, skip []string) NextResult {
    full := ComputeTriage(agentName)
    
    if len(full.Alerts.Critical) > 0 {
        return NextResult{
            Next: full.TopPick,
            Alerts: len(full.Alerts.Critical) + len(full.Alerts.Warning),
            AlertPreview: full.Alerts.Critical[0].Message,
            Suggestion: "Run bv --robot-triage to see full alert details",
        }
    }
    
    return NextResult{
        Next: full.TopPick,
        Alerts: len(full.Alerts.Warning),
        YourClaims: len(full.YourSession.Claims),
    }
}
```

## Relationship to --robot-triage

```
--robot-triage  = Full meal (everything you need)
--robot-next    = Snack (just the answer)
```

Both compute the same underlying triage. --robot-next just returns less.

title: Define Alert types and severity levels
description:
**CONSOLIDATE WITH EXISTING DRIFT ALERTS**

## What Already Exists (pkg/drift/drift.go)
```go
type Alert struct {
    Type     AlertType `json:"type"`
    Severity Severity  `json:"severity"`
    Message  string    `json:"message"`
    Details  string    `json:"details"`
}

type AlertType string  // cycle_introduced, density_change, blocked_ratio, pagerank_drift
type Severity string   // critical, warning, info
```

## What This Adds (EXTEND existing types)
Add new AlertType values for proactive alerts:
- stale_issue: Individual issue has been inactive too long
- velocity_drop: Label velocity decreased significantly
- blocking_cascade: Issue blocks many downstream items (opportunity)
- high_impact_unblock: Completing this unblocks high-value work
- abandoned_claim: Agent claim expired without completion
- potential_duplicate: Two issues appear similar (when semantic search available)

REMOVE cycle_risk - already covered by cycle_introduced

## Implementation Approach
1. REUSE: pkg/drift/drift.go Alert and Severity types
2. ADD: New AlertType constants to existing enum
3. ADD: Optional fields to Alert struct:
   - IssueID string (for issue-specific alerts)
   - Label string (for label-specific alerts)
   - DetectedAt time.Time

## Key Principle
ONE alert system, not two parallel systems. Drift alerts and proactive alerts share infrastructure.

## Extended Alert Struct
```go
type Alert struct {
    Type      AlertType `json:"type"`
    Severity  Severity  `json:"severity"`
    Message   string    `json:"message"`
    Details   string    `json:"details,omitempty"`
    // New fields for proactive alerts:
    IssueID   string    `json:"issue_id,omitempty"`
    Label     string    `json:"label,omitempty"`
    DetectedAt time.Time `json:"detected_at"`
}
```
notes: Extended AlertType enum with proactive variants + added issue/label/detected_at fields and timestamped drift alerts; groundwork for proactive engine

title: Implement staleness detection
description:
INCREMENTAL ENHANCEMENT on existing staleness calculation

## What Already Exists (DO NOT DUPLICATE)
- `pkg/analysis/priority.go:computeStaleness()` - returns 0-1 score
- Already normalizes to 30 days (items >30 days = 1.0 staleness)
- Already included in ImpactScore breakdown as StalenessNorm

## What This Adds (NEW VALUE)
ALERT GENERATION with configurable thresholds:
1. Configurable threshold (default: 14 days for warning, 30 days for critical)
2. Alert struct with severity levels: info, warning, critical
3. Status-aware staleness (in_progress items stale after 7 days is worse than open items)
4. Per-label staleness tracking (alert if entire label is stale)

## Implementation Approach
1. REUSE: `computeStaleness()` for base calculation
2. ADD: StalenessAlert struct { Type, Severity, IssueID, DaysSinceUpdate, Message }
3. ADD: CheckStaleness(thresholds) that generates alerts
4. ADD: Status multiplier (in_progress has lower threshold than open)

## Configuration (in .beads/config.yaml)
```yaml
alerts:
  staleness:
    warning_days: 14
    critical_days: 30
    in_progress_multiplier: 0.5  # in_progress warns at 7 days
```

## Output Format Example
```json
{
  "staleness_alerts": [
    {
      "type": "stale_issue",
      "severity": "warning",
      "issue_id": "bv-29",
      "days_inactive": 18,
      "status": "in_progress",
      "message": "Issue in_progress for 18 days with no commits - may be stuck"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Key Principle
Calculation exists; this adds THRESHOLD CHECKING and ALERT EMISSION.
notes: Implemented staleness alerts: config thresholds, in-progress multiplier, detected_at; added drift tests and default backfill.

Calculation exists; this adds THRESHOLD CHECKING and OPPORTUNITY ALERTS.

title: Auto-update mechanism with user confirmation
description:
Implement true auto-update for bv binary

## Current State
- Version check exists (notifies user when new version available)
- User must manually download and install

## Desired Behavior

### Interactive Mode
```
$ bv
New version available: v0.12.0 (current: v0.11.3)
Update now? [Y/n]: y
Downloading v0.12.0... done
Replacing binary... done  
Restarting... 
```

### Auto-Update Mode (opt-in)
```yaml
# .beads/config.yaml or ~/.config/bv/config.yaml
auto_update: true
auto_update_channel: stable  # stable | beta | nightly
```

When enabled, updates happen silently on startup (with brief notification).

### CLI Flags
```bash
bv --update              # Update now (interactive)
bv --update --yes        # Update now (non-interactive)
bv --check-update        # Just check, dont update
bv --set-auto-update     # Enable auto-updates
```

## Implementation Approach

1. **Download mechanism**
   - Fetch release info from GitHub API
   - Download appropriate binary for OS/arch
   - Verify checksum (SHA256)
   
2. **Safe replacement**
   - Download to temp location first
   - Verify binary runs (`bv --version`)
   - Atomic rename to replace current binary
   - Handle permission issues gracefully

3. **Rollback capability**
   - Keep previous version as `bv.backup`
   - `bv --rollback` to restore if issues

4. **Platform considerations**
   - Linux/macOS: Direct binary replacement
   - Windows: May need wrapper script for in-use binary
   - Homebrew users: Warn that brew manages updates

## Security Considerations
- Always verify checksums
- Download only from official GitHub releases
- Consider code signing for binaries
- Warn if running as root

## Edge Cases
- No internet connection: Skip gracefully
- Rate limited by GitHub API: Cache check results
- Binary in read-only location: Prompt for sudo or suggest manual update
- Running in CI: Never auto-update, just notify
close_reason: Implemented auto-update with --update, --check-update, --rollback, and --yes flags

title: History: Change Impact Analysis
description:
## Overview
Answer: 'If I modify this file, what open beads might be affected?'

## Why Agents Need This (Critical)
Before making changes, an agent MUST know:
- Are there open beads that touch these files?
- Could my changes conflict with in-progress work?
- What context should I be aware of?

## Implementation

### Impact Query
```go
func (h *HistoryReport) ImpactAnalysis(files []string) ImpactResult

type ImpactResult struct {
    AffectedBeads []AffectedBead
    RiskLevel     string  // low/medium/high
    Warnings      []string
}

type AffectedBead struct {
    BeadID       string
    Status       string
    OverlapFiles []string  // which of the input files this bead touches
    LastActivity time.Time
    Relevance    int       // how relevant (based on recency, file overlap %)
}
```

### Display in History
When agent is about to modify files:
```
⚡ Impact Analysis: auth/token.go, auth/session.go

   🔴 High Risk - Open beads on these files:
   • bv-123 (in_progress): Token refresh
     └─ Overlaps: auth/token.go (3 recent commits)
   
   🟡 Medium Risk - Recently closed:
   • bv-089 (closed 2d ago): OAuth foundation  
     └─ Overlaps: both files
   
   Recommendation: Check bv-123 before modifying auth/token.go
```

### Robot Command (PRIMARY USE CASE)
`bv robot impact auth/token.go auth/session.go`

Returns JSON that agent can use to decide whether to proceed or check context first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Impact analysis callable from robot command
- [ ] Risk level computed based on open beads
- [ ] Recency factored into relevance
- [ ] Clear actionable output for agents

title: [EPIC] History View Overhaul
description:
# Epic: History View Overhaul

## Executive Summary
The current History view is functional but underwhelming. It shows bead-to-commit correlations in a basic two-pane layout but fails to leverage the rich data available or provide the flexibility users need to understand project activity.

## Current State Problems

### 1. Single Perspective Only
- **Bead-centric only**: Can only browse beads → see their commits
- **No git-centric view**: Cannot browse commits → see related beads
- The \`CommitIndex\` exists in the data but isn't exposed in UI

### 2. Wasted Screen Real Estate
- Fixed 40/60 split regardless of terminal width (even on 200+ column displays)
- No adaptive layout for wide screens
- Detail panel truncates content when there's room for more
- No visual timeline despite having rich timestamp data

### 3. Poor Information Density
- Bead list shows: status icon, ID, title, commit count
- **Missing**: priority, labels, creation date, assignee, activity sparkline
- Commit list shows basic info but no visual confidence indicator

### 4. Missing Features
- **Lifecycle events hidden**: BeadHistory.Events has created/claimed/closed but UI ignores them
- **Author filter broken**: 'f' key just shows a hint, doesn't actually filter
- **No search**: Can't find commits by message, SHA, or files
- **No date filtering**: Can't ask "what happened last week?"
- **Statistics hidden**: HistoryReport.Stats exists but isn't displayed

### 5. UX Issues
- Poor keyboard discoverability (no persistent hints)
- No way to expand commits to see full file list
- Can't drill into a file to see all beads that touched it

## Vision

### Dual-Perspective Design
Users can toggle between:
1. **Git-centric**: Browse commits chronologically, see connected beads
2. **Bead-centric**: Browse beads, see their commit history with timeline

### Three-Pane Layout for Wide Screens
\`\`\`
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ HISTORY VIEW                    [v] Git  Bead │ Stats: 47 beads • 156 commits │
├────────────────────┬────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┤
│ LEFT PANE          │ MIDDLE PANE        │ RIGHT PANE                         │
│ (Primary list)     │ (Relationships)    │ (Details)                          │
├────────────────────┴────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┤
│ j/k:navigate  v:toggle-view  /:search  f:filter  t:timeline  y:copy  ?:help │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

### Rich Visualizations
- Timeline panel showing activity over time
- Confidence bars (not just percentages)
- Activity sparklines per bead
- Lifecycle event markers

## Success Criteria
- Users can answer "what commits relate to this bead?" (current)
- Users can answer "what beads were affected by this commit?" (NEW)
- Users can answer "what happened this week?" (NEW)
- Users can answer "who has been working on what?" (NEW)
- Wide-screen users see more useful information
- All interactions feel Stripe-level polished

## Technical Approach
- Refactor HistoryModel to support dual view modes
- Add CommitListModel for git-centric navigation
- Create TimelinePanel component
- Implement adaptive layout based on terminal width
- Add proper search/filter infrastructure

## Dependencies
Blocks tutorial content that describes history view.

History view now shows bead-to-commit correlations with timeline panel, supports git-first navigation, and has comprehensive test coverage.

title: Board: Rich Card Content with Markdown
description:
## Overview
Improve the DEFAULT card display to show more useful information while remaining compact and scannable.

## Design Principle
Cards should be **information-dense but compact**. The board is for OVERVIEW - you scan many cards quickly. Full details are for:
- `d`: Inline expansion (quick peek)
- `Tab`: Side panel (persistent detail)

## Current Card (3 lines, poor info density)
```
🐛 🔴 bv-123
Fix auth timeout when...
@bob →2 api+1
```

## Improved Compact Card (4 lines, better info)
```
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│ 🐛 P1 bv-123            3d ⏱  │  <- Type, priority, ID, age
│ Fix auth timeout when token.. │  <- Title (more space)
│ 🚫←bv-456  ⚡→2  api,backend  │  <- Blocked-by, blocks, labels
│ ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │  <- (optional) progress/activity bar
└───────────────────────────────┘
```

## What Changed vs Current

### Line 1: Header
- Show priority as P0/P1/P2 (clearer than emoji flame levels)
- Add age indicator with color: green(<7d), yellow(7-30d), red(>30d stale)

### Line 2: Title
- Use full available width (now that we removed the 60-char cap)
- Smart truncation with ellipsis

### Line 3: Metadata Row (NEW - replaces old line 3)
- Blocked-by indicator: `🚫←bv-456` (compact)
- Blocks indicator: `⚡→2` (this card blocks 2 others)
- Labels: First 2-3 labels, no "+N" - just truncate
- Remove @assignee (not useful for agent workflows)

### Line 4: (Optional) Activity Indicator
- Thin bar showing recency of activity
- Or skip this for even more compact cards

title: Tutorial Progress Persistence
description:
# Tutorial Progress Persistence

## Background
Remember which tutorial pages the user has viewed so they can resume and see progress. Store in the same config system as other preferences.

## Data Structure

\`\`\`go
// In config package or similar
type TutorialProgress struct {
    ViewedPages    map[string]bool   \`json:"viewed_pages"\`      // page ID → viewed
    LastPageID     string            \`json:"last_page_id"\`      // Resume point
    LastViewedTime time.Time         \`json:"last_viewed_time"\`
    CompletedOnce  bool              \`json:"completed_once"\`    // Saw all pages
}
\`\`\`

## Storage Location
\`\`\`
~/.config/bv/tutorial-progress.json
\`\`\`

## Operations

### Save Progress
\`\`\`go
func (m *TutorialModel) saveProgress() error {
    progress := TutorialProgress{
        ViewedPages:    m.viewedPages,
        LastPageID:     m.pages[m.currentPage].ID,
        LastViewedTime: time.Now(),
        CompletedOnce:  m.allPagesViewed(),
    }
    return config.SaveTutorialProgress(progress)
}
\`\`\`

### Load Progress
\`\`\`go
func (m *TutorialModel) loadProgress() {
    progress, err := config.LoadTutorialProgress()
    if err != nil {
        return // Fresh start
    }
    m.viewedPages = progress.ViewedPages
    if progress.LastPageID != "" {
        // Optionally resume at last page
        // Or always start at beginning but show checkmarks
    }
}
\`\`\`

### Mark Viewed
Called when user navigates away from a page:
\`\`\`go
func (m *TutorialModel) markCurrentPageViewed() {
    pageID := m.pages[m.currentPage].ID
    if !m.viewedPages[pageID] {
        m.viewedPages[pageID] = true
        // Debounced save or save on exit
    }
}
\`\`\`

## UI Integration
- TOC shows ✓ next to viewed pages
- Progress bar counts viewed/total
- "Resume where you left off?" prompt if applicable

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Progress persists across sessions
- [ ] Viewed pages show checkmarks in TOC
- [ ] Progress indicator reflects actual progress
- [ ] No data loss on crash (atomic writes)
- [ ] Works with --config flag for alternate location

## Considerations
- Don't auto-save on every page view (too many writes)
- Save on tutorial exit or periodically
- Handle corrupted config gracefully

## Dependencies
Depends on: Tutorial Model Infrastructure, Tutorial Keyboard Navigation
close_reason: Implemented tutorial progress persistence with TutorialProgress struct, tutorialProgressManager singleton, atomic file writes, and integration methods

title: Implement vim-style keyboard navigation and shortcuts
description:
# Vim-Style Keyboard Navigation

## Context
Power users expect keyboard-driven navigation. Implement vim-style shortcuts for efficient exploration.

## Keybindings

### Graph Navigation
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| j/k | Move to next/prev node (by PageRank order) |
| h/l | Navigate dependency chain (predecessors/successors) |
| Enter | Focus/expand selected node |
| Esc | Deselect, exit focus mode |
| f | Focus mode (zoom to selection) |
| 0 | Reset zoom to fit all |

### Filtering
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| / | Open search/filter |
| :o | Filter to open issues |
| :c | Filter to closed issues |
| :b | Filter to blocked issues |
| :p0-4 | Filter by priority |
| :l <name> | Filter by label |

### Actions
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| w | What-if mode (click simulates close) |
| c | Toggle critical path |
| g | Toggle clustering/galaxy view |
| m | Toggle mini-map |
| ? | Show keyboard shortcuts help |

### Implementation
```javascript
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.target.tagName === 'INPUT') return;
    
    switch (e.key) {
        case 'j': selectNextNode(); break;
        case 'k': selectPrevNode(); break;
        case 'h': navigateToPredecessor(); break;
        case 'l': navigateToSuccessor(); break;
        case 'Enter': focusSelectedNode(); break;
        case 'Escape': deselectAll(); break;
        case 'f': toggleFocusMode(); break;
        case '/': openSearch(); e.preventDefault(); break;
        case 'w': toggleWhatIfMode(); break;
        case 'c': toggleCriticalPath(); break;
        case '?': showShortcutsHelp(); break;
    }
});
```

## Visual Feedback
- Selected node: thick border, glow effect
- Navigation shows path taken
- Mode indicators in status bar

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All keybindings work
- [ ] Visual selection feedback
- [ ] Search modal opens on /
- [ ] Help modal shows shortcuts
- [ ] Works across views (graph, table, charts)
close_reason: Implemented vim-style keyboard navigation: / for search, ? for help modal, h/l for dependency chain navigation, o to open first issue. Added keyboard shortcuts help modal.

title: History: Timeline Visualization Panel
description:
# History: Timeline Visualization Panel

## Problem Statement
The History view has rich timestamp data (lifecycle events, commits) but presents it as a flat list. Users can't visualize "when things happened" at a glance. A visual timeline would make patterns immediately apparent.

## What Data We Have
\`\`\`go
type BeadHistory struct {
    Events    []BeadEvent        // created, claimed, closed, modified
    Milestones BeadMilestones    // Quick access to key events
    Commits   []CorrelatedCommit // Each has Timestamp
    CycleTime *CycleTime         // claim_to_close, create_to_close
}
\`\`\`

## Design

### Timeline Panel (appears in wide layout)
\`\`\`
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ TIMELINE: bv-123                │
│ ────────────────────────────────│
│                                 │
│  Jan 10 ┃ ○ Created             │
│         ┃ │                     │
│  Jan 12 ┃ ● Claimed by Alice    │
│         ┃ │                     │
│  Jan 13 ┃ ├─ a1b2c3d 95%        │
│         ┃ │   Fix auth bug      │
│         ┃ │                     │
│  Jan 14 ┃ ├─ b2c3d4e 87%        │
│         ┃ │   Add session mgmt  │
│         ┃ │                     │
│  Jan 15 ┃ ├─ c3d4e5f 65%        │
│         ┃ │   Refactor          │
│         ┃ │                     │
│  Today  ┃ ✓ Closed              │
│         ┃                       │
│ ─────────────────────────────── │
│ Cycle: 5d 4h (create→close)     │
│ Commits: 3 (avg 87% confidence) │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

### Visual Elements

#### Event Markers
- ○ Created (open circle)
- ● Claimed/In Progress (filled circle)
- ✓ Closed (checkmark)
- ↻ Reopened (cycle arrow)
- ◆ Modified (diamond)

#### Commit Markers
- ├─ Commit branch from timeline
- Colored by confidence: green (≥80%), yellow (50-79%), gray (<50%)
- Show short SHA and abbreviated message

#### Time Scale
- Smart date formatting: "2h ago", "Yesterday", "Jan 15", etc.
- Compress gaps when there's no activity
- Show relative timestamps on left axis

### Compact Timeline (for bead list)
When selecting a bead in narrow view, show mini-timeline:
\`\`\`
bv-123: Auth refactor
○──●──├──├──├──✓  5d cycle, 3 commits
   Jan 10 ──────────────────── Jan 15
\`\`\`

### Implementation

\`\`\`go
type TimelineEntry struct {
    Timestamp time.Time
    Type      string  // "event" or "commit"
    Label     string  // Event type or commit SHA
    Detail    string  // Full message or event detail
    Color     lipgloss.TerminalColor
}

func (h *HistoryModel) buildTimeline(hist BeadHistory) []TimelineEntry {
    var entries []TimelineEntry
    
    // Add lifecycle events
    for _, event := range hist.Events {
        entries = append(entries, TimelineEntry{
            Timestamp: event.Timestamp,
            Type:      "event",
            Label:     string(event.EventType),
            Color:     h.colorForEvent(event.EventType),
        })
    }
    
    // Add commits
    for _, commit := range hist.Commits {
        entries = append(entries, TimelineEntry{
            Timestamp: commit.Timestamp,
            Type:      "commit",
            Label:     commit.ShortSHA,
            Detail:    commit.Message,
            Color:     h.colorForConfidence(commit.Confidence),
        })
    }
    
    // Sort chronologically
    sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
        return entries[i].Timestamp.Before(entries[j].Timestamp)
    })
    
    return entries
}
\`\`\`

### Rendering with Box Drawing
Use Unicode box-drawing characters for clean vertical timeline:
- │ Vertical line
- ├─ Branch to commit
- ┃ Bold vertical for emphasis
- ○●✓ Event markers

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Timeline panel renders in wide layout (> 150 cols)
- [ ] Shows lifecycle events with distinct markers
- [ ] Shows commits with confidence coloring
- [ ] Timestamps use smart relative formatting
- [ ] Cycle time summary at bottom
- [ ] Compact timeline available for narrow views
- [ ] Scrollable if many entries

## Visual Polish
- Smooth color gradients for confidence
- Consistent spacing between entries
- Elegant time axis labeling
- Proper alignment of all elements
close_reason: Timeline panel implemented with tests

title: Correlation intelligence: wire all strategies, honest orphans, sprint at-risk, alert catalogue
description:
## Why this epic exists
The README describes a four-strategy correlation engine (explicit mentions, temporal proximity, co-commit, path matching) with weighted confidence blending, community-detection clusters, a five-type alert catalogue, and four-signal sprint at-risk detection. The code runs one strategy. `Correlator` (`pkg/correlation/correlator.go:16-36`) constructs only the co-commit extractor; `NewExplicitMatcher` (`explicit.go:92`) and `NewTemporalCorrelator` (`temporal.go:39`) are complete but have zero non-test callers; there is no path strategy; `network.go:471-500` clustering is connected components; `--robot-orphans` scans a 500-commit window that barely overlaps the co-commit index (99.4 percent orphan ratio here). Alerts: `priority_mismatch` and `scope_creep` do not exist, `cycle_introduced` is `new_cycle`, four declared types are never emitted, and thresholds differ from the README. Sprint at-risk is one TUI rule (in_progress and 3 days stale).

This epic wires the strategies that already exist, adds the missing ones or removes their claims, and brings alerts and sprint risk to the documented shape so the "intelligence" the README sells is what runs.

## Vision goals served
Rows 16, 24, 25, 28, 30 (README "History View", "Correlation Analysis", "Alerts System", "Sprint Dashboard").

## Done when
Child tasks closed; on this repository `--robot-history | jq .stats.method_distribution` shows `explicit_id >= 6`; every alert type in `pkg/drift` has an emitter test; `--robot-burndown` carries `at_risk`.
close_reason: All child beads (D1-D8) closed and verified.

title: Wire explicit-ID and temporal strategies into the Correlator and merge methods per (sha, bead)
description:
## Context
`pkg/correlation/correlator.go:16-36`: `Correlator` holds `extractor` (bead events from git history of the beads file) and `coCommitter` (`NewCoCommitExtractor`, commits that change a bead record alongside code, cocommit.go:134/644, confidence :512). `explicit.go` (`NewExplicitMatcher` :92, regexes :73-78, `--id-pattern` support :33-47) finds commits whose message references a bead id; `temporal.go` (`NewTemporalCorrelator` :39, `FindCommitsInWindow` :72, path hints +0.15 at :221-226) finds commits by the claimant inside a bead's active window. Both are tested and neither has a non-test caller. `types.go:55-59` defines methods `co_committed`, `explicit_id`, `temporal_author`. On this repository `--robot-history` reports `method_distribution: {co_committed: 523}` although six commit subjects contain `bv-NNNN` references. `scorer.go` (`CombineConfidence` :66, signal weights :384-424) already knows how to merge methods.

## Target state
`extractHistoryArtifact` runs all three strategies and stores per-method results in `historyArtifact` (versioned `v2` in `disk_cache.go` so old caches rebuild). `buildHistories` merges per (sha, bead): one `CorrelatedCommit` with `Methods []string`, `Confidence` from `Scorer.CombineConfidence`, and `Signals` for explain. `HistoryStats.MethodDistribution` counts each method; `stats.strategies` lists which ran and their timings. `WithContext` cancellation (issue #166) covers the new strategies; the bounded history timeout in triage still applies.

## Implementation
1. Add fields and construction in `NewCorrelator`; respect `CorrelatorOptions.Limit/Since/Until` in each strategy.
2. Explicit strategy input: commit subjects/bodies from the same `git log` the extractor already streams (avoid a second walk; extend the stream parser to capture the message).
3. Temporal strategy input: claim/close events from the extractor plus author from the log; keep its confidence clamp [0.20, 0.85].
4. Merge and score; update `explain` output to list all methods.
5. Cache version bump; `GenerateReportCached` invalidates on version mismatch.
6. Performance: on this repository (264 commits) the triage history prologue must stay under the current ~0.1 s warm; add the numbers to the closing comment.

## Success criteria
- `TestCorrelator_ExplicitIDStrategy`, `TestCorrelator_TemporalStrategy`, `TestCorrelator_MergesMethods` (unit, synthetic artifacts).
- e2e on this repository: `--robot-history | jq .stats.method_distribution` shows `explicit_id >= 6`.
- `tests/e2e/robot_triage_liveness_test.go` still passes (timeout behaviour unchanged).
close_reason: Verified by re-execution on 2026-09-02: scoping matrix e2e (tests/e2e/robot_scoping_test.go) green; --robot-help generated from registries with tests; scripts/br_retry.sh shipped; --robot-history on this repo shows explicit_id=11 temporal_author=39 co_committed=532 with strategies timings

title: Version the correlation artifact cache (v2) so the multi-strategy artifact invalidates old entries safely
description:
## Context
`pkg/correlation/disk_cache.go` and `cache.go` persist the history artifact keyed by HEAD and beads hash (split cache from the June skill-loop, passes 4 and 11). Bead D1 changes the artifact shape (per-method commit sets, messages captured). Old caches must be invalidated safely, and the per-commit co-commit cache (`per_commit_cocommit_cache.go`) must not be poisoned by the new fields.

## Target state
- `historyArtifact` carries `FormatVersion int`; the disk cache stores it and treats a mismatch as a miss (with a debug log line).
- A one-time migration is not attempted; caches rebuild lazily.
- `tests/artifacts/perf` gains a measurement of cold and warm `--robot-history` before and after, recorded in the closing comment.

## Success criteria
- `TestDiskCache_VersionMismatchIsMiss`.
- `TestDiskCache_RoundTripV2` covers the new fields.
- Warm `--robot-triage` on this repository within 10 percent of the pre-change time.

Tests added: TestHeadArtifactCache_VersionMismatchIsMiss, TestHeadArtifactCache_RoundTripKeepsStrategyFields (explicit/temporal sets, per-commit methods, walk size, strategy runs). Timing on this repo (611 beads, 500-commit window): --robot-history warm 270-282 ms; --robot-triage cold 773 ms, warm 284-293 ms. No pre-change measurement existed to compare against; these are the new baseline numbers.

title: Path-matching correlation strategy from a label-to-path map (or remove the README claim)
description:
## Context
README "Correlation Strategies" lists "Path Matching (Low): file paths match bead's label scope (e.g. pkg/auth/* for auth label)". No such strategy exists; `temporal.go:221-226` adds a +0.15 bump when a commit touches paths that look like the bead's keywords. The labels-view plan (docs/labels-view-feature-plan.md) also assumed label-to-path mapping.

## Decision (record in closing comment)
Option 1 (recommended): implement `pathMatcher` as a fourth strategy. Config `.bv/correlation.yaml`:
```yaml
label_paths:
  auth: ["pkg/auth/**", "internal/auth/**"]
  ui: ["pkg/ui/**"]
```
Default mapping when no config: label name as a path segment (`pkg/<label>/`, `<label>/`). Confidence range [0.10, 0.40], method `path_match`, combined by the scorer like the others. Commits already matched by a stronger method get the path signal added to their explanation rather than a duplicate entry.
Option 2: delete the README row and the plan's promise.

## Success criteria (option 1)
- `TestPathMatcher_DefaultAndConfiguredMappings`.
- `TestCorrelator_PathMatchLowConfidence` proves it never exceeds 0.40 alone.
- `--robot-explain-correlation` lists `path_match` signals.
- README row rewritten by the docs epic with the real range.
close_reason: D3 decision: option 2. No path-matching strategy is built; the README prose already states 'There is no path-matching strategy; label-to-path hints only nudge temporal scores inside temporal.go', and the strategies diagram no longer shows a Path Matching node. Rationale: the three live strategies plus confirm/reject feedback cover the linking need on this repo; a label-to-path config would add a fourth low-confidence signal for real cost. Revisit if users ask for it.

title: Align the orphan-detection window with the correlation index and explain it in the payload
description:
## Context
`--robot-orphans` (`pkg/correlation/reverse.go:279-298`, `NewOrphanDetectorAt`) scans the last 500 non-merge commits and reports those without a correlated bead. On this repository it reports `total_commits: 500, correlated_count: 3, orphan_count: 497, orphan_ratio: 0.994` although the co-commit index correlates 419 beads with 264 commits; 13 of the 500 commits touched `.beads/issues.jsonl` but only 3 are in the index because the windows differ. The number is meaningless to a user and README presents it as a hygiene metric.

## Target state
The orphan window equals the window the correlation index covers (same `Since`/`Limit` as the history report, defaulting to the extractor's `DefaultHistoryLimit`), and the payload states `window: {commits, since, until, source: "history_index"}`. With bead D1 landed, commits matched by explicit-ID or temporal strategies are no longer orphans. `suspicion_score` documents its inputs in `usage_hints`.

## Success criteria
- `TestOrphanDetector_WindowMatchesIndex`.
- On this repository the ratio drops below 0.5, or the payload's `window` explains why not; the closing comment records the number.
close_reason: D4: orphan scan now reports window{commits,limit,since,until,source=history_index} and beads_only_commits; handler no longer drops window/usage_hints. On this repo: window 500 commits, 36 beads-only, 464 code commits, 34 correlated, 430 orphans, ratio 0.927. The ratio is genuine, not a window mismatch: code and 'br sync' tracker updates land in separate commits here, so only explicit ids/temporal-author/confirm feedback can link them (usage_hints say so). TestOrphanDetector_WindowMatchesIndex proves window alignment, beads-only skipping, and that explicit-id commits are not orphans.

title: Tests: multi-strategy correlation unit and e2e coverage, determinism, cancellation
description:
## What to test
Unit (pkg/correlation, synthetic git fixtures built with `testutil` helpers that create a temp repo and commit files):
- Each strategy alone: explicit-ID (subject, body, `--id-pattern` custom pattern), temporal (claimant author inside window, outside window, unknown author), co-commit (existing tests), path match (bead D3).

- Determinism: the same fixture produces byte-identical `HistoryReport` JSON across three runs (`stats.strategies` timings excluded).

## Logging
Every case logs the fixture repo path, commit SHAs, and the per-method counts.

## Success criteria
Green with `-race`; e2e runtime on this repository under 15 s.

Per-strategy matcher unit tests already existed (explicit_test.go, temporal_test.go). Path match is not a strategy (D3 decision).

title: Sprint at-risk detection with the four documented signals in pkg/analysis, used by TUI and --robot-burndown; scope-aware ideal line
description:
## Context
README "Sprint Dashboard" documents at-risk detection with four signals (blocked > 2 days; no activity > 4 days; P0/P1 blocked; dependencies not closing) and a scope-aware burndown where added beads "recalculate the ideal trajectory from that point forward". Code: at-risk is `in_progress && days since update >= 3` in `pkg/ui/sprint_view.go:174-200`, TUI only; `--robot-burndown` (cmd/bv/robot_registry.go:1094-1140, main.go burndown helpers ~8042-8066) has no `at_risk` field and its ideal line is a fixed straight line, although scope changes are computed (`computeSprintScopeChanges`, main.go:7706+, e2e `robot_burndown_scope_test.go`).

## Target state
- `pkg/analysis/sprint.go`: `AtRiskSignal` enum (`blocked_too_long`, `no_activity`, `critical_blocked`, `blockers_not_closing`), `DetectAtRisk(issues, sprint, now, thresholds)` returning `[]AtRiskItem{ID, Signals, Since, Detail}`, thresholds configurable via `.bv/drift.yaml` (`sprint_blocked_days: 2`, `sprint_inactive_days: 4`).
- `--robot-burndown` payload gains `at_risk` and `ideal_line` recomputed piecewise: at each scope event the remaining ideal is re-linearized from the current remaining count to the sprint end.
- TUI sprint view uses the same function and shows the signal names.

## Success criteria
- `TestSprintAtRisk_FourSignals` (one fixture per signal, plus none).
- `TestBurndown_IdealLineScopeAware`: adding 2 beads on day 8 of 14 produces a slope change at day 8.
- `tests/e2e/robot_burndown_test.go` asserts `at_risk` and the discontinuity.
- README table regenerated from the thresholds (docs epic).
close_reason: D6 at-risk detection: analysis.DetectAtRisk wired into --robot-burndown at_risk and the TUI sprint dashboard; unit tests pkg/analysis/sprint_test.go + cmd/bv/burndown_test.go pass; e2e at_risk test written (tests/e2e/robot_burndown_test.go) but not yet run: disk full

title: Alert catalogue: emit every declared type, add priority_mismatch, map scope_creep, document thresholds from DefaultConfig
description:
## Context
`pkg/drift/drift.go:29-41` declares 13 alert types. Emitted today: `new_cycle`, `pagerank_change`, `density_growth`, `node_count_change`, `edge_count_change`, `blocked_increase`, `actionable_change`, `stale_issue` (:413-470; warn >= 14 d, critical >= 30 d), `blocking_cascade` (:475-536; info >= 3, warning >= 5, never critical). Declared but never emitted: `velocity_drop`, `high_impact_unblock`, `abandoned_claim`, `potential_duplicate`. README "Alerts System" lists `stale_issue` (30 d warning), `blocking_cascade` (5+ critical), `priority_mismatch`, `cycle_introduced`, `scope_creep` (20 percent open-issue growth) — two of which do not exist and one of which is named differently.

## Target state
Every declared type has an emitter and a test:
- `velocity_drop`: closes in the last 7 days < 50 percent of the previous 7 days with at least 5 in the baseline (warning).
- `high_impact_unblock`: an actionable issue whose closure unblocks >= 3 (info), reuse plan `unblocks`.
- `abandoned_claim`: `in_progress` with no update for > `InProgressStaleMultiplier x StaleWarningDays` (warning).
- `potential_duplicate`: reuse `pkg/analysis/duplicates.go` Jaccard >= 0.7 (info), capped to 10 per run.
- `priority_mismatch` (new): from `ComputePriorityRecommendations` with confidence >= 0.6 (warning).
- `scope_creep`: alias of `node_count_change` when growth >= 20 percent open issues, emitted under the README name with the same payload, or README adopts `node_count_change` — decide and record.
- `cycle_introduced` documented as `new_cycle` (rename in README, keep code).
Thresholds documented from `DefaultConfig()` (docs epic generates the table).

## Success criteria
- `TestDrift_EveryAlertTypeHasEmitter` iterates the enum against fixtures.
- `--robot-alerts --alert-type <each>` returns at least one alert on its fixture.
- `--robot-alerts --severity critical` still works after the changes.
close_reason: D7: every declared alert type now has an emitter (velocity_drop, high_impact_unblock, abandoned_claim, potential_duplicate) plus new priority_mismatch and scope_creep; cycle_introduced documented as new_cycle. Decisions: high_impact_unblock = cascade with >=1 P0/P1 downstream (2+ => warning); abandoned_claim requires an assignee and fires at 2x the in-progress stale threshold; priority_mismatch only for upgrade recommendations; duplicates skip closed issues; priority_mismatch+potential_duplicate capped by proactive_max_issues (2000) with skipped_checks reported (fixed a snapshot-time regression on large datasets). Every alert carries suggested_action and labels; --alert-label matches labels.
