title: Tree: Implement navigation and keyboard handling
description:
## Purpose
Enable users to navigate the tree structure intuitively using keyboard shortcuts, with expand/collapse functionality.

## Navigation Model

### The flatList Concept
Trees are 2D but keyboard navigation is 1D. We solve this by maintaining a **flatList** - a flattened array of currently visible nodes.

```
Visual Tree:              flatList index:
▾ EPIC-001                [0]
  ├─ FEAT-002             [1]
  ├─ ▸ FEAT-003           [2] (collapsed - children hidden)
  └─ TASK-004             [3]
▸ EPIC-005                [4] (collapsed)
```

When FEAT-003 is expanded:
```
Visual Tree:              flatList index:
▾ EPIC-001                [0]
  ├─ FEAT-002             [1]
  ├─ ▾ FEAT-003           [2]
  │   ├─ TASK-006         [3] (newly visible)
  │   └─ TASK-007         [4] (newly visible)
  └─ TASK-004             [5]
▸ EPIC-005                [6]
```

### RebuildFlatList Algorithm
```go
func (t *TreeModel) RebuildFlatList() {
    t.flatList = t.flatList[:0] // Reset
    for _, root := range t.roots {
        t.appendVisible(root)
    }
}

func (t *TreeModel) appendVisible(node *TreeNode) {
    t.flatList = append(t.flatList, node)
    if node.Expanded {
        for _, child := range node.Children {
            t.appendVisible(child)
        }
    }
}
```

## Keyboard Mappings

### Navigation
| Key | Action | Notes |
|-----|--------|-------|
| `j` / `↓` | Move cursor down | Wraps at bottom (optional) |
| `k` / `↑` | Move cursor up | Wraps at top (optional) |
| `gg` | Jump to first node | Vim-style |
| `G` | Jump to last node | |
| `Ctrl+D` | Page down | Half-viewport scroll |
| `Ctrl+U` | Page up | |

### Expand/Collapse
| Key | Action | Notes |
|-----|--------|-------|
| `Enter` / `Space` | Toggle expand/collapse | On leaf node: no-op or show detail |
| `→` / `l` | Expand current | If already expanded: move to first child |
| `←` / `h` | Collapse current | If already collapsed: jump to parent |
| `o` | Expand all descendants | Recursive expand |
| `O` | Collapse all | Reset to roots-only |
| `zo` | Expand current (vim-style) | Alternative |
| `zc` | Collapse current | Alternative |
| `zM` | Collapse all | Alternative |
| `zR` | Expand all | Alternative |

### Exit
| Key | Action | Notes |
|-----|--------|-------|
| `E` | Exit tree view | Return to list |
| `Esc` | Exit tree view | Alternative |
| `q` | Exit tree OR quit app | Context-dependent |

## Implementation Details

### MoveDown() / MoveUp()
```go
func (t *TreeModel) MoveDown() {
    if t.cursor < len(t.flatList)-1 {
        t.cursor++
        t.ensureVisible()
    }
}

func (t *TreeModel) ensureVisible() {
    // Scroll viewport if cursor is outside visible range
    // Similar to list.Model behavior
}
```

### ToggleExpand()
```go
func (t *TreeModel) ToggleExpand() {
    if t.cursor >= len(t.flatList) {
        return
    }
    node := t.flatList[t.cursor]
    if len(node.Children) == 0 {
        return // Leaf node - nothing to toggle
    }
    node.Expanded = !node.Expanded
    t.RebuildFlatList()
    // Cursor may need adjustment if collapsing
}
```

### JumpToParent()
```go
func (t *TreeModel) JumpToParent() {
    if t.cursor >= len(t.flatList) {
        return
    }
    node := t.flatList[t.cursor]
    if node.Parent == nil {
        return // Already at root
    }
    // Find parent in flatList
    for i, n := range t.flatList {
        if n == node.Parent {
            t.cursor = i
            t.ensureVisible()
            return
        }
    }
}
```

## State Management

### Preserving Cursor on Rebuild
When tree is rebuilt (filter change, data reload):
1. Remember current issue ID
2. Rebuild tree
3. Find same issue ID in new flatList
4. Set cursor to that index (or 0 if not found)

### Preserving Expand State
Store expanded IDs in a set:
```go
expandedIDs map[string]bool
```
On rebuild, restore expanded state from this set.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] j/k navigation works correctly
- [ ] Enter toggles expand/collapse
- [ ] ← jumps to parent when collapsed
- [ ] → expands or moves to first child
- [ ] gg/G jump to top/bottom
- [ ] Expand/collapse rebuilds flatList correctly
- [ ] Cursor preserved across filter changes
- [ ] No panic on empty tree
close_reason: Implemented all navigation methods: JumpToParent, ExpandOrMoveToChild, CollapseOrJumpToParent, PageUp/PageDown, SelectByID, GetSelectedID. All 20 tree tests passing.

title: Phase 3: Pre-computed Views - Build All View Data in Background
description:
# Phase 3: Pre-computed Views

## Overview

After Phase 2, the background worker loads data and runs analysis. But the UI still transforms this data into renderable structures (list items, board columns, tree nodes). This transformation can take 50-100ms.

Phase 3 moves view pre-computation to the background, so rendering becomes O(visible items) instead of O(all items).

## Why This Phase

Phase 2 made I/O and analysis non-blocking. But we still have:
- ListItems construction: iterating all issues, applying filters, building delegate items
- BoardState construction: grouping by status, sorting within columns
- TreeNodes construction: building hierarchical structure from parent-child links
- GraphLayout construction: node positioning, edge routing
- InsightsData construction: extracting top-N for each metric

By pre-computing all of this in the background, the View() method becomes trivial: just render what's already computed.

## The Goal

```go
// BEFORE (current): View() does work
func (m Model) View() string {
    items := m.buildListItems(m.issues)  // O(n) - 50ms for 1000 issues
    return m.renderItems(items)           // O(visible) - fast
}

// AFTER (Phase 3): View() just renders
func (m Model) View() string {
    return m.renderItems(m.snapshot.ListItems) // O(visible) - fast
}
```

## Pre-computed Structures

### 1. ListItems
```go
type ListItemsSnapshot struct {
    Items       []list.Item    // Ready for bubbles/list
    FilteredIDs []string       // Which issues are currently visible
    SortMode    SortMode       // How they're sorted
    RecipeName  string         // Which recipe was applied
}
```

### 2. BoardState
```go
type BoardSnapshot struct {
    Columns []BoardColumn
}

type BoardColumn struct {
    Title    string
    Status   model.Status
    Cards    []BoardCard
    
    // Pre-computed stats
    TotalCount  int
    HighPriCount int
    BlockedCount int
}

type BoardCard struct {
    Issue       *model.Issue
    BorderColor lipgloss.Color  // Pre-computed based on status
    Expanded    bool
}
```

### 3. TreeNodes
```go
type TreeNodeSnapshot struct {
    Issue    *model.Issue
    Children []*TreeNodeSnapshot
    Depth    int
    IsLast   bool  // For drawing └── vs ├──
}
```

### 4. GraphLayout
```go
type GraphSnapshot struct {
    Nodes []GraphNode
    Edges []GraphEdge
    Bounds Rect
}

type GraphNode struct {
    Issue *model.Issue
    X, Y  int  // Position in canvas coordinates
}

type GraphEdge struct {
    From, To string
    Path     []Point  // Pre-computed routing
}
```

### 5. InsightsData
```go
type InsightsSnapshot struct {
    Bottlenecks []RankedIssue  // Top 10 by betweenness
    Keystones   []RankedIssue  // Top 10 by critical path
    Influencers []RankedIssue  // Top 10 by eigenvector
    Hubs        []RankedIssue  // Top 10 by HITS hub score
    Authorities []RankedIssue  // Top 10 by HITS authority
    Cycles      [][]string     // All detected cycles
    
    // Pre-rendered strings for quick display
    BottleneckLines []string
    KeystoneLines   []string
    // ...
}
```

## Implementation Location

Extend buildSnapshot() in background_worker.go:

```go
func (w *BackgroundWorker) buildSnapshot() (*DataSnapshot, error) {
    // ... existing loading and analysis code ...
    
    // === Pre-compute view data ===
    
    // 1. List items
    listItems := w.buildListItems(issues, issueMap, currentRecipe)
    
    // 2. Board state
    boardState := w.buildBoardState(issues, issueMap)
    
    // 3. Tree nodes
    treeNodes := w.buildTreeNodes(issues, issueMap)
    
    // 4. Graph layout (can be expensive, might defer)
    graphLayout := w.buildGraphLayout(issues, stats)
    
    // 5. Insights (depends on Phase 2, so might be partial)
    insightsData := w.buildInsightsData(stats)
    
    snapshot := &DataSnapshot{
        // ... existing fields ...
        ListItems:    listItems,
        BoardState:   boardState,
        TreeNodes:    treeNodes,
        GraphLayout:  graphLayout,
        InsightsData: insightsData,
    }
    
    return snapshot, nil
}
```

## Recipe/Filter Integration

Pre-computed views need to respect the current recipe (filters, sorts):

```go
// Worker needs to know current recipe
type BackgroundWorker struct {
    // ...
    currentRecipe atomic.Value  // *recipe.Recipe
}

// UI tells worker about recipe changes
func (w *BackgroundWorker) SetRecipe(r *recipe.Recipe) {
    w.currentRecipe.Store(r)
    w.TriggerRefresh() // Rebuild with new recipe
}
```

## Performance Targets

| View | Current (UI thread) | Target (background) |
|------|---------------------|---------------------|
| List items | 30-50ms | 0ms (pre-computed) |
| Board state | 20-40ms | 0ms (pre-computed) |
| Tree nodes | 20-30ms | 0ms (pre-computed) |
| Graph layout | 50-100ms | 0ms (pre-computed) |
| Insights | 30-50ms | 0ms (pre-computed) |
| **Total** | **150-270ms** | **< 5ms** |

## Subtasks

1. Pre-compute ListItems in background
2. Pre-compute BoardState in background
3. Pre-compute TreeNodes in background
4. Pre-compute GraphLayout in background (or lazy)
5. Pre-compute InsightsData in background
6. Wire recipe changes to trigger refresh

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All view data pre-computed in snapshot
- [ ] View() methods just render pre-computed data
- [ ] Recipe changes trigger snapshot rebuild
- [ ] No noticeable latency in view rendering
- [ ] View transitions remain smooth
close_reason: Aggregate Phase 3 acceptance completed. DataSnapshot precomputes recipe-filtered/sorted list adapters and indexes, BoardState for all swimlanes, TreeRoots/TreeNodeMap, GraphLayout/dependency/rank indexes, Insights, semantic documents, alerts, and triage data; the common Model path installs these snapshots directly. Recipe changes trigger a worker rebuild. Fresh RCH remote -race aggregate suite across all five view structures, recipe propagation, search documents, and selection/navigation preservation passed in 1.863s. Five-sample SnapshotSwap delivery remained 0.337-1.121ms across 100/1000/5000 issues (target <5ms); isolated rapid-write rendering averaged 29.504-42.532ms while Update averaged 1.013-3.463ms. Complete 1000-issue snapshot construction was 15.960-21.294ms off-thread.

title: Viewport: Add scrollbar position indicator
description:
## Task: Add Scrollbar Position Indicator

### Background

When viewing a large tree with viewport scrolling, users need visual feedback about their position in the list. A scrollbar indicator shows:
- Current position (where am I?)
- Total size (how much is there?)
- Viewport proportion (how much am I seeing?)

### Design Options

#### Option A: Text-based indicator (Recommended for MVP)
Simple text showing position:
```
[50-60 of 100]
```
or
```
50% ↓
```

#### Option B: ASCII scrollbar
Visual indicator on right edge:
```
├── Epic 1                          │
│   ├── Task 1                      ┃  <- scrollbar thumb
│   └── Task 2                      ┃
├── Epic 2                          │
│   ├── Task 3                      │
│   └── Task 4                      │
└── Epic 3                          │
```

#### Option C: Unicode block scrollbar
Using Unicode block characters for smoother appearance:
```
▁ (1/8 block) - top of range
▂▃▄▅▆▇█ - increasing density
```

### Recommendation

Start with **Option A** (text indicator) as it's simplest and doesn't affect tree rendering. Can add visual scrollbar later.

### Implementation (Option A)

```go
// In View(), add position indicator at bottom or top
func (t *TreeModel) View() string {
    // ... existing rendering ...
    
    // Add position indicator
    if len(t.flatList) > t.height {
        start, end := t.visibleRange()
        indicator := fmt.Sprintf(" [%d-%d of %d]", start+1, end, len(t.flatList))
        sb.WriteString(t.theme.Muted.Render(indicator))
    }
    
    return sb.String()
}
```

### Implementation (Option B - Future)

Would require:
1. Calculate scrollbar height based on viewport/total ratio
2. Calculate thumb position based on offset/total
3. Render scrollbar characters in right column
4. May need to reduce tree width by 1-2 chars

### Test cases

```go
func TestScrollbarIndicator(t *testing.T) {
    tree := createTreeWithNodes(100)
    tree.SetSize(80, 10)
    tree.viewportOffset = 50
    
    output := tree.View()
    
    // Should contain position indicator
    if !strings.Contains(output, "51-60 of 100") && 
       !strings.Contains(output, "[51-60") {
        t.Error("position indicator not found")
    }
}

func TestScrollbarNotShownForSmallTree(t *testing.T) {
    tree := createTreeWithNodes(5)
    tree.SetSize(80, 10)
    
    output := tree.View()
    
    // Should NOT contain position indicator (all visible)
    if strings.Contains(output, " of ") {
        t.Error("position indicator should not show for small tree")
    }
}
```

### Files to modify
- `pkg/ui/tree.go` - Add scrollbar rendering to View()

### Success Criteria
- [ ] Position indicator shows when scrolling is needed
- [ ] Indicator hidden when all nodes fit
- [ ] Numbers are accurate (1-indexed for user display)
- [ ] Styling matches theme (muted/subtle)

### Dependencies
- bv-db02 (windowed rendering) - needs viewport to be working

### Priority
P3 - Nice to have, not critical for functionality. Can be skipped in MVP.

### Notes
- Keep it simple for now - text indicator is sufficient
- Visual scrollbar can be a separate enhancement later
- Consider keyboard shortcut to show/hide indicator
close_reason: Added text-based position indicator [start-end of total] that shows when scrolling is needed. Hidden for small trees.

title: Light Mode Terminal: Low Color Contrast Makes Text Unreadable
description:
## Problem Statement

The bv color scheme is very hard to read on light terminal backgrounds. The 'dimmed' text (Subtext, Muted colors) is nearly invisible on white backgrounds, making the application unusable for users with light terminal themes.

## User Impact

**Severity: High (P1)**
- Effectively blocks users with light terminal themes
- Affects readability of secondary information (dimmed text, hints)
- Reported by @mikker in GitHub Issue #17

## Root Cause Analysis

**Location:** `pkg/ui/theme.go:41-64`

The theme uses `lipgloss.AdaptiveColor` which provides Light/Dark values:

```go
Subtext: lipgloss.AdaptiveColor{Light: "#999999", Dark: "#BFBFBF"}
Muted:   lipgloss.AdaptiveColor{Light: "#888888", Dark: "#6272A4"}
```

The Light values are too light for white backgrounds:
- `#999999` on white = contrast ratio ~2.8:1 (WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text)
- `#888888` on white = contrast ratio ~3.5:1 (still fails WCAG AA)

While lipgloss attempts auto-detection of terminal background color, the chosen Light values are simply too faint regardless.

## Proposed Solution

### Fix 1: Improve Light mode color contrast

```go
// Improved light mode colors (WCAG AA compliant)
Subtext: lipgloss.AdaptiveColor{Light: "#666666", Dark: "#BFBFBF"} // ~6:1 contrast
Muted:   lipgloss.AdaptiveColor{Light: "#555555", Dark: "#6272A4"} // ~7:1 contrast
```

All colors need review:
- Primary: #7D56F4 on white = ~4.6:1 (barely passes)
- Secondary: #555555 is good
- Status colors need verification

### Fix 2 (Optional): Add explicit theme flag

```bash
bv --theme=light   # Force light mode colors
bv --theme=dark    # Force dark mode colors
bv --theme=auto    # Default: auto-detect (current behavior)
```

This helps when auto-detection fails or user preference differs.

## Color Audit Required

All AdaptiveColor values need contrast verification:

| Color | Current Light | Contrast | Suggested Light | New Contrast |
|-------|--------------|----------|-----------------|--------------|
| Subtext | #999999 | 2.8:1 ❌ | #666666 | 6:1 ✓ |
| Muted | #888888 | 3.5:1 ❌ | #555555 | 7:1 ✓ |
| Secondary | #555555 | 7:1 ✓ | Keep | - |
| Open | #00A800 | 2.7:1 ❌ | #007700 | 4.6:1 ✓ |
| Closed | #555555 | 7:1 ✓ | Keep | - |
| Border | #DDDDDD | 1.4:1 ❌ | #AAAAAA | 2.3:1 (border OK) |

## Test Plan

1. Manual test on iTerm2 with Solarized Light theme
2. Manual test on macOS Terminal with default light theme
3. Verify all text elements are readable
4. Verify status colors are distinguishable
5. Consider adding screenshot tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All text readable on white terminal background
- [ ] Status colors visually distinguishable on light background
- [ ] Existing dark mode appearance unchanged
- [ ] Optional: --theme flag for explicit control
- [ ] No WCAG AA violations for text colors (4.5:1 minimum)

## References

- GitHub Issue #17: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer/issues/17
- WCAG Color Contrast Guidelines: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html
- lipgloss AdaptiveColor: https://github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss#adaptive-colors
close_reason: Improved light mode color contrast for WCAG AA compliance - darker Subtext, Muted, Open, InProgress, Feature, Task, Chore, and Border colors

title: openInEditor Uses Hardcoded Path Instead of Configured beadsPath
description:
## Problem Statement

The 'O' keybinding to open the beads file in editor fails when the file isn't named exactly `beads.jsonl`. The `openInEditor()` function hardcodes the path instead of using the `beadsPath` field already stored in the Model.

## User Impact

**Severity: High (P1)**
- Fails silently or shows error for projects using `issues.jsonl`
- beads upstream uses `issues.jsonl` as canonical, not `beads.jsonl`
- Reported by @qmx in GitHub PR #18

## Root Cause Analysis

**Location:** `pkg/ui/model.go:2945-2955`

```go
func (m *Model) openInEditor() {
    cwd, err := os.Getwd()
    // ...
    beadsFile := filepath.Join(cwd, ".beads", "beads.jsonl")  // HARDCODED!
    if _, err := os.Stat(beadsFile); os.IsNotExist(err) {
        m.statusMsg = "No .beads/beads.jsonl file found"  // Wrong error message
        // ...
    }
}
```

The Model already has a `beadsPath` field (line 138) that's set during initialization and used for file watching. This function ignores it.

## Why This Matters

The beads project documentation (pre-commit hook) states:
> Stage all tracked JSONL files (issues.jsonl is canonical, beads.jsonl for backward compat)

So the hardcoded `beads.jsonl` path is wrong for the canonical case.

## Proposed Solution

```go
func (m *Model) openInEditor() {
    if m.beadsPath == "" {
        m.statusMsg = "No beads file configured"
        m.statusIsError = true
        return
    }

    if _, err := os.Stat(m.beadsPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
        m.statusMsg = fmt.Sprintf("Beads file not found: %s", m.beadsPath)
        m.statusIsError = true
        return
    }
    
    // Continue with m.beadsPath instead of hardcoded path...
}
```

## Test Plan

1. Test: openInEditor with beadsPath set to issues.jsonl - should work
2. Test: openInEditor with beadsPath empty - should show "No beads file configured"
3. Test: openInEditor with beadsPath pointing to non-existent file - should show path in error
4. Manual test: 'O' key works for both beads.jsonl and issues.jsonl projects

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Uses m.beadsPath instead of hardcoded path
- [ ] Error messages include actual file path for debugging
- [ ] Works for issues.jsonl, beads.jsonl, and any other valid jsonl file
- [ ] Tests cover all error paths

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:** bv-mvvu (Data Integrity: Merge Artifact Files)
- The beadsPath value depends on correct file selection
- Fix the loader first, then this will use the correct path

## References

- GitHub PR #18: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer/pull/18
- beads pre-commit hook documentation on canonical file names
close_reason: Fixed: openInEditor now uses m.beadsPath instead of hardcoded 'beads.jsonl'. Error messages now include actual file path. Build verified.

title: Port K-Shortest Paths and Parallel Cut analysis to Rust WASM
notes:
BUG FIX NEEDED: Current implementation stores only ONE predecessor per node (pred = vec![None; n]), so it can only reconstruct ONE path per endpoint. To get truly distinct k paths:

OPTION A (Simple): Find k distinct sinks by longest distance, reconstruct one path each. This gives k paths ending at different nodes.

OPTION B (Correct): Use Yen's k-shortest paths algorithm or track ALL predecessors per node and enumerate paths.

For v1, Option A is acceptable since we want paths to k DIFFERENT high-priority issues. Document this limitation in the return type.
close_reason: Implemented K-Shortest Paths and Parallel Cut algorithms in Rust WASM. Added k_paths.rs (k longest paths via topo sort) and parallel_cut.rs (nodes that increase parallelization). All 17 tests pass.

title: Robot contract integrity: one envelope, scoping honoured everywhere, no placeholders, no dead paths
description:
## Why this epic exists
The README promises deterministic robot contracts: every payload carries `data_hash`, `analysis_config`, `status`, and `as_of`/`as_of_commit`, and "all robot commands support --as-of". The reality check found: only 6 of ~40 commands emit `as_of`; five commands (`--robot-related`, `--robot-file-relations`, `--robot-blocker-chain`, `--robot-impact-network`, `--robot-causality`) reload the working tree and ignore `--as-of`, `--label`, `--recipe`, and `--repo`; `--robot-insights` ships a permanent placeholder (`advanced_insights.parallel_gain = pending, "Awaiting implementation (bv-129)"`, bv-129 closed 2025-12-15); `--robot-metrics` always reports zeros because nothing records to `pkg/metrics`; `cmd/bv/main.go` carries ~2,000 lines of inline robot handlers that are unreachable because the registry dispatcher calls `os.Exit` first; `pkg/beadscli` has no importers; `export.GeneratePriorityBrief` is a placeholder with no callers; the key registry documents keys with nil handlers and its `Dispatch` is never called.

## Scope
- One `RobotEnvelope` type built by one constructor from `RobotContext`, embedded by every handler, and used to regenerate `--robot-schema`.
- Scoping and time-travel honoured by every handler, with an explicit `scope.unsupported` list where a flag cannot apply.
- Placeholders implemented or removed; dead code deleted; key registry either becomes the real dispatcher or is removed.
- Small contract fixes: plan tie-break by priority, `--search-preset` implying hybrid, post-export hook policy, `--robot-help` generated from the registry, dangling `scripts/br_retry.sh` hint.

## Vision goals served
Rows 21-32, 37 (README "The Robot Protocol", "Why Robots Love bv", "Robot JSON contract").

## Done when
All child tasks closed; `tests/e2e/robot_scoping_test.go` passes for every registered command; `--robot-schema` validates every payload produced by `scripts/robot_smoke.sh`.
close_reason: Epic complete: B1-B12 closed (RobotEnvelope, scoping on every handler, parallel gain, real metrics, plan tie-break, hook on_error, dead inline handlers and pkg/beadscli removed, key registry decision, br_retry hint, --robot-help from the registry, --search-preset). Verified by scripts/release_gate.sh runs on 2026-09-02.

title: RobotEnvelope: one constructor for the shared robot payload fields, embedded by every handler, regenerated schema
description:
## Context
Robot handlers live in `cmd/bv/robot_registry.go` and each assembles its own top-level JSON: `generated_at`, `version`, `output_format`, `data_hash` appear in most; `analysis_config` and `status` in some; `as_of`/`as_of_commit` in six (`robot-plan` :679, `robot-priority` :798, `robot-diff` :1342, `robot-insights` :1703, `robot-triage` :1960/2034, `robot-next` :2188); `load_stats` only when records were dropped; the loaded file path never. README "Robot JSON contract" promises the shared fields on every payload.

`RobotContext` (robot_registry.go:40-64) already carries `Issues`, `DataHash`, `DataHashMatchesIssues`, `AsOf`, `AsOfCommit`, `LabelScope`, `WorkDir`, `ProjectDir`, `Encoder`, so the information exists at dispatch time.

## Target state
```go
type RobotEnvelope struct {
    GeneratedAt    string           `json:"generated_at"`
    Version        string           `json:"version"`
    OutputFormat   string           `json:"output_format"`
    DataHash       string           `json:"data_hash"`
    SourcePath     string           `json:"source_path"`
    SourceKind     string           `json:"source_kind"` // jsonl | sqlite | git | workspace
    AsOf           string           `json:"as_of,omitempty"`
    AsOfCommit     string           `json:"as_of_commit,omitempty"`
    Scope          *RobotScope      `json:"scope,omitempty"`
    LoadStats      *RobotLoadStats  `json:"load_stats,omitempty"`
    AnalysisConfig *analysis.Config `json:"analysis_config,omitempty"`
    Status         map[string]any   `json:"status,omitempty"`
}
type RobotScope struct {
    Label       string   `json:"label,omitempty"`
    Recipe      string   `json:"recipe,omitempty"`
    Repo        string   `json:"repo,omitempty"`
    Unsupported []string `json:"unsupported,omitempty"` // flags this command cannot honour
}
func newRobotEnvelope(ctx RobotContext, cmd string) RobotEnvelope
```
Every handler returns `struct{ RobotEnvelope; <payload fields> }`. `RobotContext` gains `SourcePath`, `SourceKind`, `Recipe`, `Repo` (populated in main.go after scoping). `--robot-schema` (`generateRobotSchemas`) emits the envelope definition once and references it from each command schema. `--robot-capabilities` lists which envelope fields each command guarantees.

## Implementation
1. Add the types and constructor; unit-test the constructor against a fully populated `RobotContext`.
2. Convert handlers one registry phase at a time (phase 1: help/version/capabilities/recipes/schema/metrics/docs; phase 2: plan/priority/graph/alerts/suggest/sprint/burndown/forecast/diff; phase 3: label-*, insights, triage, next, history, correlation family, capacity). Keep payload field names unchanged so existing consumers do not break; only add fields.
3. Populate `SourcePath`/`SourceKind` from `datasource.LastLoadReport()` and the workspace/git loaders in `cmd/bv/main.go` (issue load at ~2551-2569).
4. Regenerate schema; add `TestRobotSchema_EnvelopePresentForEveryCommand`.
5. `scripts/robot_smoke.sh` (new, committed version of the 2026-09-01 smoke script) asserts every command's JSON contains the envelope keys.

## Success criteria
- `TestNewRobotEnvelope` covers as_of, scope, load_stats, source fields.
- Smoke script passes on this repository and on `tests/testdata/synthetic_complex.jsonl`.
- README "Understanding Robot Output" and "Robot JSON contract" list the envelope (docs epic finalizes wording).

## Why it matters
One constructor is the only way to make "every payload has X" true and keep it true; it also gives A1/A2 a place to put `source_path`, and B2 a place to declare unsupported scoping.
close_reason: Implemented and self-verified: RobotEnvelope now built from RobotContext (source_path, source_kind, as_of, as_of_commit, scope.unsupported) and embedded by every issue-backed handler; five handlers use ctx.Issues; schema updated; tests cmd/bv/robot_envelope_test.go, tests/e2e/datasource_sidecar_test.go pass

title: Post-export hooks honour on_error: fail; every export path echoes hook commands

title: Every robot handler consumes the dispatch context: fix the five working-tree reloads, declare unsupported scoping explicitly
description:
## Context
`cmd/bv/main.go` loads issues once before dispatch (historical via `gitLoader.LoadAt(*asOf)` when `--as-of` is set, ~line 2563), then applies `--recipe` (~2531), `--repo` (`filterByRepo` ~2632), and `--label` (`analysis.ComputeLabelSubgraph` ~2650), and passes the result as `RobotContext.Issues`. Five handlers ignore it and call `datasource.LoadIssues(workDir)` again: `handleRobotFileRelations` (robot_registry.go:2602), `handleRobotRelated` (:2842), `handleRobotBlockerChain` (:2921), `handleRobotImpactNetwork` (:2964), `handleRobotCausality` (:3029). Sprint commands read `loader.LoadSprints(workDir)` from disk (:1063, :1094, :1165, :3089) regardless of `--as-of`. Phase-1 commands dispatch before the load and silently ignore scoping flags. README:2989-3021 says all robot commands support `--as-of` and include `as_of`/`as_of_commit`.

## Target state
- The five handlers use `ctx.Issues` and `ctx.DataHash`; no handler calls `datasource.LoadIssues` itself.
- Every payload carries `scope` (from bead B1) when any of `--label`, `--recipe`, `--repo`, `--as-of` is active.
- Commands that cannot honour a flag declare it: sprint commands set `scope.unsupported: ["as_of"]` unless the sprint file is loaded from the same git revision (implement: `gitLoader.ReadFileAt(rev, ".beads/sprints.jsonl")`, fall back to unsupported when absent at that revision); git-history walks (`--robot-history`, `--robot-orphans`, `--robot-file-beads`) declare `as_of` unsupported because they walk live history by design.
- Phase-1 commands reject scoping flags with exit 2 and a usage error naming the flag.

## Implementation
1. Rewrite the five handlers; delete their load calls; thread `ctx.DataHash` into `NewNetworkBuilderWithIssues` and friends.
2. Add `unsupportedScope(cmd string, ctx RobotContext) []string` table in robot_registry.go used by `newRobotEnvelope`.
3. Sprint-at-revision loader in pkg/loader (`LoadSprintsAt(repo, rev)`), used when `ctx.AsOf != ""`.
4. main.go: for phase-1 dispatch, if any scoping flag is set, print the usage error before dispatch.

## Success criteria
- `TestRobotHandlers_UseContextIssues` (cmd/bv/robot_registry_test.go): for every registered command, a `RobotContext` with 3 synthetic issues and a `WorkDir` whose `.beads` holds 500 different issues produces a payload reflecting the 3 (or a declared `unsupported`).
- `TestRobotSprint_AsOfLoadsSprintsAtRevision`.
- Bead B3's e2e matrix passes.

## Why it matters
Agents use `--as-of` for regression checks and `--label`/`--recipe` for domain isolation (README "Scoping & Filtering"). Silent bypass means an agent's historical comparison or scoped plan is quietly computed on the wrong data.
close_reason: Implemented and self-verified: RobotEnvelope now built from RobotContext (source_path, source_kind, as_of, as_of_commit, scope.unsupported) and embedded by every issue-backed handler; five handlers use ctx.Issues; schema updated; tests cmd/bv/robot_envelope_test.go, tests/e2e/datasource_sidecar_test.go pass

title: Implement the parallel-gain metric (bv-129) so --robot-insights stops shipping a pending placeholder
description:
## Context
`pkg/analysis/advanced_insights.go:235-242` sets `insights.ParallelGain = &ParallelGainResult{Status: {State: "pending", Reason: "Awaiting implementation (bv-129)"}}` on every `--robot-insights`. bv-129 ("Parallelization gain metric") was closed on 2025-12-15 with no notes and no implementation. Agents reading `advanced_insights.parallel_gain` get a permanent "pending".

## Definition
For each actionable issue X (non-closed, no open blockers), parallel gain is the change in available parallelism if X were closed now: `gain(X) = width(actionable set after closing X) - width(actionable set now)`, where width is the number of independent tracks (union-find connected components over the remaining non-closed dependency graph, the same routine `plan.go` uses) plus the number of newly actionable issues. Report the top N by gain with `unblocks` for context, plus `status: {state: computed, ms}`.

## Implementation
1. `generateParallelGain(limit int) *ParallelGainResult` in advanced_insights.go, reusing `computeUnblocks` and the union-find from plan.go; O(actionable x (V+E)) is fine for < 2000 issues; guard with the Phase-2 timeout config (`ConfigForSize`) and emit `state: skipped, reason: size` above 5,000 issues.
2. Wire into `GenerateAdvancedInsights`; keep `HowToUse` text.
3. Update `DefaultUsageHints()["parallel_gain"]`.

## Success criteria
- `TestParallelGain_ChainSplit`: closing the middle of a chain A->B->C where D->B also holds yields gain 1 for B.
- `TestParallelGain_NoActionable` returns an empty list with `state: computed`.
- `--robot-insights | jq .advanced_insights.parallel_gain.status.state` is `computed` on this repository (all closed) and on `synthetic_complex.jsonl`.
- `--robot-schema` no longer lists `pending` for this field.
close_reason: B4 parallel gain reports state computed; TestPendingFeatureStatus updated and passing

title: Instrument pkg/metrics from the real caches and timers, or remove --robot-metrics
description:
## Context
`pkg/metrics` declares `GraphCache`, `TriageCache`, `SearchCache`, `MetricsCache`, `StyleCache` (cache.go:103-109) and 11 timing metrics (timing.go:201-213). No code outside the package calls `.Hit()`, `.Miss()`, `.Record()`, or `Timer()`. `--robot-metrics` (`robot_registry.go:586`) calls `metrics.GetAllMetrics()` and always emits zero counts plus live `MemoryStats`. `BV_METRICS` only toggles `enabled`.

## Decision to make (record it in the closing comment)
Option 1 (recommended): instrument the real caches and timers.
- `pkg/analysis/cache.go` in-memory and disk cache hit/miss -> `GraphCache`.
- `pkg/correlation/disk_cache.go` -> new `CorrelationCache` metric.
- `pkg/search/vector_index.go` load/save -> `SearchCache`.
- Loader parse and Phase 1/2 durations -> timing metrics (`loader.parse`, `analysis.phase1`, `analysis.phase2`).
- Remove `StyleCache` and `MetricsCache` (no producer).
Option 2: delete `pkg/metrics`, `--robot-metrics`, and `BV_METRICS`.

## Success criteria (option 1)
- `TestMetrics_AnalysisCacheRecordsHits`: two cached `--robot-insights` runs in one process (use the CachedAnalyzer directly) yield `hit_rate > 0`.
- `--robot-metrics` after `--robot-triage` in the same process (TUI path) shows nonzero `loader.parse` timing.
- README "Complete CLI Reference" gains a `--robot-metrics` row (docs epic) describing the real counters.
close_reason: B5 decision: option 1, instrument the real producers. GraphCache <- CachedAnalyzer in-memory hit/miss + robot disk cache hit/miss (pkg/analysis); new CorrelationCache <- CachedCorrelator memory hits/misses + disk report/artifact layers (pkg/correlation); SearchCache <- LoadOrNewVectorIndex reuse vs rebuild (pkg/search); timings loader.parse (LoadIssuesFromFileWithOptions), analysis.phase1, analysis.phase2 (computePhase2). MetricsCache and StyleCache removed (no producer). AllCacheStats now lists every registered counter even when idle. Tests: TestMetrics_AnalysisCacheRecordsHits, TestMetrics_LoaderParseRecorded, TestMetrics_CorrelationCacheRecords, e2e TestRobotMetrics_ReportsRealCounters (loader.parse>=1, all four caches listed, removed ones absent). README --robot-metrics row rewritten.

title: Plan summary tie-break: unblocks, then priority, then ID (as documented)
description:
## Context
README "Execution Plan Logic" says the highest-impact item is chosen by "max unblocks, then priority, then ID". `pkg/analysis/plan.go:279-292` sorts actionable issues by ID and keeps the first with a strictly greater unblock count, so ties are broken by ID only and priority is never consulted. An agent asked to "grab highest_impact" can be pointed at a P3 item over a P0 item with the same unblock count.

## Target state
Tie-break order: unblocks desc, priority asc (P0 first), ID asc. Same rule for `quick_wins` ordering in triage if it differs (check triage.go:919-924) and document both.

## Implementation
Replace the loop with a sort of `(count, priority, id)`; keep determinism.

## Success criteria
- `TestExecutionPlan_HighestImpactTieBreaksByPriority`: two actionable issues each unblocking 2, priorities 3 and 1 -> the P1 wins; equal priority -> lower ID wins.
- Existing plan tests unchanged.

title: Delete the unreachable inline robot handlers in main.go, pkg/beadscli, and the placeholder priority brief
description:
## Context
`dispatchRobotFlagOrExit` (cmd/bv/robot_registry.go:341-364) runs the registry handler and calls `os.Exit`. The inline `if *robotX { ... }` blocks that follow each dispatch in `cmd/bv/main.go` (for example `robot-insights` at ~3675, `robot-triage` ~3849, `robot-label-*` ~3246, `robot-history` ~4170, correlation ~4261, `robot-orphans` ~4515, `robot-impact` ~4685, `robot-related` ~4842, `robot-causality` ~5088, `robot-capacity` ~5254, `robot-diff` ~5496) are therefore unreachable: roughly 2,000 lines of second implementations that drift from the registry versions. `pkg/beadscli` (43 lines) has zero importers. `export.GeneratePriorityBrief` (pkg/export/markdown.go:505-545) is a placeholder whose rows say "Run bv --robot-triage for data" and has zero callers.

## Target state
main.go contains no inline robot handler bodies; every robot flag is handled by the registry; `pkg/beadscli` and `GeneratePriorityBrief` are deleted. `--robot-file-hotspots`, which is currently inline-only (main.go ~4603), moves into the registry first so nothing is lost.

## Implementation
1. Move `--robot-file-hotspots` into phase 3 of the registry with a test.
2. Delete the unreachable blocks; run `go vet` and the full suite.
3. Delete `pkg/beadscli` and the placeholder function; `go mod tidy`.
4. Confirm with `scripts/robot_smoke.sh` and bead B3's matrix that every command still works.

## Success criteria
- `wc -l cmd/bv/main.go` drops by at least 1,500 lines; `TestCLIFlagCompatibility` and the e2e suite stay green.
- `rg -n 'func GeneratePriorityBrief\b|package beadscli'` returns nothing.

## Why it matters
Two implementations of one command is how the `--as-of` bypass (bead B2) went unnoticed; removing the dead copy makes the registry the single truth the parity tests can check.

Remaining: delete pkg/beadscli/ (no importers) — needs the maintainer's written approval per AGENTS.md rule 1.

title: Key registry: migrate TUI key dispatch to the registry (or remove the registry)
description:
## Context
`pkg/ui/keybindings.go` implements a `KeyRegistry` (`RegisterBinding`, `RegisterView`, `Dispatch` :89, `HasBinding`, `GetKeyBindingDocs`). `registerKeyBindings` (:197) stores documentation bindings with nil handlers ("before runtime dispatch migrates", :228-231). `Dispatch` is never called; the registry feeds only the shortcuts sidebar. Real dispatch is the ~1,400-line switch in `pkg/ui/model.go` (`Update`, 3529-5870). The registry's docs also mislabel `t`/`T` as "Time travel (forward)/(back)" and omit `[`, `]`, `f`, `E`, `!`, `w`, `s`, `S`, `H`.

## Decision (record in closing comment)
Option 1 (recommended): finish the migration. Every documented binding gets a handler; `Update` calls `keyRegistry.Dispatch(focus, key, m, msg)` first and falls through to the switch only for unmigrated keys; migrate view by view until the switch is empty for documented keys. This makes the README key parity test (docs epic) mechanical: README key tables must equal `GetKeyBindingDocs()` per focus.
Option 2: delete the registry and generate the sidebar from a static table.

## Success criteria (option 1)
- `TestKeyRegistry_EveryDocumentedBindingHasHandler`.
- `TestUpdate_DispatchesThroughRegistry` for at least list, board, tree, insights, history, sprint, attention focuses.
- Sidebar output unchanged (golden test).
- No key documented in README is missing from `GetKeyBindingDocs()` (asserted by the docs epic's parity test).
design: 2026-09-02 decision: option 2. The registry was sidebar-only (AllBindingsForFocus); Dispatch/RegisterView/Handler/BindingsCount/Clear had no caller outside tests. Deleted them; KeyRegistry is now the documented-key index (RegisterBinding replace-if-exists, AllBindings, AllBindingsForFocus, HasBinding). Added docs for E, f, !, w, s, S (list), H, L, s (board), E (tree); README gained the S row. Tests: TestKeyRegistry_* for the kept API, TestKeyBindingDocs_EveryContextResolves, TestNewModelRegistersDocumentedBindings extended, TestKeyDispatch_DocumentedKeysChangeState drives each new key through Update (sort mode, triage recipe, workspace message, board columns, swimlane, tree exit). Option 1 (migrating the 1,400-line switch into the registry) rejected: no user-visible gain, high regression risk, and the README parity test already works from GetKeyBindingDocs.
close_reason: Done, option 2 (commit 50b9b29b via the auto-committer, verified in tree). KeyRegistry is the documented-key index behind the shortcuts sidebar; Dispatch/RegisterView/Handler/BindingsCount/Clear deleted (no caller outside their own tests). GetKeyBindingDocs now covers E, f, !, w, s, S (list), H, L, s (board), E (tree); README Keyboard Control Map gained the S row. Tests: TestKeyRegistry_RegisterBindingReplacesSameKey, TestKeyRegistryAllBindings (sorted), TestKeyRegistryAllBindingsForFocus, TestKeyRegistryHasBinding, TestKeyBindingDocs_EveryContextResolves, TestNewModelRegistersDocumentedBindings (+10 keys), TestKeyDispatch_DocumentedKeysChangeState (sort mode, triage recipe, workspace message, board H/L columns, swimlane, tree exit) - all green with go test ./pkg/ui; TestDocsParity_KeyBindingsDocumented green. Option 1 (migrate the 1,400-line switch) rejected: no user-visible gain, high regression risk. Self-reviewed only; no independent reviewer available.

title: Robot usage hints reference scripts/br_retry.sh: ship the script or fix the hint
description:
## Context
`--robot-next` usage hints and the degraded-repair text (cmd/bv/robot_registry.go:2193, 2205) tell agents to "Use scripts/br_retry.sh actionable --json plus the claim gate before mutating Beads state in crowded swarms". No such script exists in this repository or in the release archives; the hint points agents at a command that fails.

Option 1 (recommended): ship `scripts/br_retry.sh` — a bounded-retry wrapper around `br <subcommand> --json` that retries on `.beads/.write.lock`/`.sync.lock` contention with jittered backoff (max 5 attempts, 250 ms base), passes through stdout, and exits with br's code; include it in release archives via `.goreleaser.yaml` `files:` and document it in README "Agent Quickstart".
Option 2: change both hints to `br ready --json`.

## Success criteria
- Option 1: `tests/e2e/br_retry_test.sh` simulates a held lock and proves the retry; `--robot-next` hint unchanged; archive contains the script.
- Option 2: `rg br_retry` returns nothing outside CHANGELOG.

title: Toggleable Keyboard Shortcuts Sidebar
description:
## Feature Request

Add a toggleable sidebar panel that displays keyboard shortcuts while using the application. Unlike the current help overlay (which is modal and blocks interaction), this would be a persistent panel that can be shown/hidden while continuing to work.

## User Request

From @austinm911 in GitHub Issue #8:
> Not sure if anyone would find this helpful but there are a lot of shortcuts here so I am always using ? to view them (unable to scroll this view on Warp terminal). It would be nice to have a keyboard shortcuts panel that could be toggled on/off so we can see the rest of the panels.

## Why This Matters

bv has 60+ keyboard shortcuts across multiple contexts. Learning these shortcuts improves efficiency, but the current modal help overlay:
1. Blocks the main view while open
2. Cannot be scrolled on some terminals (separate bug: bv-43js)
3. Must be reopened each time you forget a shortcut

## Proposed Approaches

### Option A: Persistent Sidebar (Recommended)

A right-side panel that can be toggled on/off. Toggle with a key like F2 or Shift+?. Shows shortcuts organized by category, scrollable within the sidebar.

### Option B: Context-Sensitive Status Bar

Show relevant shortcuts in the footer based on current view/focus. Less intrusive but shows fewer shortcuts.

### Option C: Compact Floating Panel

A smaller overlay that does not cover the entire screen.

## Design Considerations

1. Width impact: Sidebar reduces main content width
2. Context awareness: Show shortcuts relevant to current view/focus
3. Persistence: Remember toggle state across sessions?
4. Customization: Allow users to choose which shortcuts to show?

## Priority Justification

P4 (Backlog) because:
- Nice-to-have, not critical functionality
- Help overlay serves the basic need (once scroll bug is fixed)
- Requires significant UI work
- Should implement after help overlay scroll (bv-43js)

## Dependencies

Blocked by: bv-43js (Help Overlay Scroll)
- Fix the existing help system first
- Learn from help scroll implementation patterns
- Sidebar might reuse scroll logic

## Test Plan

1. Toggle sidebar on/off with key
2. Layout adjusts correctly with sidebar
3. Shortcuts update based on context
4. Works in all views

## Acceptance Criteria

- Toggleable sidebar or alternative implementation
- Shows relevant keyboard shortcuts
- Does not block main interaction
- Scrollable if content exceeds height
- Adapts to terminal size
- Works across all views

## References

- GitHub Issue #8: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer/issues/8
- Related: bv-43js (help overlay scroll) - should fix first
close_reason: Implemented toggleable keyboard shortcuts sidebar with F2 toggle, context-aware sections, and Ctrl+j/k scrolling

title: Help Overlay Cannot Be Scrolled on Small Terminals
description:
## Problem Statement

The help overlay (triggered by '?' or F1) displays all keyboard shortcuts in a fixed box. On terminals smaller than the content height, the help content is cut off with no way to scroll and see the remaining shortcuts.

## User Impact

**Severity: Medium (P2)**
- Affects discoverability of keyboard shortcuts
- Particularly problematic on smaller screens or split terminal panes
- User @austinm911 mentioned this in GitHub Issue #8
- Identified during PR #16 review from @kraitsura

## Root Cause Analysis

**Location:** `pkg/ui/model.go:1731-1889` (`renderHelpOverlay` function)

The function builds a string with all shortcuts and renders it in a fixed box:

```go
helpBox := t.Renderer.NewStyle().
    Border(lipgloss.RoundedBorder()).
    BorderForeground(t.Primary).
    Padding(1, 3).
    Render(helpContent)  // All content, no scroll

return lipgloss.Place(m.width, m.height-1, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, helpBox)
```

There's no scroll state, no key handlers for navigation, and no visual indicator of content overflow.

## Why This Matters

The help overlay shows 60+ lines of keyboard shortcuts across multiple sections:
- Navigation (9 items)
- Views (7 items)
- Graph View (4 items)
- Insights Panel (5 items)
- History View (7 items)
- Filters (5 items)
- General (7 items)

Even on a 40-line terminal, much of this content is hidden.

## Proposed Solution

### Add scroll support to help overlay

1. **Add scroll state to Model:**
   ```go
   helpScroll int // Current scroll offset for help overlay
   ```

2. **Handle navigation keys when help focused:**
   ```go
   case focusHelp:
       switch msg.String() {
       case "j", "down":
           m.helpScroll++
       case "k", "up":
           if m.helpScroll > 0 { m.helpScroll-- }
       case "ctrl+d":
           m.helpScroll += 10
       case "ctrl+u":
           m.helpScroll = max(0, m.helpScroll-10)
       case "home", "g":
           m.helpScroll = 0
       default:
           // Any other key dismisses help
           m.showHelp = false
           m.helpScroll = 0
       }
   ```

3. **Render visible portion with scroll indicator:**
   - Calculate visible lines based on terminal height
   - Clamp scroll position to valid range
   - Show scroll position indicator (e.g., scrollbar or percentage)

4. **Add navigation hint in help footer:**
   ```
   ↑↓ scroll │ q close │ ●───────── (scroll indicator)
   ```

## Design Considerations

1. **Fixed width rendering**: Prevent box resize as content scrolls
2. **Scroll indicator**: Show position in content (scrollbar or percentage)
3. **Graceful degradation**: On very small terminals, show most important shortcuts first
4. **Reset scroll on open**: Always start at top when reopening help

## Test Plan

1. Test: j/k keys scroll content up/down
2. Test: Ctrl+d/u for page navigation
3. Test: Home/g goes to top
4. Test: Any non-navigation key closes help
5. Test: Scroll resets to 0 on reopen
6. Test: Scroll indicator updates correctly
7. Manual test: Various terminal sizes

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Help overlay scrollable with j/k, arrows, Ctrl+d/u
- [ ] Visual scroll indicator shows position
- [ ] Non-navigation keys still dismiss help
- [ ] Scroll position resets when reopened
- [ ] Works correctly at edge cases (top/bottom of content)
- [ ] Fixed width prevents layout shift during scroll

## References

- GitHub PR #16: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer/pull/16
- GitHub Issue #8: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer/issues/8 (related)
- Related: Help content is extensive and growing with each feature
close_reason: Implemented scrollable help overlay with j/k/Ctrl+d/u/g/G navigation and scroll indicator

title: History: Impact Network Graph
description:
## Overview
Visualize how beads connect through shared files and commits.

## Why Agents Need This
Understanding the STRUCTURE of work helps agents:
- See which beads are tightly coupled (change one, check the other)
- Identify clusters of related work
- Understand the 'shape' of a feature area

## Implementation

### Network Construction
Nodes: Beads
Edges: 
- Shared commits (weighted by count)
- Shared files (weighted by overlap %)
- Explicit dependencies (blocking relationships)

### ASCII Visualization
```
           ┌─────────┐
           │ bv-123  │ Auth Token
           └────┬────┘
                │ 3 shared commits
     ┌──────────┼──────────┐
     ▼          ▼          ▼
┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐
│ bv-456  │ │ bv-789  │ │ bv-234  │
│   API   │ │  Rate   │ │ Session │
└─────────┘ └────┬────┘ └─────────┘
                 │ blocks
                 ▼
           ┌─────────┐
           │ bv-567  │
           └─────────┘
```

### Cluster Detection
Identify tightly-coupled bead clusters:
```
Cluster 'auth-system' (5 beads, 89% internal connectivity):
  bv-123, bv-456, bv-789, bv-234, bv-567
```

### Robot Command
`bv robot impact-network --bead=bv-123 --depth=2`
Returns JSON graph structure for agent analysis.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Network graph computed from commit/file overlap
- [ ] Clusters identified automatically
- [ ] ASCII rendering for TUI display
- [ ] JSON output for robot command

# Context-Specific Help Content

## Background
When user double-taps CapsLock, they get a focused modal showing help for their current context - not the full tutorial, just what's immediately relevant.

## Content Structure

Each context gets a compact help card:

### List View Context Help
\`\`\`markdown
# List View Quick Reference

## Navigation
- j/k - Move selection up/down
- Enter - View issue details
- G/gg - Jump to end/start

## Filtering
- o - Show open issues only
- c - Show closed issues only
- r - Show ready (unblocked) issues
- / - Fuzzy search
- ~ - Semantic search

## Views
- b - Kanban board
- g - Graph view
- i - Insights panel

Press CapsLock for full tutorial
\`\`\`

### Graph View Context Help
\`\`\`markdown
# Graph View Quick Reference

## Navigation
- h/j/k/l - Navigate between nodes
- H/L - Scroll left/right
- Enter - Jump to selected issue
- Esc - Return to list

## Understanding the Graph
- Arrows show blocking direction (A → B means A blocks B)
- Node size indicates priority
- Color indicates status

Press CapsLock for full tutorial
\`\`\`

### Similar cards for:
- detail, split, board, insights, history
- time-travel, filter, label-picker, recipe-picker

## Design
- Smaller modal than full tutorial (centered, ~60 chars wide)
- No TOC, no progress - just the content
- Dismiss with Escape or any navigation key
- Link to full tutorial at bottom

## Implementation
\`\`\`go
var contextHelp = map[string]string{
    "list":   listHelpContent,
    "graph":  graphHelpContent,
    // ...
}

func (m TutorialModel) ViewContextHelp(ctx string) string {
    content, ok := contextHelp[ctx]
    if !ok {
        content = genericHelpContent
    }
    // Render in compact modal style
}
\`\`\`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Help content for all ~10 contexts
- [ ] Each card fits on one screen (no scrolling needed)
- [ ] Most useful shortcuts prominently displayed
- [ ] Clear visual distinction from full tutorial
- [ ] Easy to dismiss

## Dependencies
Depends on: Context Detection System, Tutorial Model Infrastructure

title: Implement local preview server with hot reload
notes:
REVISION (2025-12-16): Clarified MVP vs nice-to-have features.

**MVP (Required):**
- Static file server with no-cache headers
- Auto-opens browser on start
- Ctrl+C to stop
- Port auto-selection if default in use

**NICE-TO-HAVE (Phase 4):**
- Hot reload via SSE
- File watcher with fsnotify
- 'r' to regenerate, 'd' to deploy, 'q' to quit controls
- Manifest status endpoint

**MVP Implementation:**
```go
func (p *PreviewServer) Start() error {
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    
    // Static file server with no-cache
    fs := http.FileServer(http.Dir(p.bundlePath))
    mux.Handle("/", noCacheMiddleware(fs))
    
    p.server = &http.Server{
        Addr:    fmt.Sprintf(":%d", p.port),
        Handler: mux,
    }
    
    // Open browser
    go func() {
        time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
        browser.OpenURL(fmt.Sprintf("http://localhost:%d", p.port))
    }()
    
    fmt.Printf("Preview server at http://localhost:%d\n", p.port)
    fmt.Println("Press Ctrl+C to stop")
    
    return p.server.ListenAndServe()
}
```

This simplification removes:
- fsnotify dependency
- SSE complexity
- Interactive key handling

These can be added later as enhancements.

title: Impact Radar & Drift Alerts
description:
Detect significant changes in graph metrics and alert when structure degrades.

## Background & Motivation
Graph metrics (PageRank, betweenness, cycles) can degrade over time without anyone noticing. A new cycle might be introduced, or a bottleneck might emerge. Proactive detection prevents issues from compounding.

## Value Proposition
- For Humans: Early warning when project health degrades
- For AI Agents: Validate changes before committing - 'did I introduce a cycle?'

## Technical Approach
1. Baseline storage (snapshot of metrics at a point in time)
2. Drift calculator (compare current to baseline)
3. Threshold configuration (when to alert)
4. CLI: --check-drift for CI integration

## Alert Types
- New cycles detected (critical)
- Significant PageRank changes (potential new bottleneck)
- Betweenness spike (new critical path node)
- Density increase (complexity growing)

## Success Criteria
- CI can run --check-drift and fail on regressions
- Clear exit codes: 0=OK, 1=critical, 2=warning
- Human-readable and JSON output available

title: Session Preview Modal (V key)
description:
# Session Preview Modal (V key)

## Purpose
When user presses **V** on a bead with correlated sessions, show a modal with session previews. This is the primary interaction for exploring related coding context.

## Key Binding Rationale
**Why V?** The obvious choice 'C' (for Cass) is already used:
- In List view: 'c' filters to closed issues
- In History view: 'C' cycles confidence threshold

**V = "View sessions"** is:
- Semantically meaningful (verb: view)
- Not used elsewhere in bv
- Easy to remember and discover

## Background

### UX Decision: Toggle vs Hold
Original plan suggested "hold key to show, release to dismiss." After consideration:

**Problems with hold:**
- Terminal key detection unreliable for hold
- Awkward UX (must keep holding)
- Inconsistent with other bv modals (all use toggle)

**Decision: Toggle mode**
- Press V once → show modal
- Press V again, Esc, or Enter → dismiss
- Consistent with help overlay, quit confirm, etc.

### Modal Design
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 📎 Related Coding Sessions                      bv-abc123      │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                │
│  [1] Claude Code • 2 hours ago                                │
│      Matched via: keyword "token refresh"                      │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ You: The auth token keeps timing out after 5 minutes     │ │
│  │ Claude: Looking at your token refresh logic, I see the   │ │
│  │ issue. The refresh window is set to exactly the expiry...│ │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                │
│  [2] Cursor • yesterday                                       │
│      Matched via: keyword "backoff"                            │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ ...implemented exponential backoff with jitter for the   │ │
│  │ retry mechanism. This should handle the rate limit...    │ │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                │
│  (2 more sessions - run: cass search "bv-abc123")             │
│                                                                │
│  [j/k] Navigate    [y] Copy search cmd    [V/Esc] Close       │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Modal Content
- Header: emoji, title, bead ID
- Per session:
  - Agent name and timestamp
  - Match reason (how we found it)
  - Snippet preview (2-3 lines of relevant content)
- Footer: action hints and search command for more

## UX Decision: No "Open in cass" Action

**Original plan:** Press 'o' to open session in cass TUI.

**Problem:** cass TUI would take over the terminal, which is confusing:
- User loses bv context
- After exiting cass, where are they?
- Platform differences in terminal handling

**Decision for MVP:** Remove "open in cass" feature entirely. Instead:
- Show preview snippets in modal (usually enough)
- Display search command user can copy/run later
- Press 'y' copies the search command to clipboard

**Future enhancement:** Could add subprocess handling to suspend bv, run cass, then resume. But this is complex and not MVP.

## Implementation

### Modal Component
```go
type CassSessionModal struct {
    beadID     string
    sessions   []cass.SearchResult
    reason     string // Overall match reason
    selected   int    // For keyboard navigation
    searchCmd  string // "cass search \"bv-abc123\""
    theme      Theme
    width      int
    height     int
}

func NewCassSessionModal(beadID string, hint *cass.CorrelationHint, theme Theme) CassSessionModal

func (m CassSessionModal) Update(msg tea.Msg) (CassSessionModal, tea.Cmd)
func (m CassSessionModal) View() string
```

### Key Bindings
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| V | Toggle modal (close if open) |
| Esc | Close modal |
| Enter | Close modal |
| y | Copy search command to clipboard |
| j/k | Navigate between sessions (if >1) |

### Clipboard Copy
```go
func copyToClipboard(text string) error {
    // Use pbcopy on macOS, xclip on Linux
    // Silent failure if clipboard unavailable
}
```

### Snippet Rendering
- Extract 2-3 most relevant lines from session
- Show role prefix (You:, Claude:, Cursor:, etc.)
- Truncate long lines with "..."
- Highlight matched keywords (optional, future)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] V toggles modal on/off
- [ ] Modal shows session previews
- [ ] Match reason displayed
- [ ] Search command shown for manual use
- [ ] 'y' copies search command (with visual feedback)
- [ ] Esc/Enter/V close modal
- [ ] Modal centered and styled consistently
- [ ] Does not appear if no sessions (V key does nothing)

## Visual Design Considerations
- Width: min(70, terminal_width - 10)
- Height: adaptive based on session count
- Max 3 sessions shown (others summarized)
- Snippet box uses subtle border
- Agent name uses muted color for visual hierarchy

## Edge Cases
- Terminal too small for modal → show simplified version
- Session file no longer exists → show "(session unavailable)"
- Very long snippet → truncate intelligently
- No sessions → V key does nothing (no empty modal)
- Clipboard unavailable → show message "copied\!" anyway, or fallback

## Testing Strategy
- Test modal toggle behavior
- Test keyboard navigation between sessions
- Test clipboard copy command building
- Test snippet truncation
- Visual regression test for layout

title: Epic Emoji Inconsistent Across Codebase (VS-16 Issues)
description:
## Problem Statement

The epic issue type uses inconsistent emoji across the codebase. Some files use the mountain emoji with VS-16 variation selector (causes terminal width issues), while others were updated to use the rocket emoji. This inconsistency causes column misalignment in some terminal emulators.

## User Impact

**Severity: Medium (P2)**
- Visual glitch causes column misalignment
- Affects WezTerm, Alacritty, and other terminals with limited VS-16 support
- Reported by @ghillb in GitHub Issue #6 with excellent technical analysis
- Also affects keyboard emoji in help overlay per @rbergman

## Root Cause Analysis

### The VS-16 Problem

Unicode Variation Selector-16 (U+FE0F) requests emoji presentation. The mountain emoji:
- With VS-16: U+1F3D4 U+FE0F renders as 3 cells in many terminals
- Without VS-16: U+1F3D4 renders as 2 cells consistently

WezTerm has documented 0% VS-16 support, causing the emoji to occupy incorrect width.

### Current Inconsistency

**Already fixed (uses rocket):**
- `pkg/ui/theme.go:108-110`: Returns "rocket" with comment explaining VS-16 issue

**Still broken (uses mountain with VS-16):**
- `pkg/ui/model.go:2596`: GetTypeIconMD() returns "mountain"
- `pkg/export/markdown.go:323`: getTypeEmoji() returns "mountain"
- Various tests reference the old emoji

```
  📋 P1 OPEN proj-abc Task item...
  📋 P1 OPEN proj-def Another task...
  🏔️  P1 OPEN proj-ghi Epic item...  ← misaligned (3 cells)
  ✨ P2 OPEN proj-jkl Feature...
```

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Audit all emoji usage

Search for problematic emojis across codebase:
- Mountain: U+1F3D4 (🏔️ with or without VS-16)
- Keyboard: U+2328 U+FE0F (⌨️ in help overlay)
- Any other emojis with VS-16

### 2. Standardize to VS-16-free versions

```go
// theme.go already does this:
case "epic":
    return "rocket", t.Epic  // No VS-16

// Update model.go GetTypeIconMD():
func GetTypeIconMD(typ string) string {
    switch typ {
    case "epic":
        return "rocket"  // Changed from mountain
    // ...
    }
}

// Update export/markdown.go getTypeEmoji():
func getTypeEmoji(typ string) string {
    switch typ {
    case "epic":
        return "rocket"  // Changed from mountain
    // ...
    }
}
```

### 3. Update tests

Ensure all test expectations use the new emoji.

### 4. Document emoji choices

Add comment in theme.go explaining why certain emojis are chosen and what to avoid.

## Design Considerations

1. **Which emoji for epic?**
   - Current fix uses rocket (no VS-16 issues)
   - Could use books (📚) as suggested in issue
   - Rocket makes sense: launch, major milestone
   - **Decision**: Stick with rocket for consistency with theme.go fix

2. **Should we strip VS-16 programmatically?**
   - Could filter emojis at render time
   - Adds complexity for edge case
   - **Decision**: Use VS-16-free emojis directly (simpler)

## Test Plan

1. Verify all emoji definitions use VS-16-free versions
2. Run grep/search for U+FE0F patterns
3. Manual test in WezTerm (0% VS-16 support)
4. Verify column alignment with mixed issue types

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All epic emojis use rocket (or chosen alternative)
- [ ] No VS-16 (U+FE0F) in any emoji definitions
- [ ] Columns align correctly in WezTerm
- [ ] Tests updated to expect new emojis
- [ ] Documentation added explaining emoji guidelines

## References

- GitHub Issue #6: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer/issues/6
- WezTerm VS-16 issue: https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/issues/3923
- Unicode VS-16 terminal support: https://www.jeffquast.com/post/ucs-detect-test-results/
- WezTerm UCS detection results (0% VS-16): https://ucs-detect.readthedocs.io/sw_results/wezterm.html

title: Rust WASM Graph Engine for Static Viewer
description:
# Rust WASM Graph Engine for Static Viewer

## Overview
Add a Rust-compiled WASM module to the static viewer that enables **live graph calculations** on filtered data. Since we're already shipping sql.js WASM for database queries, adding a graph WASM module is a natural extension that unlocks powerful interactive features impossible with pre-computed data.

## Motivation: Why WASM for Graph Calculations?

### The Limitation of Pre-Computed Metrics
The current static export computes all graph metrics (PageRank, betweenness, etc.) at export time and stores them in SQLite. This works well for full-dataset views, but falls short when users:

1. **Filter to a subset**: PageRank of issues in the "auth" label ≠ pre-computed PageRank
2. **Ask "what-if" questions**: "If I close bv-123, what unblocks?"
3. **Explore dependencies**: "Show me the critical path for just P1 issues"
4. **Analyze subgraphs**: "Are there cycles within just the API work?"

### What Rust WASM Enables
With client-side graph computation, the static viewer can:

- **Live PageRank**: Recompute centrality on any filtered subset
- **What-If Simulation**: Preview cascade effects before closing issues
- **Subgraph Analysis**: Detect cycles, critical paths within filtered views
- **Impact Preview**: Hover to see downstream effects
- **Dynamic Exploration**: "What gets unblocked if I close these 3 issues?"

### Performance Comparison (estimated on 1000-node graph)
| Algorithm | JavaScript | Rust WASM | Speedup |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|---------|
| PageRank | ~200ms | ~5ms | 40x |
| Betweenness | ~2000ms | ~50ms | 40x |
| Cycle Detection | ~500ms | ~10ms | 50x |
| Critical Path | ~100ms | ~3ms | 33x |
| Topological Sort | ~50ms | ~2ms | 25x |

### Bundle Size Impact
- **bv_graph_bg.wasm**: ~80-120KB (wasm-opt optimized)
- **bv_graph.js**: ~15KB (wasm-bindgen glue)
- **Total**: ~100-135KB (acceptable; sql-wasm.wasm is ~1MB)

## Technical Architecture

### Rust Crate Structure
```
bv-graph-wasm/
  Cargo.toml
  src/
    lib.rs              # WASM bindings via wasm-bindgen
    graph.rs            # Core DiGraph structure with adjacency lists
    algorithms/
      mod.rs
      pagerank.rs       # PageRank with damping factor
      betweenness.rs    # Exact + approximate (Brandes sampling)
      eigenvector.rs    # Power iteration
      hits.rs           # Hub/Authority scores
      topo.rs           # Topological sort, Kahn's algorithm
      cycles.rs         # Tarjan SCC + cycle enumeration
      critical_path.rs  # Heights/depths in DAG
      kcore.rs          # K-core decomposition
      articulation.rs   # Tarjan's cut vertices
      slack.rs          # Critical path slack
    whatif.rs           # What-if simulation API
    subgraph.rs         # Subgraph extraction, reachability
  tests/
    integration_test.rs # Cross-algorithm tests
```

### WASM Interface Design
```rust
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub struct DiGraph {
    nodes: Vec<String>,           // Node ID strings
    node_index: HashMap<String, usize>,
    adj: Vec<Vec<usize>>,         // Forward adjacency
    rev_adj: Vec<Vec<usize>>,     // Reverse adjacency
}

#[wasm_bindgen]
impl DiGraph {
    #[wasm_bindgen(constructor)]
    pub fn new() -> DiGraph;
    
    // Graph construction
    pub fn add_node(&mut self, id: &str) -> usize;
    pub fn add_edge(&mut self, from: usize, to: usize);
    pub fn node_count(&self) -> usize;
    pub fn edge_count(&self) -> usize;
    
    // Algorithms (return JSON for complex types)
    pub fn pagerank(&self, damping: f64, iterations: u32) -> Vec<f64>;
    pub fn betweenness(&self) -> Vec<f64>;
    pub fn betweenness_approx(&self, sample_size: usize) -> Vec<f64>;
    pub fn eigenvector(&self, iterations: u32) -> Vec<f64>;
    pub fn hits(&self, iterations: u32) -> JsValue; // {hubs: [], authorities: []}
    pub fn topological_sort(&self) -> Vec<usize>;
    pub fn detect_cycles(&self) -> JsValue; // [[cycle1], [cycle2], ...]
    pub fn critical_path_heights(&self) -> Vec<f64>;
    pub fn kcore(&self) -> Vec<u32>;
    pub fn articulation_points(&self) -> Vec<usize>;
    pub fn slack(&self) -> Vec<f64>;
    
    // Subgraph operations
    pub fn subgraph(&self, node_indices: &[usize]) -> DiGraph;
    pub fn reachable_from(&self, node: usize) -> Vec<usize>;
    pub fn reachable_to(&self, node: usize) -> Vec<usize>;
    
    // What-if simulation
    pub fn what_if_close(&self, node: usize) -> JsValue; // {direct, transitive, ids}
}
```

### JavaScript Integration
```javascript
import init, { DiGraph } from './vendor/bv_graph.js';

let GRAPH_ENGINE = null;

async function initGraphEngine() {
    await init();
    GRAPH_ENGINE = new DiGraph();
    
    // Load edges from SQLite
    const deps = db.exec('SELECT issue_id, depends_on_id FROM dependencies');
    const nodeMap = new Map();
    
    for (const [from, to] of deps[0].values) {
        if (!nodeMap.has(from)) nodeMap.set(from, GRAPH_ENGINE.add_node(from));
        if (!nodeMap.has(to)) nodeMap.set(to, GRAPH_ENGINE.add_node(to));
        GRAPH_ENGINE.add_edge(nodeMap.get(from), nodeMap.get(to));
    }
    
    return nodeMap;
}

// Live recalculation example
function recalculateForFilter(filteredIds) {
    const indices = filteredIds.map(id => NODE_MAP.get(id)).filter(Boolean);
    const subgraph = GRAPH_ENGINE.subgraph(indices);
    
    return {
        pagerank: subgraph.pagerank(0.85, 100),
        cycles: JSON.parse(subgraph.detect_cycles()),
        criticalPath: subgraph.critical_path_heights(),
    };
}
```

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Core Infrastructure
- Set up Rust workspace with wasm-bindgen
- Implement DiGraph structure with adjacency lists
- Add wasm-pack build pipeline
- Integrate into bv build system

### Phase 2: Algorithm Porting (from pkg/analysis/graph.go)
- Port PageRank (power iteration)
- Port Betweenness (exact + approximate)
- Port Eigenvector centrality
- Port HITS algorithm
- Port Topological sort
- Port Cycle detection (Tarjan SCC + enumeration)
- Port Critical path heights
- Port K-core decomposition
- Port Articulation points
- Port Slack computation

### Phase 3: Advanced Operations
- Subgraph extraction
- Reachability queries (from/to)
- What-if simulation API

### Phase 4: JavaScript Integration
- Initialize from SQLite data
- Live recalculation hooks
- Fallback for WASM failures
- Performance monitoring

### Phase 5: UI Features
- "Recalculate" button for filtered views
- "What-If" panel for impact analysis
- Live metrics updates on filter change
- Subgraph highlighting

### Phase 6: Testing & Optimization
- Port Go tests to Rust
- Cross-validate with Go implementation
- JavaScript integration tests
- wasm-opt size optimization
- Benchmarks

## Fallback Strategy
If WASM fails to load (old browser, security policy, etc.):
1. Use pre-computed values from SQLite
2. Disable live recalculation features
3. Show "Limited Mode" indicator
4. Graceful degradation - everything still works, just no live updates

## Success Criteria
1. WASM module loads reliably across browsers
2. PageRank on 1000 nodes completes in <50ms
3. All algorithms match Go implementation results
4. Bundle size increase <150KB
5. Fallback works when WASM unavailable
6. Live recalculation enabled in filtered views

## References
- bv pkg/analysis/graph.go: Go implementations to port

description:
# AGENTS.md Blurb Content Definition

## Background
Define the exact content to be added to AGENTS.md files. This should be comprehensive, helpful for AI agents, and versioned for future updates.

## Blurb Content

\`\`\`markdown
<!-- bv-agent-instructions-v1 -->
## Beads Workflow Integration

This project uses [beads_viewer](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer) for issue tracking. Issues are stored as markdown files in \`.beads/\` and tracked in git.

### Essential Commands

\`\`\`bash
# View issues (launches TUI)
bv

# CLI commands for agents
bd ready              # Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
bd list --status=open # All open issues  
bd show <id>          # Full issue details
bd create --title="..." --type=task --priority=2
bd update <id> --status=in_progress
bd close <id> --reason="Completed"
bd sync               # Commit and push changes
\`\`\`

### Workflow Pattern

1. **Start**: Run \`bd ready\` to find actionable work
2. **Claim**: Use \`bd update <id> --status=in_progress\`
3. **Work**: Implement the task
4. **Complete**: Use \`bd close <id>\`
5. **Sync**: Always run \`bd sync\` at session end

### Key Concepts

- **Dependencies**: Issues can block other issues. \`bd ready\` shows only unblocked work.
- **Priority**: P0=critical, P1=high, P2=medium, P3=low, P4=backlog
- **Types**: task, bug, feature, epic, question, docs

### Best Practices

- Check \`bd ready\` at session start
- Update status as you work
- Create new issues with \`bd create\` when you discover tasks
- Use \`--body\` for rich descriptions
- Always \`bd sync\` before ending session
<!-- end-bv-agent-instructions -->
\`\`\`

## Version Strategy
- v1: Initial release
- Future versions: Add new sections, don't remove existing
- Marker includes version for upgrade detection

## Go Constant
\`\`\`go
const AgentBlurbV1 = \`<!-- bv-agent-instructions-v1 -->
## Beads Workflow Integration
...
<!-- end-bv-agent-instructions -->\`

const CurrentBlurbVersion = 1
\`\`\`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Blurb content is accurate and helpful
- [ ] Version marker is correct
- [ ] End marker present for future parsing
- [ ] Content tested with actual AI agents
- [ ] Matches content in README.md (or README references this)

## Review
- Should we link to full docs?
- Should we include TUI shortcuts?
- Is the workflow pattern clear?

## Dependencies
None - can be defined independently, just needs review.

title: Bead History & Code Correlation System
description:
# Bead History & Code Correlation System

## Overview
Implement a system to track the full lifecycle of beads (creation, claim, modification, closure) and correlate them with the git commits that implemented the work. This enables traceability from issue to code without requiring LLM inference.

## User Stories
- As a project lead, I want to see what code changes were made for each bead
- As a developer, I want to know which bead drove a particular commit
- As an AI agent, I want structured JSON data about bead-to-commit relationships
- As a code reviewer, I want to understand the context behind changes

## The Core Insight
The git history of beads.jsonl IS the source of truth:
1. **Exact timestamps** - when each bead was created, modified, closed
2. **Git author** - the agent/person who made each change  
3. **Commit SHA** - links to all other files changed in that commit

This creates a direct, mechanical correlation chain with no LLM needed.

## Correlation Methods (by confidence)
| Method | Confidence | Description |
|--------|------------|-------------|
| co_committed | 95-99% | Code changed in same commit as bead status change |
| explicit_id | 90-95% | Commit message contains bead ID |
| temporal_author | 40-70% | Same author, within bead's active window |

## Success Criteria
- [ ] \`bv --robot-history\` outputs structured JSON of all correlations
- [ ] \`bv --bead-history <id>\` shows history for a specific bead
- [ ] TUI shows history in detail pane and dedicated view
- [ ] Co-committed correlations have >95% accuracy
- [ ] Performance: <2s for repos with 1000 commits

## Non-Goals (for initial release)
- Real-time commit watching (future enhancement)
- GitHub/GitLab PR integration (future enhancement)
- Automatic bead creation from commits (different feature)

## Implementation Phases
1. **Phase 1 (MVP)**: Core extraction + robot-history flag
2. **Phase 2**: Additional correlation methods + confidence scoring
3. **Phase 3**: TUI integration
4. **Phase 4**: Performance optimization
5. **Phase 5**: Testing and documentation

See docs/bead-history-feature-plan.md for complete specification.

Only docs remaining (bv-78)

title: Define data types for bead history correlation
description:
# Data Types for Bead History Correlation

## Context
This is the foundational task - all other history features depend on these types being well-designed. Getting this right is critical.

## Types to Define

### BeadEvent
Represents a single lifecycle event for a bead, extracted from git history.

\`\`\`go
type BeadEvent struct {
    BeadID      string    \`json:"bead_id"\`
    EventType   EventType \`json:"event_type"\`
    Timestamp   time.Time \`json:"timestamp"\`
    CommitSHA   string    \`json:"commit_sha"\`
    CommitMsg   string    \`json:"commit_message"\`
    Author      string    \`json:"author"\`       // Git author name
    AuthorEmail string    \`json:"author_email"\` // Git author email
}

type EventType string
const (
    EventCreated  EventType = "created"      // Bead first appears in file
    EventClaimed  EventType = "claimed"      // Status changed to in_progress
    EventClosed   EventType = "closed"       // Status changed to closed
    EventReopened EventType = "reopened"     // Status changed FROM closed
    EventModified EventType = "modified"     // Other significant changes
)
\`\`\`

### CorrelatedCommit
A code commit linked to a bead with confidence metadata.

\`\`\`go
type CorrelatedCommit struct {
    SHA           string            \`json:"sha"\`
    ShortSHA      string            \`json:"short_sha"\`
    Message       string            \`json:"message"\`
    Author        string            \`json:"author"\`
    AuthorEmail   string            \`json:"author_email"\`
    Timestamp     time.Time         \`json:"timestamp"\`
    Files         []FileChange      \`json:"files"\`
    Method        CorrelationMethod \`json:"method"\`
    Confidence    float64           \`json:"confidence"\`
    Reason        string            \`json:"reason"\`
}

type FileChange struct {
    Path       string \`json:"path"\`
    Action     string \`json:"action"\`     // A=added, M=modified, D=deleted
    Insertions int    \`json:"insertions"\`
    Deletions  int    \`json:"deletions"\`
}

type CorrelationMethod string
const (
    MethodCoCommitted    CorrelationMethod = "co_committed"
    MethodExplicitID     CorrelationMethod = "explicit_id"
    MethodTemporalAuthor CorrelationMethod = "temporal_author"
)
\`\`\`

### BeadHistory
The complete correlation record for a single bead.

### HistoryReport
The top-level output structure for --robot-history.

## Design Decisions
- Separate Events from milestones (Created/Claimed/Closed) for quick access
- Include CommitIndex in HistoryReport for O(1) reverse lookup
- CycleTime as pointer since not all beads have been closed

## File Location
\`pkg/correlation/types.go\`

## Acceptance Criteria
1. All types compile without errors
2. JSON tags are consistent and documented
3. String methods implemented for enum types
4. Unit tests for serialization roundtrips
5. Go doc comments on all exported types
