title: [RC-V1] Bind release approval evidence to clean source and shipped artifacts
description:
## Observed gap and background
docs/RELEASING.md requires a full gate on the exact release commit but tells the maintainer to change/commit CHANGELOG after the gate. .goreleaser.yaml has no consuming gate check. RELEASE_GATE_SKIP and ALLOW_MISSING can still produce PASSED. GitHub API on 2026-09-04 lists CI/Release and five other workflows disabled. Downloaded v0.23.0 Linux archive digest eb8bd29259846159104e531c90a0a0f80559a297e5cba3ad03213d7fe549da56 matches GitHub, but binary reports tag 0b770db4 and vcs.modified=true. That establishes no tampering; it fails to establish exact clean-source provenance. Release assets contain five archives and checksums, not the promised SBOM/manifest.

## Required implementation
Extend existing release gate to write a machine-readable receipt recording source revision/tree, relevant untracked/dirty inputs, toolchain, dataset hash, stage outcomes/skips and test commands. Local diagnostic runs may skip, but only a complete clean receipt may authorize the existing packaging flow. Package first from the bound tree, inspect embedded build info, then record archive hashes and attach evidence to release packaging; fail on changed source, skipped stage, missing receipt or revision mismatch. Move changelog/version commit before final gate. Reconcile manifest/SBOM documentation with actual emitted artifacts. Preserve the documented local-release policy; do not enable paid CI or publish as part of implementation.

## Verification and acceptance
Script self-tests with synthetic Git trees and fake stage runners: clean full pass accepted; one skipped/missing/failed stage, post-gate edit, untracked build input, wrong revision, changed artifact or dirty binary rejected. Positive rebuilt artifact verifies its receipt and checksums without any network publication. Include evidence filenames, hashes and concise reasons in diagnostics.

## Delivery constraints
Work in existing implementation/test files where sensible. Do not delete files, rewrite unrelated work, create compatibility shims, or run browser-opening product actions. Build, vet, first-party formatting and relevant tests must pass after implementation. Retain concise failing-before/passing-after evidence with source revision, fixture identity, command, exit code and observed-versus-expected results. The companion test bead is required for completion of this gap.
design: Ambition rounds: existing gate composes all required proofs into one receipt, with pass/fail/skipped distinct. Diagnostic success is not release eligibility. Commit version/docs before final gate. Keep receipt/build outputs outside source to avoid recursive hashes. Record tree/revision/build inputs/toolchain and then archive digests after packaging; reject a post-gate edit or an unmatched binary. Publish validation evidence only through separately authorized release operations. Closure cannot use --force to substitute partial checks for acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] A complete clean gate receipt validates the packaged binary's revision and archive digests.
- [x] Skipped/failed/missing checks, post-gate edits and dirty or mismatched binaries cannot authorize packaging as verified.
- [x] Version/docs are committed before gate and no circular self-hash is required.
- [x] A focused regression fails before this change and passes afterward; affected build/vet/format/tests pass.
notes: Refinement 4: the receipt is an audit artifact, not a cryptographic attestation against a malicious host. Bind only explicitly declared build inputs; exclude the receipt/output path from the source hash and reject undeclared build-relevant untracked inputs. V1 proves receipt enforcement with controls; the final integration task composes real V2/V4/V5 outcomes before declaring a release verified.

## Final completion criterion for the 2026-09-04 reality check
Baseline a90029b8 had 615 closed and zero open beads but observable scope/readiness/action-routing failures plus recipe and proof gaps. This task closes the delivery loop only after all fifteen gap companions pass. It is deliberately open: writing this plan does not fix the product.

## Required checks
1. Run build, vet, first-party formatting, full local and RCH test suites under their documented environments; run required race coverage. Preserve the separate outcomes.
2. Re-run the six-issue counterexample: api-1/backend depends on web-1/frontend depends on ops-1/ops; independent web-9/frontend; api-closed closed; api-defer deferred. Empty label must return no selected issues; repo/label restriction never promotes a globally blocked issue; text/hybrid scoped search excludes ineligible IDs; plan/triage/next/recipe agree on dependency eligibility.
3. Re-run partial workspace (api/safe plus failed missing repo), historical snapshot whose live issue changed, and two real workspaces with colliding local IDs. Authority diagnostics and command routes must be truthful; no mutation command is actually executed against user projects.
4. Verify every recipe view and export field, existing navigation/filter/sort/hook behavior, actual documentation examples and native/browser journeys. Independently evaluate the fixed keyword/hybrid relevance corpus (P5), preserving per-query results and the stated narrowed semantic scope.
5. Recheck performance on frozen datasets with source/configuration identity and result parity, then rebuild/pin graph WASM and package a clean binary with a complete, current gate receipt. Verify the packaged bytes rather than just the working-tree source. No external publication is part of this task.
6. Rescore all 42 vision checklist rows in the existing docs/planning/REALITY_CHECK_BRIDGE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md in place. WORKING needs actual evidence; UNPROVEN does not become WORKING through a closing comment. Recorded narrowed semantic-search/scheduling scope remains explicit.
7. Inspect all implementation and proof acceptance criteria plus br ready/dependency cycles and bv robot-triage/plan/insights. Do not force-close this task while prerequisites remain open. Any residual finding gets an explicit open follow-up before claiming delivery complete.

## Required record
Source and release identities, fixture hashes/commands, expected/observed results, native/browser/RCH environment, per-stage pass/fail/skipped and artifact paths. Correctness, release reproducibility and proof completeness are independent assertions. No unverified deployment or platform is counted green.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All fifteen implementation/proof pairs are complete with evidence.
- [ ] Full source tests and packaged-binary regressions agree on the same revision.
- [ ] Native, browser, RCH, WASM, relevance and performance outcomes are explicit and required checks pass.
- [x] The 42-row checklist is rescored in place with no unowned residual.
- [ ] No --force closure, user-project mutation, publication or silent skip substitutes for verification.

Refinement 1: verified all 32 beads for ownership/dependency meaning. Separated S1 registry tests from S2 search coverage to avoid a false prerequisite. Replaced ambiguous proof titles and made epic/final closure explicit.
Refinement 2: checked each bead's measurable outcome and negative control. Replaced generic shared acceptance checklists on all 28 child tasks with gap-specific assertions; proof tasks now explicitly verify independently rather than requiring a companion to themselves. All fourteen gaps retain unit/integration/E2E coverage and diagnostic evidence.

Added P5 ranking-quality evaluation plus independent proof; final acceptance now covers FIFTEEN gap pairs (superseding fourteen in the original description). P2 waits on performance, relevance, release, provenance, browser and native results so docs cannot outrun their evidence.
Refinement 4: all 34 beads reviewed against actual bv triage/plan/insights and br ready/dependencies. Zero cycles. Clarified dependency-ready versus claimable sets, cache/hash identities, bounded diagnostics, concurrent action revalidation, receipt trust boundary and P1/P5 ownership. Updated the final description itself to fifteen gap pairs; no stale count remains in its instructions.
Refinement 5 complete: all 34 current beads rechecked with the unchanged Phase 5 template. No further substantive changes found. Validation: 15 implementation/proof pairs, 79 dependency edges (48 blocking, 31 parent-child), all proofs block final integration, no dangling dependencies, all acceptance/context present, DB/export descriptions agree, zero cycles, eight ready implementation tasks. title: [RC-V1 proof] Prove release receipts reject skipped, stale and dirty builds
description:
## Independent proof target
docs/RELEASING.md requires a full gate on the exact release commit but tells the maintainer to change/commit CHANGELOG after the gate. .goreleaser.yaml has no consuming gate check. RELEASE_GATE_SKIP and ALLOW_MISSING can still produce PASSED. GitHub API on 2026-09-04 lists CI/Release and five other workflows disabled. Downloaded v0.23.0 Linux archive digest eb8bd29259846159104e531c90a0a0f80559a297e5cba3ad03213d7fe549da56 matches GitHub, but binary reports tag 0b770db4 and vcs.modified=true. That establishes no tampering; it fails to establish exact clean-source provenance. Release assets contain five archives and checksums, not the promised SBOM/manifest.

## Behavior that must be established
Extend existing release gate to write a machine-readable receipt recording source revision/tree, relevant untracked/dirty inputs, toolchain, dataset hash, stage outcomes/skips and test commands. Local diagnostic runs may skip, but only a complete clean receipt may authorize the existing packaging flow. Package first from the bound tree, inspect embedded build info, then record archive hashes and attach evidence to release packaging; fail on changed source, skipped stage, missing receipt or revision mismatch. Move changelog/version commit before final gate. Reconcile manifest/SBOM documentation with actual emitted artifacts. Preserve the documented local-release policy; do not enable paid CI or publish as part of implementation.

## Required unit/integration/E2E coverage
Script self-tests with synthetic Git trees and fake stage runners: clean full pass accepted; one skipped/missing/failed stage, post-gate edit, untracked build input, wrong revision, changed artifact or dirty binary rejected. Positive rebuilt artifact verifies its receipt and checksums without any network publication. Include evidence filenames, hashes and concise reasons in diagnostics.

## Test workmanship and closure
Extend existing test files and harnesses. Test public behavior with a deliberately broken case/old-code negative control; do not merely mirror the implementation or assert keys exist. Log fixture/seed, source revision, argv, relevant nonsecret environment, expected and observed IDs/state, stdout/stderr and exit code on failures. Preserve artifacts for diagnosis. Run focused tests plus existing affected-package suite; use race tests for shared state and real platform/browser execution only where this task requires it. Never count a skipped prerequisite or missing runner as passed. This proof task depends on bv-oonu.1; it can be designed beforehand but closes only after the real implementation and evidence succeed.
design: Ambition rounds: existing gate composes all required proofs into one receipt, with pass/fail/skipped distinct. Diagnostic success is not release eligibility. Commit version/docs before final gate. Keep receipt/build outputs outside source to avoid recursive hashes. Record tree/revision/build inputs/toolchain and then archive digests after packaging; reject a post-gate edit or an unmatched binary. Publish validation evidence only through separately authorized release operations. Closure cannot use --force to substitute partial checks for acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Independently verify: A complete clean gate receipt validates the packaged binary's revision and archive digests.
- [x] Independently verify: Skipped/failed/missing checks, post-gate edits and dirty or mismatched binaries cannot authorize packaging as verified.
- [x] Independently verify: Version/docs are committed before gate and no circular self-hash is required.
- [x] Capture positive and negative control evidence with source revision, fixture, argv, expected/observed values and failure artifacts.
- [x] Required real-service/platform/browser runs are completed where specified; no skipped prerequisite is marked passed.
notes: Refinement 4: the receipt is an audit artifact, not a cryptographic attestation against a malicious host. Bind only explicitly declared build inputs; exclude the receipt/output path from the source hash and reject undeclared build-relevant untracked inputs. V1 proves receipt enforcement with controls; the final integration task composes real V2/V4/V5 outcomes before declaring a release verified.
close_reason: Independently reran complete gate harness, old-code negative, intact sealed archive verification and syntax/static checks at frozen hashes; all original V1 mechanism acceptance met. No native/browser/WASM or real-release claim.

title: [RC-V2] Complete reproducible graph-WASM source provenance and fail on mismatch
description:
## Observed gap and background
docs/PROVENANCE.md explicitly says graph WASM source correspondence is owed: prior build 67c14abd… differs from vendored fb2c84ee…. scripts/build_graph_wasm.sh pins bindgen to Cargo.lock, but there is no rust-toolchain.toml, wasm-opt is optional/unpinned, and a DIFFERENT comparison still exits success. All 15 vendor hashes verify current bytes only. bv-huf5.4 is closed without a matching rebuild receipt.

## Required implementation
Pin compiler/target, dependency lock, bindgen and optimizer version/options; distinguish optimized/nonoptimized output as different pipelines. Make graph glue and WASM one provenance unit with source tree hash and build environment. Rebuild in an isolated output directory; compare byte-for-byte or document unavoidable nondeterminism with a reviewed equivalence procedure, never merely bless a different hash. Update reviewed vendored artifacts and manifest together through the maintainer's normal change process. Gate source correspondence and fail mismatch. Include optional hybrid scorer provenance only when it is actually shipped; preserve JS fallback.

## Verification and acceptance
Two clean builds under the pinned pipeline, manifest/glue/WASM hash checks, wrong bindgen/compiler/optimizer, lock drift, one-byte tamper, missing target/tool and mismatched generated glue. Real graph-WASM parity fixtures verify algorithms, not just file presence. Retain both build receipts and hashes; no green source-correspondence claim if the toolchain cannot run.

## Delivery constraints
Work in existing implementation/test files where sensible. Do not delete files, rewrite unrelated work, create compatibility shims, or run browser-opening product actions. Build, vet, first-party formatting and relevant tests must pass after implementation. Retain concise failing-before/passing-after evidence with source revision, fixture identity, command, exit code and observed-versus-expected results. The companion test bead is required for completion of this gap.
design: Ambition rounds: pinned compiler, target, bindgen and optimizer constitute a single pipeline, including whether optimization is enabled. Glue+WASM+manifest must correspond to one rebuild. Independent algorithmic parity supplements byte checks; it cannot silently replace failed provenance. Missing toolchain or unequal artifact yields explicit incomplete/fail. Two isolated positive builds and a deliberately mismatched pipeline are required.

title: [RC-V2 proof] Prove reproducible WASM and reject pipeline/artifact mismatch
description:
## Independent proof target
docs/PROVENANCE.md explicitly says graph WASM source correspondence is owed: prior build 67c14abd… differs from vendored fb2c84ee…. scripts/build_graph_wasm.sh pins bindgen to Cargo.lock, but there is no rust-toolchain.toml, wasm-opt is optional/unpinned, and a DIFFERENT comparison still exits success. All 15 vendor hashes verify current bytes only. bv-huf5.4 is closed without a matching rebuild receipt.

## Behavior that must be established
Pin compiler/target, dependency lock, bindgen and optimizer version/options; distinguish optimized/nonoptimized output as different pipelines. Make graph glue and WASM one provenance unit with source tree hash and build environment. Rebuild in an isolated output directory; compare byte-for-byte or document unavoidable nondeterminism with a reviewed equivalence procedure, never merely bless a different hash. Update reviewed vendored artifacts and manifest together through the maintainer's normal change process. Gate source correspondence and fail mismatch. Include optional hybrid scorer provenance only when it is actually shipped; preserve JS fallback.

## Required unit/integration/E2E coverage
Two clean builds under the pinned pipeline, manifest/glue/WASM hash checks, wrong bindgen/compiler/optimizer, lock drift, one-byte tamper, missing target/tool and mismatched generated glue. Real graph-WASM parity fixtures verify algorithms, not just file presence. Retain both build receipts and hashes; no green source-correspondence claim if the toolchain cannot run.

## Test workmanship and closure
Extend existing test files and harnesses. Test public behavior with a deliberately broken case/old-code negative control; do not merely mirror the implementation or assert keys exist. Log fixture/seed, source revision, argv, relevant nonsecret environment, expected and observed IDs/state, stdout/stderr and exit code on failures. Preserve artifacts for diagnosis. Run focused tests plus existing affected-package suite; use race tests for shared state and real platform/browser execution only where this task requires it. Never count a skipped prerequisite or missing runner as passed. This proof task depends on bv-oonu.3; it can be designed beforehand but closes only after the real implementation and evidence succeed.
design: Ambition rounds: pinned compiler, target, bindgen and optimizer constitute a single pipeline, including whether optimization is enabled. Glue+WASM+manifest must correspond to one rebuild. Independent algorithmic parity supplements byte checks; it cannot silently replace failed provenance. Missing toolchain or unequal artifact yields explicit incomplete/fail. Two isolated positive builds and a deliberately mismatched pipeline are required.

title: [RC-V3 proof] Prove local and RCH environment-independent test execution
description:
## Independent proof target
Full local go test ./... passes 29 packages. RCH run fails TestLoadSprintsMissingFileIsOK, TestLoadIssues_NonExistentBeadsDir, TestGetBeadsDir_EmptyRepoPath_UsesCwd, TestError_NotGitRepository and TestWorkspaceAutoDiscoveryFromNestedDir because worker TMPDIR is inside the project. UI editor tests assume installed GUI tools; GraphView_GoldenASCII differs through ANSI output. Remote benchmark succeeds. This is concrete release verification portability failure, not evidence all those product features are broken.

## Behavior that must be established
Use explicit isolated discovery roots/ceilings in tests that claim no ancestor project, and test ancestor discovery separately. Make editor tests control lookup and argv through temporary executables; pin rendering capability for ASCII goldens. Avoid blanket skips, setting global product behavior to please tests, or disabling valuable discovery. Keep browser suppression and isolated config behavior. Extend current TestMain/helpers with narrowly scoped environment handling and explain the RCH invocation contract.

## Required unit/integration/E2E coverage
Run the named regressions with TMPDIR outside and beneath a repository, parent .beads and .bv configs, TERM/COLORTERM/NO_COLOR variations, no GUI editor and a controlled editor. Then local and RCH complete standard suites; log worker identity, temp-root relationship and relevant nonsecret env, never tokens. A deliberately broken discovery expectation must still fail.

## Test workmanship and closure
Extend existing test files and harnesses. Test public behavior with a deliberately broken case/old-code negative control; do not merely mirror the implementation or assert keys exist. Log fixture/seed, source revision, argv, relevant nonsecret environment, expected and observed IDs/state, stdout/stderr and exit code on failures. Preserve artifacts for diagnosis. Run focused tests plus existing affected-package suite; use race tests for shared state and real platform/browser execution only where this task requires it. Never count a skipped prerequisite or missing runner as passed. This proof task depends on bv-oonu.5; it can be designed beforehand but closes only after the real implementation and evidence succeed.
design: Ambition rounds: test-environment handling must be narrowly owned. Preserve genuine ancestor discovery tests and environment-sensitive integration coverage while isolating fixtures that claim an empty parent. Log only nonsecret environment needed for diagnosis. Do not blanket skip remote failures or weaken golden expectations.

title: [RC-V4] Prove dashboard offline and mobile journeys beyond bundle boot markers
description:
## Observed gap and background
Export/E2E tests pass and verify SQLite FTS5, files and references. scripts/dashboard_browser_smoke.sh checks console boot markers but does not interact, go offline/reload, or test mobile. CSP removes script unsafe-inline but retains unsafe-eval for Alpine; this is documented residual defense, not a demonstrated exploit. Graph WASM and optional hybrid WASM have distinct fallback behavior. No browser was opened during the 2026-09-04 audit.

## Required implementation
Extend the existing opt-in headless-browser harness to exercise search, filters, detail/comments, graph navigation, charts/Mermaid and copy controls at desktop and narrow/mobile viewport. Verify first load, offline subsequent reload, route persistence, service-worker update and JS fallback when optional hybrid WASM is absent. Preserve detailed failure artifacts and allow loopback-only network observation. Keep BV_NO_BROWSER/BV_TEST_MODE gates on product desktop launches. Record the remaining Alpine unsafe-eval policy clearly; a future CSP migration must pass the same journeys before removal. Never treat missing browser as a passing required proof stage.

## Verification and acceptance
Real exported bundle and browser, not DOM stubs. Require actual result IDs and visible state, no uncaught exceptions/CSP refusals, successful offline reload after priming, no external network reliance, no horizontal loss of key controls at narrow viewport. Negative controls break a local asset, disable cache priming and inject an unsafe display string; distinguish expected fallback from broken app. Retain console, network and screenshot/DOM evidence only in test artifacts.

## Delivery constraints
Work in existing implementation/test files where sensible. Do not delete files, rewrite unrelated work, create compatibility shims, or run browser-opening product actions. Build, vet, first-party formatting and relevant tests must pass after implementation. Retain concise failing-before/passing-after evidence with source revision, fixture identity, command, exit code and observed-versus-expected results. The companion test bead is required for completion of this gap.
design: Ambition rounds: proof requires real visible state and result IDs, offline reload after priming and changed-assets negative control, not boot logs alone. Test 360px mobile width and ordinary desktop with keyboard access. Keep browser opt-in and suppress OS browser launches. Do not claim unsafe-eval is already removed; the accepted residual is explicit. Optional hybrid scorer absence must retain JS functionality, unlike missing required SQL/WASM assets which must fail the journey.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Actual dashboard search/detail/graph/charts/Mermaid controls work on desktop and 360px viewport.
- [x] Primed offline reload and service-worker update preserve valid application state.
- [x] Missing required asset fails, optional hybrid WASM absence falls back, and console/network evidence is retained.
- [x] A focused regression fails before this change and passes afterward; affected build/vet/format/tests pass.
close_reason: Independent root review: frozen V4 source matches; real desktop/360px stopped-origin offline/update browser journeys and negative controls pass; full export and affected E2E plus build/vet/format pass. Exact evidence and bounded inventory in comment.

title: [RC-V4 proof] Prove browser search, graph, offline reload and mobile journeys
description:
## Independent proof target
Export/E2E tests pass and verify SQLite FTS5, files and references. scripts/dashboard_browser_smoke.sh checks console boot markers but does not interact, go offline/reload, or test mobile. CSP removes script unsafe-inline but retains unsafe-eval for Alpine; this is documented residual defense, not a demonstrated exploit. Graph WASM and optional hybrid WASM have distinct fallback behavior. No browser was opened during the 2026-09-04 audit.

## Behavior that must be established
Extend the existing opt-in headless-browser harness to exercise search, filters, detail/comments, graph navigation, charts/Mermaid and copy controls at desktop and narrow/mobile viewport. Verify first load, offline subsequent reload, route persistence, service-worker update and JS fallback when optional hybrid WASM is absent. Preserve detailed failure artifacts and allow loopback-only network observation. Keep BV_NO_BROWSER/BV_TEST_MODE gates on product desktop launches. Record the remaining Alpine unsafe-eval policy clearly; a future CSP migration must pass the same journeys before removal. Never treat missing browser as a passing required proof stage.

## Required unit/integration/E2E coverage
Real exported bundle and browser, not DOM stubs. Require actual result IDs and visible state, no uncaught exceptions/CSP refusals, successful offline reload after priming, no external network reliance, no horizontal loss of key controls at narrow viewport. Negative controls break a local asset, disable cache priming and inject an unsafe display string; distinguish expected fallback from broken app. Retain console, network and screenshot/DOM evidence only in test artifacts.

## Test workmanship and closure
Extend existing test files and harnesses. Test public behavior with a deliberately broken case/old-code negative control; do not merely mirror the implementation or assert keys exist. Log fixture/seed, source revision, argv, relevant nonsecret environment, expected and observed IDs/state, stdout/stderr and exit code on failures. Preserve artifacts for diagnosis. Run focused tests plus existing affected-package suite; use race tests for shared state and real platform/browser execution only where this task requires it. Never count a skipped prerequisite or missing runner as passed. This proof task depends on bv-oonu.7; it can be designed beforehand but closes only after the real implementation and evidence succeed.
design: Ambition rounds: proof requires real visible state and result IDs, offline reload after priming and changed-assets negative control, not boot logs alone. Test 360px mobile width and ordinary desktop with keyboard access. Keep browser opt-in and suppress OS browser launches. Do not claim unsafe-eval is already removed; the accepted residual is explicit. Optional hybrid scorer absence must retain JS functionality, unlike missing required SQL/WASM assets which must fail the journey.

- [x] Independently verify: Actual dashboard search/detail/graph/charts/Mermaid controls work on desktop and 360px viewport.

- [x] Capture positive and negative control evidence with source revision, fixture, argv, expected/observed values and failure artifacts.
- [x] Required real-service/platform/browser runs are completed where specified; no skipped prerequisite is marked passed.
close_reason: Original independent browser acceptance completed with real Chromium 152, exact frozen source, visible desktop/360px state, server-stopped offline reload, updates/fallback and failing old/required/unprimed controls. No physical-phone or browser-FTS5 claim.

title: [RC-V5] Verify native installation and update on every advertised distribution path
description:
## Observed gap and background
v0.23.0 publishes darwin amd64/arm64, linux amd64/arm64, windows amd64 archives. Verified Linux amd64 archive runs. docs/RELEASING.md admits PowerShell installer tests ran on Linux, not Windows. README recommends Homebrew/Scoop, while GoReleaser sets skip_upload:true for both; actual storefront currency was not established. Recent Windows SQLite URI fix is unit-tested but no native execution evidence was gathered.

## Required implementation
Extend existing release verification with native OS/architecture receipts for install, version, robot-capabilities, a tiny real Beads project, update/no-update, and Windows drive/space paths. Resolve Homebrew/Scoop manifests read-only against the intended released archive/digest and document the actual publishing step. No package-store or release publication is authorized by this task. Use isolated install directories; missing native runners are explicit proof gaps rather than Linux simulation passes. Test supported Nix build/version as part of this distribution inventory.

## Verification and acceptance
Real native Windows and macOS plus Linux release artifacts; checksums and embedded revision match; corrupted archive/checksum and wrong-version binary fail closed; existing install survives failed update; no desktop browser; unsupported OS/arch errors are actionable. Save OS/arch/toolchain/artifact hashes and command results. A mocked HTTP server may cover failure branches, but cannot substitute for native positive proof.

## Delivery constraints
Work in existing implementation/test files where sensible. Do not delete files, rewrite unrelated work, create compatibility shims, or run browser-opening product actions. Build, vet, first-party formatting and relevant tests must pass after implementation. Retain concise failing-before/passing-after evidence with source revision, fixture identity, command, exit code and observed-versus-expected results. The companion test bead is required for completion of this gap.
design: Ambition rounds: prove the new user's actual package-store version as well as archive availability. Build-info revision, package checksum and native capabilities must agree. Linux PowerShell simulation covers failure logic only; it cannot close native Windows proof. No CI enablement, external publication, or replacement of the maintainer's installation is implied.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each advertised OS/architecture has native install, capabilities and update evidence tied to an artifact digest.
- [x] Windows drive/space paths and failed-update preservation pass natively.
- [x] Homebrew/Scoop manifests and supported Nix build identify the intended version; missing runners remain unproven.
- [ ] A focused regression fails before this change and passes afterward; affected build/vet/format/tests pass.

title: Unit test: dependency_suggest.go - Dependency fix suggestions
description:
Create comprehensive unit tests for pkg/analysis/dependency_suggest.go

## File Overview
dependency_suggest.go analyzes the dependency graph and suggests:
- Missing dependencies based on content similarity
- Redundant/transitive dependencies to remove
- Incorrect dependency directions

## Test Cases to Implement
1. **Missing Dependency Detection**
   - Two issues with similar titles/content, no dep link
   - Issue A mentions issue B's ID in description
   - Parent/child relationships without explicit deps
   - Epic with tasks but no deps defined

2. **Redundant Dependency Detection**
   - Transitive dependency (A->B->C, A->C is redundant)
   - Self-loops if not caught elsewhere
   - Duplicate dependency entries

3. **Direction Suggestions**
   - Low-priority depending on high-priority (unusual)
   - Closed issue depending on open issue
   - Epic depending on task (should be reversed)

4. **Confidence Scoring**
   - High confidence for explicit ID mentions
   - Medium confidence for title similarity
   - Low confidence for weak signals
   - Verify scores in 0.0-1.0 range

5. **Edge Cases**
   - Empty graph
   - Single issue (no suggestions possible)
   - Fully connected graph
   - Graph with cycles

## Implementation Notes
- Create test graphs with known expected suggestions
- Use golden files for complex scenarios
- Test with real-world-like issue content

title: History View Session Timeline Integration
description:
# History View Session Timeline Integration

## Purpose
Integrate cass sessions into the History view timeline, showing sessions alongside commits in chronological order. This provides the richest context for understanding how work was done.

## ⚠️ COORDINATION NOTE
This bead should be implemented **after or in coordination with** the History View Overhaul epic (bv-1d4i). The History view is being redesigned, and implementing session integration before that is complete would require rework.

**Recommended approach:** 
1. Complete History view overhaul (bv-1d4i) first
2. Then add session integration to the new architecture
3. OR coordinate closely if implementing in parallel

## Background

### Why History View?
The History view is specifically designed for retrospective analysis—understanding "what happened" for a bead. Coding sessions are a crucial part of that story:

- Commits show WHAT changed
- Sessions show HOW/WHY it was changed

Combining both in a timeline tells the complete story.

### Current History View Structure
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ bv-abc123: Fix token refresh timeout                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Timeline                                                    │
│                                                             │
│ Dec 17, 3:45pm  📝 e1f2a3b "Fix retry logic"              │
│ Dec 17, 2:00pm  📝 9d8c7b6 "Add timeout handling"         │
│ Dec 16, 5:00pm  📝 a1b2c3d "Initial auth implementation"  │
│                                                             │
│ Dec 15, 10:00am ✨ Created                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### With Session Integration
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ bv-abc123: Fix token refresh timeout                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Timeline                                                    │
│                                                             │
│ Dec 17, 5:30pm  ✓ Closed                                   │
│ Dec 17, 3:45pm  📝 e1f2a3b "Fix retry logic"              │
│ Dec 17, 3:00pm  📎 Claude Code session (42 messages)       │  ← NEW
│ Dec 17, 2:00pm  📝 9d8c7b6 "Add timeout handling"         │
│ Dec 17, 1:30pm  📎 Cursor session (18 messages)            │  ← NEW
│ Dec 16, 5:00pm  📝 a1b2c3d "Initial auth implementation"  │
│                                                             │
│ Dec 15, 10:00am ✨ Created                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Implementation

### Timeline Entry Types
```go
type TimelineEntryType int
const (
    EntryCommit TimelineEntryType = iota
    EntrySession  // NEW
    EntryCreated
    EntryClosed
    EntryMilestone
)

type TimelineEntry struct {
    Type      TimelineEntryType
    Timestamp time.Time
    // For commits:
    CommitHash string
    CommitMsg  string
    // For sessions:
    SessionPath string
    Agent       string
    MessageCount int
}
```

### Correlation Strategy for History View
Unlike the main list view (which correlates on selection), History view should:
1. Correlate **only the selected bead** (not all visible)
2. Use cached results if available
3. Trigger background fetch if not cached
4. Display commits immediately, add sessions when ready

This avoids the performance problem of batch-correlating many beads.

### Merging Timelines
```go
func mergeTimelines(commits []TimelineEntry, sessions []TimelineEntry) []TimelineEntry {
    // Combine and sort by timestamp descending
    // Handle timestamp ties: commits before sessions at same timestamp
    // This reflects that commits are the "result" of session work
}
```

### Session Entry Rendering
```go
func renderSessionEntry(entry TimelineEntry, theme Theme) string {
    // Dec 17, 3:00pm  📎 Claude Code session (42 messages)
    timestamp := entry.Timestamp.Format("Jan 2, 3:04pm")
    return fmt.Sprintf("%s  📎 %s session (%d messages)",
        timestamp, entry.Agent, entry.MessageCount)
}
```

### Selecting a Session Entry
When user navigates to and selects a session entry:
- Show expanded preview inline (2-3 key snippets)
- Or: Show message "Press C for full session preview"
- Consistent with main list view modal behavior

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sessions appear in timeline with correct timestamps
- [ ] Sessions sorted correctly with commits (commits first on ties)
- [ ] Session entries show agent and message count
- [ ] Can navigate to session entries with j/k
- [ ] Selecting session shows preview or hint
- [ ] Timeline loads immediately (sessions added async)
- [ ] Timeline still works perfectly when cass unavailable

## Graceful Degradation
If cass unavailable or returns empty:
- Timeline shows commits only (existing behavior)
- No "no sessions" message
- No visual indication of missing feature
- No loading spinners

## Performance Considerations
- Correlate only selected bead (not batch)
- Use cached results aggressively
- Limit session search to bead activity window (+/- 7 days)
- Sessions appear async (don't block commit display)

## Testing Strategy
- Test timeline merging algorithm
- Test various timestamp orderings
- Test tie-breaking (commits before sessions)
- Test empty session lists
- Test navigation behavior
- Test async loading (sessions appear after commits)
- Visual regression test
close_reason: Session timeline integration complete: Sessions appear in timeline with timestamps, sorted correctly with commits, entries show agent/message count, navigation works, async loading implemented, graceful degradation when cass unavailable. All tests pass.

title: Fix follow-up issues from recent robot/correlation changes
description:
Fresh-eyes review found a few follow-ups:

1) Correlation incremental path (`pkg/correlation/incremental.go`) still uses `--format=%H|...` but now feeds output into `Extractor.parseGitLogOutput`, which expects NUL-delimited headers. This silently breaks incremental history updates.

2) `Extractor.parseGitLogOutput` scanner max token is 1MB while streaming path uses 10MB; align to 10MB to match loader and avoid truncation on large diffs.

3) `--robot-triage` `usage_hints` in `cmd/bv/main.go` reference stale jq paths (e.g. `.triage.blockers`, `.triage.quick_ref.next_up`). Update hints to match current JSON schema.

4) Minor clarity: update outdated comment for `Recommendation.Action` in `pkg/analysis/triage.go` (now a human-readable action hint).

Acceptance:
- Incremental correlation extraction works again (format matches parser)
- `--robot-triage` hints are accurate for current schema
- gofmt + `go test ./...` pass
notes:
Fixed follow-ups from fresh-eyes review:
- Correlation incremental extraction now uses NUL-delimited git log headers to match `Extractor.parseGitLogOutput`.
- `Extractor.parseGitLogOutput` scanner max token size bumped to 10MB (match loader/stream).
- `--robot-triage` usage_hints updated to match actual JSON schema.
- Updated outdated comment for `Recommendation.Action` (human-readable action hint).

title: Robot status output shows pending/empty states
description:
Problem:
- `bv --robot-plan` and `bv --robot-priority` emit `.status` with `state: pending` for all metrics and empty states for `KCore/Articulation/Slack`.
- This breaks the robot JSON contract and makes agents think metrics are still running even though bv exits immediately.

Repro:
- `bv --robot-plan | jq .status`
- `bv --robot-priority | jq .status`

Expected:
- Status should be deterministic and reflect what was actually computed for the command (`computed`/`approx`/`timeout`/`skipped`), with no `pending`/empty states.

Acceptance:
- `--robot-plan` and `--robot-priority` status fields never contain `pending`/empty states at process exit.
- If metrics are intentionally not computed for a fast path, they are marked `skipped` with a reason.
notes:
Implemented fix: `--robot-plan` and `--robot-priority` now wait for analysis completion before emitting `.status`, eliminating `pending`/empty states.

- `--robot-plan` skips expensive centrality metrics by default and marks them `skipped` with reason `not computed for --robot-plan`; still computes fast structural signals (k-core/articulation/slack) for a complete status contract.
- Tests updated to enforce no `pending`/empty states in robot outputs.

title: Perf: speed up startup by removing redundant work (no output changes)
description:
## Goal
Make bv measurably faster and more scalable at startup by removing *waste* (redundant computation, dead work, avoidable O(V·E) passes), **without changing any results/output**.

This is specifically about:
- TUI startup responsiveness (Model construction, Phase 1 readiness)
- Robot-mode command latency for analysis-heavy outputs
- CPU + allocation efficiency when graphs get large (hundreds/thousands of issues)

## Context / Why this matters
bv is intentionally a “graph sidecar” for Beads. As projects grow, the analysis pipeline becomes the dominant cost, and the *worst* kind of cost is redundant work that produces identical results.

We already observed several clear cases of:
- computing values and discarding them
- computing the same derived data multiple times from the same inputs
- per-node work that can be replaced with a linear pass

These are “free wins”: they improve speed and reduce CPU without changing behavior.

## Non-goals
- Do **not** change metric definitions, scoring weights, or recommendation ordering.
- Do **not** skip metrics or change what gets computed (unless explicitly gated behind an opt-in flag AND the default remains identical).
- Do **not** change the shape of robot JSON outputs.
- Do **not** change UI behavior/interaction.

## Out of scope (explicitly)
- Any product/UX changes.
- The export wizard / huh dependency decisions.

## Success criteria (high-level)
- `go test ./...` passes.
- Output invariants hold on fixtures: triage recommendations/unblocks/velocity remain identical.
- Measurable reduction in startup CPU/allocations on a “large graph” fixture.
design:
## Candidate improvements (no output change)
1) Remove dead work in triage:
   - `pkg/analysis/triage.go` calls `analyzer.GetExecutionPlan()` and discards it.

2) Remove unused precompute in impact scoring:
   - `pkg/analysis/priority.go` builds/sorts a dependents map that is never used.

3) Avoid computing full triage just to extract velocity:
   - `cmd/bv/main.go` uses `analysis.ComputeTriage()` inside `--robot-insights` only to read `ProjectHealth.Velocity`.

4) Reduce asymptotic cost of “unblocks map” construction:
   - current triage builds unblocks by calling a per-node graph traversal.
   - can compute equivalently in ~O(E) by counting open blockers + grouping dependents.

5) Eliminate duplicated analyzer/stats construction in the TUI:
   - `pkg/ui/model.go` builds analyzer+stats, then calls `analysis.ComputeTriage()` which builds another analyzer+stats.

## Risks / tricky bits
- Must preserve dependency semantics:
  - only blocking deps matter (`dep.Type.IsBlocking()`)
  - missing blockers must not block (graceful degradation)
  - duplicated deps in JSONL must not double-count (graph edges are unique)
- Determinism: stable ordering of IDs in outputs.
- Avoid introducing time-based flaky tests; focus on functional invariants.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No robot JSON output shape changes (field names/types).
- [ ] Existing unit tests remain green; new invariance tests added where appropriate.
- [ ] Documented benchmark protocol to measure improvements.
- [ ] Demonstrated CPU/allocation reduction on at least one large synthetic fixture.
close_reason: All core P1 performance optimizations complete: O(E) unblocks, TUI reuses analyzer/stats, velocity helper, dead code removed, invariance tests added. Remaining items are P2 docs and P3 optional optimizations.

## Goal

## Why

## Scope
- Define benchmark commands/datasets for:
  - TUI startup (Phase 1 ready + Phase 2 completion)
  - `bv --robot-triage`, `bv --robot-plan`, `bv --robot-insights`

  - unblocks map correctness
  - velocity computation
  - (optional) triage recommendation stability on a small fixture

## Principles
- No flaky time assertions.
- Prefer fixed clocks (`now`) + deterministic fixtures.
- Prefer “fast vs slow reference” equivalence tests for algorithmic changes.

- Preserve semantics (including graceful degradation when Phase 2 isn’t ready).

title: Perf: compute triage unblocks map in O(E) (no per-node traversal)
description:
## Problem
Triage currently builds an “unblocks map” by calling `analyzer.computeUnblocks(issueID)` for every open issue.

This can devolve to O(V·E) and becomes expensive on large graphs.

## Goal
Compute the same unblocks map in ~O(E):
- Precompute each issue’s count of open blockers (only existing blocking deps).
- Build blocker -> dependents adjacency lists.
- Dependent is unblocked by closing blocker B iff openBlockerCount[dependent] == 1 and B is that blocker.

## Correctness requirements
- Only blocking deps count (`dep.Type.IsBlocking()`).
- Missing blockers do not block.
- Duplicate deps must not double-count.
- Unblocks lists must be deterministically sorted.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] O(E) implementation matches reference algorithm on fixtures.
- [ ] No triage output changes.
- [ ] `go test ./...` passes.

title: Insights: Enhanced Heatmap Visualization
description:
## Overview
Dramatically improve the heatmap visualization in Insights view using advanced lipgloss features.

## Current State
```
📊 Priority Heatmap  Score vs Depth (H=toggle view)
      │  0-.2  .2-.4  .4-.6  .6-.8  .8-1
──────┼────────────────────────────────
  D=0 │    ·     █2    ██5    █3     ·
 D1-2 │    ·      ·    ██8   ███12   █4
 D3-5 │    ·      ·     █3    ██7    █2
D6-10 │    ·      ·      ·     █2     ·
 D10+ │    ·      ·      ·      ·     ·

Legend: · empty █ few ██ some ███ many/urgent
```

Problems:
- ASCII table borders
- Cluttered cell content (█2)
- No background colors
- No interactivity
- Cramped legend

## Enhanced Design

### Visual Improvements

#### 1. Solid Background Cells
Use `lipgloss.Background()` for true heatmap cells:
```go
cellStyle := t.Renderer.NewStyle().
    Background(heatColor).
    Foreground(contrastColor).  // White or black for readability
    Padding(0, 1).
    Align(lipgloss.Center)
```

#### 2. Color Gradient
Implement proper heat gradient (cool → hot):
```
0 items:    #1a1a2e (dark blue/gray)
1-2 items:  #16213e (navy)
3-5 items:  #0f4c75 (blue)
6-10 items: #e94560 (coral)
10+ items:  #ff2e63 (hot pink/red)
```

Or use existing theme colors intelligently:
```go
func GetHeatGradient(intensity float64, t Theme) lipgloss.Color {
    // Interpolate between t.Secondary (cold) and t.Primary (hot)
}
```

#### 3. Clean Cell Content
Show EITHER:
- Just the count number (with background color indicating intensity)
- Just a solid block (for minimal look)

Recommended: Number with colored background
```
┌─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐
│     │  2  │  5  │  3  │     │  <- Numbers only, background = heat
├─────┼─────┼─────┼─────┼─────┤
│     │     │  8  │ 12  │  4  │
└─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘
```

#### 4. Proper Axis Labels

```
        ┌─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┬─────┐

 ───    ├─────┼─────┼─────┼─────┼─────┤

 ↓      ├─────┼─────┼─────┼─────┼─────┤
 Root   │     │     │  3  │  7  │  2  │
        └─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┴─────┘
```

#### 5. Marginal Totals
Show row/column sums:
```
        0-.2  .2-.4  .4-.6  .6-.8  .8-1  │ Total
  D=0     -      2      5      3     -   │  10
 D1-2     -      -      8     12     4   │  24
 D3-5     -      -      3      7     2   │  12
D6-10     -      -      -      2     -   │   2
 D10+     -      -      -      -     -   │   0
────────────────────────────────────────┼─────
Total     0      2     16     24     6   │  48
```

### Interactivity Improvements

#### Cell Selection
- j/k: Move selection between rows
- h/l: Move selection between columns
- Enter: Drill down into selected cell (show issues in that bucket)

#### Drill-Down View
When pressing Enter on a cell:
```
┌─ Issues in Score .6-.8, Depth 1-2 (12 items) ────────────┐
│                                                          │
│ bv-123  P1  Fix auth timeout                             │
│ bv-456  P1  API rate limiting                            │

│ ...                                                      │
│                                                          │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Layout Improvements

- Calculate cell width based on available space
- Minimum cell width: 5 chars
- Expand cells on wide terminals

Vertical legend on the side or expanded horizontal:
```
Heat Scale:
  ░░░  0     (empty)
  ▒▒▒  1-2   (few)
  ▓▓▓  3-5   (some)
  ███  6-10  (many)
```

## Implementation

title: Board: Smart Empty Column Handling
description:
## Overview
Empty columns should not waste horizontal space.

## Current Behavior
Empty columns take the same width as columns with items.
```
OPEN(15)     PROGRESS(8)  BLOCKED(0)   CLOSED(50)
████████     ████████     (empty)      ████████
████████     ████████                  ████████
```
The empty BLOCKED column wastes ~25% of width.

## Solution: Two Modes (Simple)

### Mode 1: Show All (Default for Status swimlane)
Keep all columns visible, even if empty. Users expect to see the full workflow.
Empty columns show as minimal-width placeholders.

### Mode 2: Hide Empty (Default for other swimlanes)
For Priority/Type groupings, hide columns with no items.
```
P0(3)          P1(8)           P2(12)
████████████   ████████████    ████████████
```
(P3 and P4 columns hidden because they have no items)

## Implementation

### Automatic Behavior
- **Status swimlane**: Always show all 4 columns (even if empty)
- **Priority swimlane**: Hide empty priority columns
- **Type swimlane**: Hide empty type columns

### Manual Toggle
`e`: Toggle empty column visibility (override auto behavior)

### Visual Indicator
When columns are hidden:
```
BOARD [by: Priority] [+2 hidden]
```

### Navigation
When navigating with `h/l`:
- If empty columns are hidden, skip them
- If empty columns are shown (minimal), allow navigating into them

## Removed from Scope
- ~~Three modes (collapse/minimize/show)~~ - Too complex. Two modes is sufficient.
- ~~Auto-expand on content~~ - Confusing behavior. Keep it simple.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Status view always shows all 4 columns
- [ ] Priority/Type views hide empty columns by default
- [ ] `e` toggles empty column visibility
- [ ] Hidden column count shown in header
- [ ] Navigation skips hidden columns
close_reason: Implemented smart empty column handling: Status mode shows all columns, Priority/Type hide empty. 'e' key toggles visibility. Title bar shows swimlane mode and hidden count. Commit b827f64.

title: e2e: graph export determinism test compared unpinned generated_at timestamps
description: TestGraphExport_DeterministicOutput ran --robot-graph twice and compared stdout byte-for-byte without SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, so the payload's second-granular generated_at made it flake whenever the runs straddled a second boundary (observed once under host load on 2026-09-02). Fix: pin SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1700000000 for both runs and assert the pinned timestamp, so the test exercises the documented reproducibility contract.

title: History: Git-Centric View Mode
description:
# History: Git-Centric View Mode

## Problem Statement
Currently the History view is bead-centric only: you select a bead and see its commits. But users often want the inverse: browse commits chronologically and see which beads each commit relates to.

The data already supports this - \`HistoryReport.CommitIndex\` maps SHA → []BeadID - but the UI doesn't expose it.

## User Stories
1. "I want to see recent commits and understand what work they represent"
2. "A commit looks suspicious, which issues does it relate to?"
3. "What has the team been working on (git activity perspective)?"

## Design

### View Mode Toggle
Press \`v\` to toggle between:
- **Bead Mode** (current): Left=Beads, Right=Commits for selected bead
- **Git Mode** (new): Left=Commits, Right=Beads for selected commit

### Git Mode Layout
\`\`\`
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ HISTORY VIEW [Git Mode]                          47 beads • 156 commits │
├─────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ COMMITS                     │ RELATED BEADS                            │
│ ─────────────────           │ ─────────────────                        │
│ ▸ a1b2c3d Fix auth bug      │ ● bv-123 [P1] Auth refactor (95%)       │
│   Alice • 2h ago            │   in_progress • 5 commits total          │
│   3 files changed           │                                          │
│                             │ ✓ bv-456 [P2] Add session tests (78%)   │
│   b2c3d4e Add session mgmt  │   closed • 3 commits total               │
│   Alice • 5h ago            │                                          │
│   7 files changed           │                                          │
│                             │                                          │
│   c3d4e5f Refactor handlers │ ────────────────────────────────────────│
│   Bob • 1d ago              │ COMMIT DETAILS                           │
│   12 files changed          │ ─────────────────                        │
│                             │ SHA: a1b2c3d4e5f67890abcdef...           │
│   d4e5f6g Update docs       │ Author: Alice <alice@example.com>        │
│   Carol • 2d ago            │ Date: 2025-01-15 14:30:45                │
│   2 files changed           │                                          │
│                             │ Message:                                 │
│                             │ Fix auth bug causing session timeout     │
│                             │                                          │
│                             │ Files:                                   │
│                             │  M src/auth.go         +45 -12          │
│                             │  M src/auth_test.go    +89 -0           │
│                             │  A src/session.go      +120 -0          │
├─────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ j/k:commits  Tab:pane  v:bead-mode  y:copy-sha  Enter:jump  esc:close  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

### Implementation

#### New Data Structure
\`\`\`go
type CommitListEntry struct {
    SHA         string
    ShortSHA    string
    Message     string
    Author      string
    Timestamp   time.Time
    FileCount   int
    BeadIDs     []string  // From CommitIndex
    BeadCount   int
}

type HistoryModel struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    viewMode      historyViewMode // beadMode or gitMode
    commitList    []CommitListEntry
    selectedCommit int
}
\`\`\`

#### Building Commit List
On mode switch to Git mode, build commit list from all correlated commits:
\`\`\`go
func (h *HistoryModel) buildCommitList() {
    seen := make(map[string]bool)
    for _, hist := range h.report.Histories {
        for _, commit := range hist.Commits {
            if !seen[commit.SHA] {
                h.commitList = append(h.commitList, CommitListEntry{
                    SHA: commit.SHA,
                    // ... fill from commit ...
                    BeadIDs: h.report.CommitIndex[commit.SHA],
                })
                seen[commit.SHA] = true
            }
        }
    }
    // Sort by timestamp descending (most recent first)
    sort.Slice(h.commitList, ...)
}
\`\`\`

### Keyboard Changes
- \`v\` - Toggle view mode (new)
- In Git mode:
  - j/k navigates commits (was beads)
  - J/K navigates related beads (new)
  - Enter jumps to selected bead in main list

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] \`v\` key toggles between Bead and Git modes
- [ ] Git mode shows commits sorted by recency
- [ ] Selected commit shows related beads with confidence
- [ ] Commit details panel shows files changed
- [ ] Enter on a bead jumps to it in main list
- [ ] y copies selected commit SHA
- [ ] Mode persists during session (resets on close)

## Visual Polish
- Mode indicator in header: [Git Mode] vs [Bead Mode]
- Smooth transition between modes (no jarring rerender)
- Consistent styling with existing views
close_reason: Added Git-centric view mode with v toggle, commits on left, related beads on right

title: Make the feedback loops real: triage and correlation feedback change results
description:
## Why this epic exists
The README sells two learning loops: `--feedback-accept/ignore` "learns from your accept/ignore decisions to tune recommendation weights", and `--robot-confirm/reject-correlation` "improves correlation accuracy over time". Both are write-only today. `pkg/analysis/feedback.go` computes `GetEffectiveWeights()` but nothing outside the file calls it; `priority.go:162-169` multiplies the package constants. Five accepts and five ignores on a fixture changed the reported adjustments and left every triage score identical to 1e-11. `pkg/correlation/feedback.go` stores confirm/reject, but `Correlator.assembleReport` never reads the store; a confirmed pair keeps confidence 0.99 and a rejected pair stays in the history.

Shipping state that is written but never read is worse than not having the feature: users spend effort training a system that cannot learn. This epic makes both loops real, with tests that prove the effect, or removes the flags and README sections if the user decides against them.

## Vision goals served
Rows 26, 27 (README "Feedback System (Adaptive Recommendations)", "Correlation Feedback System").

## Done when
Child tasks closed; `tests/e2e/feedback_effect_test.go` and the correlation feedback e2e both demonstrate a changed output after feedback and a byte-identical output after reset.
close_reason: All child beads closed and verified (see their close reasons).

title: Priority scoring takes a Weights value (defaults from the constants) instead of reading constants inline
description:
## Context
Composite priority scoring in `pkg/analysis/priority.go` multiplies eight package-level constants (`WeightPageRank` 0.22, `WeightBetweenness` 0.20, `WeightBlockerRatio` 0.13, `WeightStaleness` 0.05, `WeightPriorityBoost` 0.10, `WeightTimeToImpact` 0.10, `WeightUrgency` 0.10, `WeightRisk` 0.10; lines 55-62) directly in the scoring loop (162-169). `pkg/analysis/feedback.go` computes `GetEffectiveWeights()` (314-346) as a `map[string]float64` normalized to sum 1.0, but nothing consumes it. To let feedback (bead C2) and, later, per-project configuration influence scoring, the weights must be a value the analyzer is given.

## Target state
```go
type Weights struct{ PageRank, Betweenness, BlockerRatio, Staleness, PriorityBoost, TimeToImpact, Urgency, Risk float64 }
func DefaultWeights() Weights            // from the constants
func (w Weights) Normalized() Weights    // sum to 1.0, guard zero
func (f *FeedbackData) Weights() Weights // effective weights as the struct
```
`Analyzer` gains `WithWeights(Weights)` (or an options struct already used by `ComputeTriageWithOptionsAndTime`); the scoring loop reads `a.weights`. `ScoreBreakdown` gains `weights_used` so payloads show what was applied.

## Success criteria
- `TestDefaultWeights_MatchConstantsAndSumToOne`.
- `TestScoreBreakdown_UsesProvidedWeights`: two weight sets produce different `Score` for the same issue; default weights reproduce today's numbers exactly (golden on `synthetic_complex.jsonl`).
- No behaviour change for callers that do not pass weights (existing priority/triage tests unchanged).
close_reason: Implemented and verified: unit tests in pkg/analysis/weights_test.go and e2e tests tests/e2e/feedback_effect_test.go, tests/e2e/datasource_sidecar_test.go pass (go test, self-verified by re-execution)

title: Wire feedback effective weights into triage, next, priority, and TUI hints; report them in the payload
description:
## Context
`--feedback-accept <id>` / `--feedback-ignore <id>` / `--feedback-show` / `--feedback-reset` (cmd/bv/main.go:2391-2513) maintain `.beads/feedback.json` through `pkg/analysis/feedback.go` (`RecordFeedback`, `Save`, `Reset`, `Summary`). `--robot-triage` loads the file only to attach an informational block (robot_registry.go:1939-1944). Experiment on 2026-09-01: five accepts of one fixture issue and five ignores of another moved the reported adjustments (BlockerRatio 1.10, PageRank 1.046) while every triage score stayed identical to 1e-11. README "Feedback System (Adaptive Recommendations)" says the system "learns from your accept/ignore decisions to tune recommendation weights".

## Target state
When `.beads/feedback.json` exists and has at least `MinFeedbackSamples` (existing constant, verify value) entries, triage and priority recommendations are computed with `feedback.Weights()` (bead C1). The triage payload gains `feedback: {applied: bool, sample_size: n, effective_weights: {...}, adjustments: {...}}`. `--feedback-reset` restores defaults and the payload shows `applied: false`. The TUI priority hints (`p`) use the same weights (they call the same analyzer).

## Implementation
1. robot_registry.go triage/next/priority handlers: after `LoadFeedback`, pass `fb.Weights()` via the analyzer options.
2. `pkg/ui/model.go` analysis construction: load feedback once at startup and on file change.
3. Payload block; schema regeneration.
4. README: docs epic rewrites the section using the real 8-factor model.

## Success criteria

title: Session-Bead Correlation Engine
description:
# Session-Bead Correlation Engine

## Purpose
The "brain" of the integration—intelligently match cass sessions to beads using multiple strategies. This determines which sessions are relevant to which issues.

## Background

### The Correlation Challenge
Sessions and beads are created independently:
- Users do not explicitly tag sessions with bead IDs
- Session titles may not match bead titles exactly
- Timestamps may not align perfectly
- Same session might relate to multiple beads

We need smart heuristics to find meaningful connections.

### Correlation Quality Matters
False positives (irrelevant sessions shown) erode trust. False negatives (missing relevant sessions) reduce value. We optimize for **precision over recall**—better to show fewer, highly relevant sessions than many questionable ones.

## Correlation Strategies

### Strategy 1: ID Mention (Highest Confidence)
Search for the bead ID literally in sessions:
```go
query := fmt.Sprintf("%q", bead.ID) // e.g., "bv-abc123"
```
**Score bonus**: +100 (definitive match)
**When useful**: When users or agents explicitly mention issue IDs

### Strategy 2: Keyword Extraction (Medium Confidence)
Extract meaningful words from bead title, search with time filter:
```go
keywords := extractKeywords(bead.Title)
// "Fix token refresh timeout" → ["token", "refresh", "timeout"]
query := strings.Join(keywords[:3], " ")
```
**Score bonus**: +30 to +60 (depends on match quality)
**When useful**: Most common case—thematic matching

### Strategy 3: Timestamp Proximity (Lower Confidence)
Sessions occurring near bead activity (creation, updates, closure):
```go
days := daysBetween(bead.CreatedAt, bead.ClosedAt)
if days == 0 { days = 1 }
opts.Days = days + 1 // Search window
```
**Score bonus**: +10 to +30 (time proximity weighting)
**When useful**: Closed beads where work was recent

### Strategy 4: Combined Scoring
Blend strategies for final ranking:
```go
finalScore := baseScore * (1 + timeDecay) * workspaceBoost
// timeDecay: Recent sessions score higher
// workspaceBoost: Same workspace scores 2x
```

## Implementation

### Correlation Hint Type
```go
type CorrelationHint struct {
    BeadID       string          // Which bead this is for
    SessionCount int             // Total matching sessions
    TopSessions  []SearchResult  // Up to 3 best matches
    TopScore     float64         // Highest session score
    Reason       string          // "id_mention", "keywords", "timestamp"
    Keywords     []string        // Keywords used (for display)
}
```

### Correlation Flow
```
For each bead:
1. Check cache first (return if fresh hit)
2. Try ID mention search
   └─ Found → return with high confidence
3. Extract keywords from title
4. Search keywords with time filter
5. Filter by workspace (if available)
6. Score and rank results
7. Cache and return top matches
```

### Keyword Extraction
```go
func extractKeywords(title string) []string {
    // Remove common words: "the", "a", "and", "fix", "add", "update", etc.
    // Remove short words (< 3 chars)
    // Lowercase and dedupe
    // Return up to 5 keywords
}

var stopWords = map[string]bool{
    "the": true, "a": true, "an": true, "and": true, "or": true,
    "fix": true, "add": true, "update": true, "remove": true,
    "implement": true, "create": true, "delete": true,
    "for": true, "to": true, "in": true, "on": true, "at": true,
    "bug": true, "issue": true, "feature": true, "task": true,
}
```

### Workspace Filtering
Critical for relevance—sessions from unrelated projects pollute results:
```go
func workspaceFromBeadsPath(beadsPath string) string {
    // /path/to/project/.beads/beads.jsonl → /path/to/project
    return filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(beadsPath))
}
```

## Scoring Configuration

### ⚠️ TUNABILITY NOTE
All scoring weights should be **exported constants** that can be adjusted based on real-world usage. Initial values are educated guesses; expect to tune after deployment.

```go
// pkg/cass/scoring.go - All values are tunable
const (
    // Base scores by match type
    ScoreIDMention      = 100  // Definitive evidence
    ScoreExactKeyword   = 50   // Strong thematic link  
    ScorePartialKeyword = 30   // Probable relation
    
    // Multipliers
    MultiplierSameWorkspace = 2.0  // Critical for relevance
    
    // Time decay bonuses
    BonusRecent24h = 20   // Session within 24 hours of bead activity
    BonusRecent7d  = 10   // Session within 7 days
    PenaltyOld30d  = -10  // Session older than 30 days
    
    // Threshold for display
    MinScoreThreshold = 25  // Below this, don't show session
    
    // Result limits
    MaxSessionsReturned = 3  // Top N sessions per bead
    MaxKeywordsExtracted = 5 // Keywords from title
)
```

### Scoring Table (Reference)
| Factor | Weight | Rationale |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| ID mention | +100 | Definitive evidence |
| Exact keyword match | +50 | Strong thematic link |
| Partial keyword match | +30 | Probable relation |
| Same workspace | 2x multiplier | Critical for relevance |
| Recent session (<24h) | +20 | Fresh context |
| Recent session (<7d) | +10 | Relevant context |
| Older session (>30d) | -10 | May be stale |

**Minimum threshold for display: 25 points** (avoids noise)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ID mention strategy works
- [ ] Keyword extraction handles edge cases (empty, very long titles)
- [ ] Timestamp proximity filtering works
- [ ] Combined scoring produces sensible rankings
- [ ] Workspace filtering dramatically improves relevance
- [ ] Results are cached with appropriate TTL
- [ ] Empty beads (no title) handled gracefully
- [ ] All scoring constants are configurable

## Edge Cases
- Bead with empty title → skip keyword strategy, rely on ID/timestamp
- Bead with very long title → truncate to 5 keywords
- Many beads with similar keywords → ensure distinct sessions per bead
- Closed bead with no activity dates → use created_at only
- Workspace path unavailable → search all (lower precision, warn in debug log)
- Title is just "Bug" or "Fix" → all keywords filtered, skip keyword strategy

## Testing Strategy
- Test each strategy in isolation
- Test combined scoring with known inputs/outputs
- Test keyword extraction edge cases
- Test workspace filtering
- Test scoring threshold behavior
- Benchmark performance (target <500ms for single correlation)
close_reason:
Implemented Session-Bead Correlation Engine with:
- Keyword extraction with stop word filtering
- Three correlation strategies: ID mention (highest confidence), keyword search (medium), timestamp proximity (lower)
- Combined scoring with workspace boost (2x multiplier for same workspace)
- LRU cache integration
- 20 comprehensive tests, all pass with -race
- staticcheck clean

title: Topological Work-Plan Generator
description:
Leverage the existing DAG analysis to generate linearized, dependency-respecting work plans. This is the highest-value feature because it directly answers the question every developer and AI agent asks: 'What can I actually work on right now?'

## Background & Motivation
The analysis package already computes TopologicalOrder via topo.Sort(). However, this raw ordering isn't directly actionable because:
1. It includes closed issues
2. It doesn't filter to 'leaf nodes' (tasks with no open blockers)
3. It's not exposed via CLI for programmatic access

## Value Proposition
- For Humans: A 'Smart To-Do' view showing only actionable items eliminates cognitive overhead of scanning blocked tasks.
- For AI Agents: --robot-plan enables autonomous workflows where agents can request a strictly ordered task list, preventing work on blocked items.

## Technical Approach
1. Add GetActionableIssues() to analysis package - returns issues where all blocking dependencies are closed
2. Add GetExecutionPlan() - returns topologically sorted actionable items with parallel tracks identified
3. CLI flag --robot-plan outputs JSON with execution order
4. TUI view showing actionable items grouped by parallel tracks

## Success Criteria
- Agent can request plan and receive valid execution order
- Plan respects all blocking dependencies
- Parallel tracks (independent work streams) are identified
- Zero actionable items shown when all open issues are blocked

title: Add GetActionableIssues() to analysis package
description:
Identify issues that can be worked on immediately - those with no open blocking dependencies.

## Algorithm
func (a *Analyzer) GetActionableIssues() []model.Issue:
  - Skip closed issues
  - Skip issues with open blockers (only 'blocks' type creates hard deps)
  - Missing blockers don't block (graceful degradation)

## Key Design Decisions
1. Only 'blocks' type creates hard dependencies - 'related' and 'parent-child' are informational
2. Missing blockers don't block - Graceful degradation when referenced issue doesn't exist
3. Closed issues are never actionable - They're done

## File Changes

- pkg/analysis/graph_test.go: Add comprehensive tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Correctly identifies issues with no open blockers
- [ ] Handles missing dependency references gracefully
- [ ] Handles cycles gracefully
- [ ] Unit tests cover all edge cases

title: Add GetExecutionPlan() with parallel track detection
description:
Generate a dependency-respecting execution plan with parallel tracks identified for concurrent work.

## Data Structure
type ExecutionPlan struct {
    Tracks []ExecutionTrack
    Total  int
}

type ExecutionTrack struct {
    TrackID string
    Items   []PlanItem
    Reason  string  // Why these are grouped
}

type PlanItem struct {
    ID          string
    Title       string
    Priority    int
    UnblocksIDs []string  // What becomes actionable when done
}

## Algorithm
1. Get actionable issues from GetActionableIssues()
2. Identify connected components among actionable issues
3. Within each component, sort by priority then topological order
4. For each item, compute what it unblocks

## Considerations
- Parallel Tracks: Independent subgraphs can be worked on concurrently
- Unblocks Info: Helps prioritize - 'doing X unblocks 5 other tasks'
- Priority Integration: Within tracks, respect explicit priority

## File Changes
- pkg/analysis/plan.go: New file with plan generation logic
- pkg/analysis/plan_test.go: Tests

title: Context Packs & Recipes System
description:
Implement named workflow presets ('recipes') that bundle filters, layouts, and exports into one-command operations. This dramatically simplifies common workflows for both humans and AI agents.

## Background & Motivation
Users repeatedly perform the same sequences: 'Show me blocked high-priority items' or 'Export a release changelog'. Currently this requires remembering multiple flags. Recipes encode these patterns.

## Value Proposition
- For Humans: 'bv --recipe triage' replaces 'bv --status open,blocked --priority 0,1 --sort priority'
- For AI Agents: Recipes provide semantic entry points - 'triage mode' vs 'release mode' vs 'dependency analysis mode'

## Technical Approach
1. Define recipe schema (YAML)
2. Embed sensible default recipes
3. Allow user-defined recipes in .bv/recipes.yaml
4. CLI: bv --recipe <name> or bv -r <name>
5. TUI: Recipe picker with descriptions

## Built-in Recipes
- triage: Open/blocked issues, sorted by priority
- release-cut: Recently closed issues for changelog
- blocked-review: All blocked items with blocker info
- dependency-risk: High betweenness/PageRank items
- quick-wins: Low-priority, no-dependency items
- stale: Items not updated in 14+ days

title: Define recipe schema and configuration structure
description:
Design the YAML schema for recipe definitions that is both human-writable and machine-parseable.

## Schema Design
recipes:
  triage:
    description: 'Focus on urgent open/blocked items'
    filters:
      status: [open, blocked]
      priority_max: 2
    sort:
      by: priority
      direction: asc
    view: board
    export: null

## Schema Fields
- description: Human-readable explanation
- filters: Issue filtering criteria
- sort: Sort order
- view: Which view to activate
- export: Optional auto-export configuration
- metrics: Optional metric-based filtering
