title: AGENTS.md Project Preference Storage
description:
# AGENTS.md Project Preference Storage

## Background
When user declines the AGENTS.md prompt with "Don't ask again," we need to remember this per-project.

## Storage Design

### Location
\`\`\`
~/.config/bv/agent-prompts/
├── <project-hash-1>.json
├── <project-hash-2>.json
└── ...
\`\`\`

### Project Hash
Use SHA256 of absolute working directory path (truncated):
\`\`\`go
func projectHash(workDir string) string {
    abs, _ := filepath.Abs(workDir)
    hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(abs))
    return hex.EncodeToString(hash[:8]) // 16 char hex
}
\`\`\`

### Preference File Format
\`\`\`json
{
    "project_path": "/Users/dev/myproject",
    "dont_ask_again": true,
    "declined_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "blurb_version_offered": 1
}
\`\`\`

### Operations

\`\`\`go
type AgentPromptPreference struct {
    ProjectPath         string    \`json:"project_path"\`
    DontAskAgain        bool      \`json:"dont_ask_again"\`
    DeclinedAt          time.Time \`json:"declined_at,omitempty"\`
    BlurbVersionOffered int       \`json:"blurb_version_offered"\`
    BlurbVersionAdded   int       \`json:"blurb_version_added,omitempty"\`
    AddedAt             time.Time \`json:"added_at,omitempty"\`
}

func LoadAgentPromptPreference(workDir string) (*AgentPromptPreference, error)
func SaveAgentPromptPreference(workDir string, pref AgentPromptPreference) error
func ShouldPromptForAgentFile(workDir string, currentVersion int) bool
\`\`\`

### Decision Logic
\`\`\`go
func ShouldPromptForAgentFile(workDir string, currentVersion int) bool {
    pref, err := LoadAgentPromptPreference(workDir)
    if err != nil {
        return true // New project, never prompted
    }
    
    if pref.DontAskAgain {
        // BUT: if we have a newer blurb version, maybe ask again?
        // For now: respect "don't ask again" absolutely
        return false
    }
    
    // They declined but didn't check "don't ask again"
    // For now: respect that too (prompt only on explicit request)
    return false
}
\`\`\`

## Future Consideration
- What if blurb version updates? Could offer upgrade prompt.
- For now, "don't ask again" means never for this project.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Preferences saved per-project
- [ ] Path hashing is consistent
- [ ] Load/save work correctly
- [ ] Missing preference file means "new project"
- [ ] Decision logic respects preferences

## Dependencies
None - can be developed independently.
close_reason: Implemented preference storage with full test coverage

title: Data source correctness: allowlist discovery, silent probing, source_path in every payload
description:
## Why this epic exists
The 2026-09-01 reality check found that bv's data-source discovery (internal/datasource) treats every `*.jsonl` in `.beads/` as a candidate issue file and loads the freshest one. `br` writes `sync_base.jsonl` (a full prior snapshot with valid issue records) and bv writes `sprints.jsonl` and `correlation_feedback.jsonl` beside `issues.jsonl`. Reproduced on this repository: with `sync_base.jsonl` touched one hour newer, every robot command reported 682 issues instead of 541 with a different `data_hash`, and no payload field named the file that was read. The probe of `sprints.jsonl` also prints "Warning: skipping invalid issue on line 1: issue title cannot be empty" on every TUI start, export, and drift check.

For a triage engine whose whole value is "deterministic, trustworthy graph facts for agents", silently analysing the wrong file is the worst possible failure. This epic makes discovery an allowlist, makes probing silent, and makes the chosen source visible in every payload.

## Scope
- Allowlist discovery derived from `loader.PreferredJSONLNames` plus explicit overrides (`BEADS_DB`, `--db`).
- Warnings only for the selected source, never for rejected candidates.
- `BV_MAX_LINE_SIZE_MB` honoured on the datasource (robot) path.
- `source_path` / `source_kind` in the robot envelope (delivered by the robot-contract epic's envelope bead; this epic populates it).
- Unit, integration, and e2e coverage with fixtures that put a fresher sidecar beside `issues.jsonl`.

## Vision goals served
Reality-check checklist rows 1, 21-37, 39 (README "Data Loading & Self-Healing", "Robustness & Self-Healing", "Why Robots Love bv").

## Done when
Every child task is closed, `scripts/robot_smoke.sh` passes against the sidecar fixtures with clean stderr, and README describes the allowlist rule and the `source_path` field.
close_reason: All child beads closed and verified (see their close reasons).

title: Discovery allowlist: only issue-file names are JSONL candidates; sidecars never load
description:
## Context
bv discovers the Beads issue file by scanning `.beads/` (internal/datasource/source.go, `DiscoverSources`, lines ~240-280). Every `*.jsonl` becomes a candidate unless its name contains `.backup`, `.orig`, `.merge`, equals `deletions.jsonl`, or starts with `beads.left`/`beads.right`. `SelectBestSourceWithOptions` (select.go:54-61, 103-115) orders candidates freshest-first. `loadAndValidateJSONL` (load.go:330-372) accepts the first candidate that yields at least one valid issue.

`br` maintains `.beads/sync_base.jsonl` (a full snapshot of a previous state, all records valid). `bv` itself writes `.beads/sprints.jsonl` (no `_type` field) and `.beads/correlation_feedback.jsonl`. `bd` workspaces can carry `memories.jsonl` and `interactions.jsonl`. Any of these that is newer than `issues.jsonl` is probed first; `sync_base.jsonl` wins outright.

Reproduction (2026-09-01, main @ 03f92509): copy `.beads/` to a scratch dir, `touch -d '+1 hour' sync_base.jsonl`, run `BEADS_DIR=<dir> bv --robot-triage`: `issue_count` 682 instead of 541, `data_hash` 993ec7ae... instead of d9d7d1f6.... Nothing in the payload names the file. The June 2026 skill-loop fix ("BUG-D1 sprints.jsonl shadowing") only rejects files with zero valid issues, which `sync_base.jsonl` is not.

## Why it matters
bv's value proposition is deterministic, trustworthy graph facts for agents (README "Cognitive Offloading", "Why Robots Love bv"). Silently analysing a stale snapshot violates it completely, and the failure is invisible because `data_hash` looks legitimate.

## Target state
Discovery is an allowlist: only names in `loader.PreferredJSONLNames` (`issues.jsonl`, `beads.jsonl`, `beads.base.jsonl`) are JSONL candidates. Explicit overrides (`BEADS_DB` pointing at a file, `--db`) bypass the allowlist. Every other `.jsonl` (including `sync_base.jsonl`, `sprints.jsonl`, `correlation_feedback.jsonl`, `memories.jsonl`, `interactions.jsonl`) is never a candidate and is logged at debug level as "skipped: not an issue file name". SQLite discovery (`beads.db`) is unchanged.

## Implementation
1. `internal/datasource/source.go`: replace the suffix check with `isIssueFileName(name string) bool` that returns true only for `loader.PreferredJSONLNames` entries; keep the existing exclusion list as a second guard.
2. `DiscoveryOptions` gains `ExplicitPath string` (from `BEADS_DB` file or `--db`) that is added as a candidate regardless of name, with `Priority` above local JSONL.
3. `loader.GetBeadsDir` / `loader.FindBeadsFile` (pkg/loader/loader.go:38-140) already use the preferred-name list; make `datasource` import the same slice so there is one source of truth.
4. Verbose/debug logging (`opts.Logger`) lists every file seen and the decision.
5. Update README "Data Loading & Self-Healing" step list and "Robustness & Self-Healing" bullet to describe the allowlist (the docs epic owns the final prose; this bead changes the two sentences that would otherwise be false).

## Success criteria
- `TestDiscoverSources_IgnoresSidecars` (internal/datasource/source_test.go): fixture with `issues.jsonl` plus newer `sync_base.jsonl`, `sprints.jsonl`, `correlation_feedback.jsonl`, `memories.jsonl`, `interactions.jsonl` returns exactly one JSONL candidate.
- `TestDiscoverSources_ExplicitPathBypassesAllowlist`: `BEADS_DB=/x/custom.jsonl` is a candidate.
- `TestLoadIssues_FresherSyncBaseDoesNotWin` (load_report_test.go): issue count and `ComputeDataHash` equal the `issues.jsonl` values.
- `go test ./internal/datasource -race` green.

## Files
internal/datasource/source.go, select.go (no behaviour change, comment update), load.go (uses the same list), pkg/loader/loader.go (export the list if not already), README.md (two sentences).
close_reason: Implemented with unit/integration tests; self-verified by re-running go test (see internal/datasource/sidecar_test.go, pkg/analysis/plan_test.go, pkg/search/config_test.go, cmd/bv/search_output_test.go)

title: Silent candidate probing: buffer loader warnings, report only for the selected source, expose candidates in load_stats
description:
## Context
`internal/datasource/load.go` builds a `loadRecorder` per candidate (`newLoadRecorder`, line 77) whose warning callback prints "Warning: skipping invalid issue on line N: ..." immediately in non-robot mode (robot mode, `BV_ROBOT=1`, suppresses stderr per issue #190). Because candidates are probed in freshest-first order, a rejected candidate's warnings reach the user even though the file is then discarded. Reproduced on this repository: `.beads/sprints.jsonl` (no `_type`, first record has no title) is newer than `issues.jsonl`, so `bv` (TUI), `bv --export-md`, `bv --export-graph`, and `bv --check-drift` all print "Warning: skipping invalid issue on line 1: issue title cannot be empty" although `issues.jsonl` loads 541/541.

After the allowlist (bead A1) sprints.jsonl is no longer probed, but the same leak would recur for any legitimately-named candidate that loses (for example a corrupt `beads.jsonl` beside a good `issues.jsonl`), so the recorder must buffer.

## Target state
Warnings from candidate probing are buffered per candidate and emitted only for the candidate that is finally selected. Rejected candidates contribute a single debug-level line ("rejected <path>: <reason>, <n> warnings suppressed"). `LoadReport` gains `Candidates []CandidateReport{Path, Selected, Reason, Warnings int}` so `load_stats` (robot) and `--profile-startup` (human) can show what was considered.

## Implementation
1. `loadRecorder.warn` appends to `warnings` always; add `flush(w io.Writer)` that prints them; call `flush` only after `loadAndValidateJSONL` returns success for that candidate.
2. `loadSmart` (load.go:270) collects `CandidateReport` for each attempt and stores it on the committed `LoadReport`.
3. `robotLoadStatsFromLastLoad` (cmd/bv/main.go:8359) includes `candidates` when more than one was considered, even when `Errors == 0`.
4. `--profile-startup` prints the candidate table.

## Success criteria
- `TestLoadIssues_ProbeIsSilent`: newer invalid `beads.jsonl` beside valid `issues.jsonl`; stderr empty in non-robot mode; `LoadReport.Candidates` lists both with the loser marked rejected.
- `TestLoadIssues_SelectedSourceStillWarns`: malformed line in the selected file still prints exactly one warning.
- e2e `tests/e2e/datasource_sidecar_test.go` (created by bead A4) asserts clean stderr for `--export-md` and `--check-drift`.

## Files
internal/datasource/load.go, cmd/bv/main.go (load stats, profile-startup), tests.
close_reason: Implemented with unit/integration tests; self-verified by re-running go test (see internal/datasource/sidecar_test.go, pkg/analysis/plan_test.go, pkg/search/config_test.go, cmd/bv/search_output_test.go)

title: Honour BV_MAX_LINE_SIZE_MB on the datasource (robot) path
description:
## Context
README documents `BV_MAX_LINE_SIZE_MB` ("Max JSONL line size in MB; larger lines are skipped with a warning", default 10). The variable is read only on TUI paths: `pkg/ui/background_worker.go:1738` (into `loadOptions.BufferSize`) and `pkg/ui/model.go:3123`. The robot/datasource path (`internal/datasource/load.go:81-92`, `loadRecorder.options()`) never sets `BufferSize`, so every robot command uses `loader.DefaultMaxBufferSize` (10 MiB) regardless of the variable. A repository with a 12 MB description line loads in the TUI with the variable set and silently drops the issue in `--robot-triage`.

## Target state
One helper `loader.MaxLineSizeFromEnv() int` returns the configured buffer size (validated: 1..1024 MB, default 10) and is used by both the TUI and the datasource path. Robot `load_stats.warnings` records dropped oversized lines as today.

title: Cass Detection and Health Checking
description:
# Cass Detection and Health Checking

## Purpose
Determine if cass is installed and operational before attempting any integration. This is the foundation of the entire feature—every other component depends on knowing cass availability.

## Background

### Why Detection Matters
Unlike a library dependency, cass is an external binary that may or may not be installed. We cannot assume its presence. Detection must be:
- Fast (sub-100ms)
- Cached (avoid repeated checks)
- Silent on failure (no error messages to users)

### cass Health States
| Exit Code | Meaning | Our Response |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| 0 | Healthy, ready to search | Enable integration |
| 1 | Needs indexing | Disable integration (silent) |
| 3 | Index missing/corrupt | Disable integration (silent) |
| Other/timeout | Unknown error | Disable integration (silent) |

## Implementation

### Detection Flow
```
1. Check if "cass" exists in PATH
   └─ No → StatusNotInstalled, stop
   
2. Run "cass health" with 2s timeout
   └─ Timeout → StatusNotInstalled, stop
   └─ Exit 0 → StatusHealthy, continue
   └─ Exit 1 → StatusNeedsIndex, stop
   └─ Other → StatusNotInstalled, stop

3. (Optional) Run "cass capabilities --json"
   └─ Cache supported features
```

### Caching Strategy
- Cache detection result for 5 minutes
- Re-check on explicit user action (future: "refresh cass" command)
- Invalidate cache on error during search

### Types
```go
type Status int
const (
    StatusUnknown Status = iota
    StatusNotInstalled
    StatusNeedsIndex
    StatusHealthy
)

type Detector struct {
    status    Status
    checkedAt time.Time
    cacheTTL  time.Duration
    mu        sync.RWMutex
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Detects cass binary in PATH
- [ ] Runs health check with timeout
- [ ] Caches result with TTL
- [ ] Thread-safe for concurrent access
- [ ] Zero output/errors when cass not found
- [ ] Returns StatusHealthy only when cass ready

## Edge Cases
- cass binary exists but is not executable
- cass hangs on health check (timeout protection)
- PATH changes during bv session (cache invalidation)
- Multiple cass binaries in PATH (use first found)

## Testing Strategy
- Mock exec.LookPath for binary detection
- Mock exec.Command for health check responses
- Test all status transitions
- Test cache expiration
- Test concurrent access safety
close_reason: Implemented pkg/cass/detector.go with full test coverage (17 tests). Features: PATH detection, health check with timeout, TTL caching, thread-safe concurrent access, silent failure mode.

title: Search ranking: improve short-query relevance in hybrid mode
description:
# Rationale
Hybrid search is intended to *find specific beads quickly* while still surfacing high-impact items when they are actually relevant. Right now, short/generic queries (e.g., "benchmarks") can be dominated by high-impact items that are lexically unrelated. This hurts primary search intent; triage already exists for impact-driven prioritization.

The change should make hybrid search more literal for short queries and improve recall for obvious lexical matches, without removing the benefit of graph-aware ranking for longer, descriptive queries.

# Proposed Change
1. **Two-stage retrieval**
   - Stage 1: text search selects top-K candidates (e.g., 200).
   - Stage 2: hybrid scoring re-ranks only that candidate set.
   - This prevents high-impact but lexically unrelated items from displacing obvious matches.

2. **Short-query weight dampening**
   - For short queries (<=2 tokens or <12 chars), increase text weight and reduce graph weights (pagerank/impact/priority), keeping hybrid mostly for tie-breaks.
   - Longer queries keep existing presets.

3. **Tests**
   - Unit test: short query keeps exact lexical matches above unrelated high-impact items.
   - E2E: on this repo’s beads, query "benchmarks" returns `bv-61hu` within top-N using hybrid default/impact-first.

# Acceptance Criteria
- Hybrid search never returns a fully irrelevant high-impact item *above* a direct lexical match for short queries.
- The top-N for "benchmarks" includes `bv-61hu` (or equivalent direct match) for hybrid mode.
- Tests added and passing.
notes: Starting implementation: candidate gating + short-query dampening + tests.

- \`Ctrl+u\` - Half page up

title: [EPIC] Graph-Aware Hybrid Search Ranking
description:
## Overview

Transform bv's search from pure text matching to graph-aware hybrid ranking that combines text relevance with PageRank, actionability, impact, priority, and recency.

## Problem Statement

bv positions itself as a "graph-aware triage engine" with precomputed metrics (PageRank, betweenness, critical path, cycles, HITS, eigenvector, k-core). However, search functionality completely ignores these metrics:

- **TUI semantic search**: Pure dot product of vector embeddings
- **CLI --robot-search**: Pure dot product of vector embeddings
- **Web FTS5 search**: Pure BM25 text relevance

This is a fundamental misalignment. A user searching "authentication bug" should see HIGH-IMPACT authentication bugs first, not just any text match.

## Solution: Hybrid Ranking Formula

```
hybrid_score = 0.40 × text_relevance   # Core search match
             + 0.20 × pagerank         # Graph importance
             + 0.15 × status_weight    # Actionability (open > closed)
             + 0.10 × impact_weight    # Blocker count normalized
             + 0.10 × priority_weight  # P0 > P4
             + 0.05 × recency_weight   # Temporal decay
```

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Backward Compatible**: Default mode remains text-only; hybrid is opt-in via --search-mode=hybrid
2. **Graceful Degradation**: Missing metrics fall back to text-only, no failures
3. **Configurable Weights**: Presets for common use cases (bug-hunting, sprint-planning, impact-first)
4. **Performance Target**: <2x overhead vs text-only for typical queries

## Weight Presets

- **default**: Balanced across all factors
- **bug-hunting**: Boost priority and impact (0.20 priority, 0.15 impact)
- **sprint-planning**: Boost actionability (0.25 status)
- **impact-first**: Boost graph importance (0.30 pagerank, 0.20 impact)
- **text-only**: Pure text search (1.0 text, 0.0 everything else)

## Success Criteria

1. High-PageRank issues rank higher for same text match
2. Open issues rank higher than closed for same text match
3. P0 bugs rank higher than P4 bugs for same text match
4. Preset switching works without code changes
5. Existing tests pass without modification
6. Performance within 2x of baseline

## Architecture

```
Search Request → Text Search Layer → MetricsCache → HybridScorer → Ranked Results
```

Components:
- **MetricsCache**: Lazy-loads PageRank, status, priority, blockerCount from graph analysis
- **HybridScorer**: Computes weighted sum with configurable weights
- **WeightPreset**: Named configurations for common use cases

## Scope

IN SCOPE:
- HybridScorer interface and implementation
- MetricsCache for search-time metric access
- CLI, TUI, and Web integration
- Weight presets and configuration
- Unit and integration tests
- Documentation updates

OUT OF SCOPE (future work):
- True semantic embeddings (sentence-transformers/OpenAI)
- Click-through feedback loop
- Query expansion/synonyms
- Machine-learned ranking
notes: All hybrid search sub-tasks complete, including optional WASM scorer integration

title: Design HybridScorer interface and weight configuration
description:
## ⚠️ EDGE CASE: Zero Text Weight Warning

If text weight < 0.1, add WARNING (not error) in Validate():
```go
if w.TextRelevance < 0.1 {
    log.Printf("WARNING: text weight %.2f is very low; results may not match query", w.TextRelevance)
}
```

---

## Objective

Define the Go interface for HybridScorer and the weight configuration data structures. This is the foundational design that all other tasks depend on.

## Deliverables

### 1. HybridScorer Interface (pkg/search/hybrid_scorer.go)

```go
// HybridScorer computes hybrid search scores combining text relevance with graph metrics.
type HybridScorer interface {
    // Score computes the hybrid score for an issue given its text score and metrics.
    // Returns the final score and component breakdown.
    Score(issueID string, textScore float64) (HybridScore, error)
    
    // Configure sets the weights for hybrid scoring.
    Configure(weights Weights) error
    
    // GetWeights returns the current weight configuration.
    GetWeights() Weights
}

// HybridScore contains the final score and component breakdown for transparency.
type HybridScore struct {
    IssueID         string             `json:"issue_id"`
    FinalScore      float64            `json:"score"`
    TextScore       float64            `json:"text_score"`
    ComponentScores map[string]float64 `json:"component_scores,omitempty"`
}
```

### 2. Weight Configuration (pkg/search/weights.go)

```go
// Weights defines the relative importance of each ranking factor.
// All weights should sum to 1.0 for normalized scoring.
type Weights struct {
    TextRelevance float64 `json:"text"`     // Core search match quality
    PageRank      float64 `json:"pagerank"` // Graph centrality importance
    Status        float64 `json:"status"`   // Actionability (open > closed)
    Impact        float64 `json:"impact"`   // Blocker count normalized
    Priority      float64 `json:"priority"` // User-assigned priority
    Recency       float64 `json:"recency"`  // Temporal decay
}

// Validate checks that weights are valid (non-negative, sum to ~1.0).
func (w Weights) Validate() error

// Normalize scales weights to sum to 1.0.
func (w Weights) Normalize() Weights
```

### 3. Weight Presets (pkg/search/presets.go)

```go
// PresetName identifies a named weight configuration.
type PresetName string

const (
    PresetDefault       PresetName = "default"
    PresetBugHunting    PresetName = "bug-hunting"
    PresetSprintPlanning PresetName = "sprint-planning"
    PresetImpactFirst   PresetName = "impact-first"
    PresetTextOnly      PresetName = "text-only"
)

// GetPreset returns the weights for a named preset.
func GetPreset(name PresetName) (Weights, error)

// ListPresets returns all available preset names.
func ListPresets() []PresetName
```

## Design Considerations

1. **Extensibility**: Interface allows future implementations (e.g., ML-based scorer)
2. **Transparency**: ComponentScores breakdown enables debugging and user understanding
3. **Validation**: Weights validated to prevent invalid configurations
4. **JSON-friendly**: All structs have JSON tags for CLI/API output

## Normalization Functions

Document these in comments:
- StatusWeight: {open: 1.0, in_progress: 0.8, blocked: 0.5, closed: 0.1}
- PriorityWeight: P0→1.0, P1→0.8, P2→0.6, P3→0.4, P4→0.2
- RecencyWeight: exp(-days_since_update / 30)
- ImpactWeight: blocker_count / max_blocker_count (or 0.5 if max=0)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Interface defined with clear documentation
- [ ] Weight struct with validation
- [ ] All 5 presets defined with values matching design doc
- [ ] Unit tests for Weights.Validate() and Weights.Normalize()
- [ ] No implementation yet - just interfaces and types

## Files to Create

- pkg/search/hybrid_scorer.go (interface + types)
- pkg/search/weights.go (Weights struct + presets)
- pkg/search/weights_test.go (validation tests)

Depends on (1):
  → bv-xbar: [EPIC] Graph-Aware Hybrid Search Ranking [P1]

Blocks (6):

  ← bv-xbar.11: Unit tests for HybridScorer and MetricsCache [P1]
  ← bv-xbar.2: Implement MetricsCache for search-time metric access [P1]
  ← bv-xbar.3: Implement HybridScorer with configurable weights [P1]
  ← bv-xbar.7: Web export: Add graph metrics to SQLite export [P1]
  ← bv-xbar.8: Web export: JavaScript HybridScorer in viewer.js [P1]

title: Add weight presets and environment configuration
description:
## 🔧 SCOPE REDUCED: No Config File

**REMOVED:** Config file support (~/.config/bv/search.json) - bv has no config system.

**KEEP:** CLI flags + environment variables are sufficient for v1.

---

## Objective

Implement the weight preset system and environment variable configuration for hybrid search, enabling users to customize ranking behavior without code changes.

## Preset Definitions

### Go Implementation (pkg/search/presets.go)

```go
var presets = map[PresetName]Weights{
    PresetDefault: {
        TextRelevance: 0.40,
        PageRank:      0.20,
        Status:        0.15,
        Impact:        0.10,
        Priority:      0.10,
        Recency:       0.05,
    },
    PresetBugHunting: {
        TextRelevance: 0.30,
        PageRank:      0.15,
        Status:        0.15,
        Impact:        0.15,
        Priority:      0.20, // Boosted for bug severity
        Recency:       0.05,
    },
    PresetSprintPlanning: {
        TextRelevance: 0.30,
        PageRank:      0.20,
        Status:        0.25, // Boosted for actionability
        Impact:        0.15,
        Priority:      0.05,
        Recency:       0.05,
    },
    PresetImpactFirst: {
        TextRelevance: 0.25,
        PageRank:      0.30, // Boosted graph importance
        Status:        0.10,
        Impact:        0.20, // Boosted blocker impact
        Priority:      0.10,
        Recency:       0.05,
    },
    PresetTextOnly: {
        TextRelevance: 1.00,
        PageRank:      0.00,
        Status:        0.00,
        Impact:        0.00,
        Priority:      0.00,
        Recency:       0.00,
    },
}
```

## Environment Variables

```bash
# Override default search mode
BV_SEARCH_MODE=hybrid         # text|hybrid

# Override default preset when mode=hybrid
BV_SEARCH_PRESET=default      # default|bug-hunting|sprint-planning|impact-first|text-only

# Custom weights (JSON, overrides preset)
BV_SEARCH_WEIGHTS='{"text":0.5,"pagerank":0.3,"status":0.1,"impact":0.05,"priority":0.03,"recency":0.02}'
```

## Configuration Precedence

1. CLI flags (highest priority)
2. Environment variables
3. Config file (~/.config/bv/search.json)
4. Built-in defaults (lowest priority)

## Config File Format

```json
// ~/.config/bv/search.json
{
  "default_mode": "hybrid",
  "default_preset": "default",
  "custom_presets": {
    "my-team": {
      "text": 0.35,
      "pagerank": 0.25,
      "status": 0.15,
      "impact": 0.10,
      "priority": 0.10,
      "recency": 0.05
    }
  }
}
```

## Validation

Weights must:
- Be non-negative
- Sum to 1.0 (±0.001 tolerance)
- Have all 6 fields present

```go
func (w Weights) Validate() error {
    if w.TextRelevance < 0 || w.PageRank < 0 || w.Status < 0 ||
       w.Impact < 0 || w.Priority < 0 || w.Recency < 0 {
        return errors.New("weights must be non-negative")
    }
    
    sum := w.TextRelevance + w.PageRank + w.Status + w.Impact + w.Priority + w.Recency
    if math.Abs(sum-1.0) > 0.001 {
        return fmt.Errorf("weights must sum to 1.0, got %.3f", sum)
    }
    
    return nil
}
```

```
                               - impact-first: Boost PageRank and blocker count

  --search-weights <json>      Custom weights (overrides preset)
                               Example: '{"text":0.5,"pagerank":0.3,...}'

Environment variables: BV_SEARCH_MODE, BV_SEARCH_PRESET, BV_SEARCH_WEIGHTS
```

title: Implementation notes: Critical fixes and considerations
description:
## Purpose

This task documents critical implementation details discovered during the design review. **READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING OTHER TASKS.**

## ⚠️ CRITICAL FIX #1: Over-fetch Strategy (bv-xbar.5, bv-xbar.6)

**Problem:** Naive re-ranking fails to surface high-graph-score issues with mediocre text scores.

**Example:**
- Issue A: text=0.6, pagerank=0.9 → hybrid≈0.75 (should rank high!)
- Issue B: text=0.8, pagerank=0.1 → hybrid≈0.35

Getting top-10 by text score excludes A, so re-ranking can't fix it.

**Solution:** Over-fetch 2-3x candidates before hybrid scoring:
\`\`\`go
fetchLimit := limit * 3  // Over-fetch for re-ranking
textResults, _ := idx.SearchTopK(queryVec, fetchLimit)
// Apply hybrid scoring to ALL candidates, then trim to limit
\`\`\`

bv-xbar.8 (web) already has this: \`limit * 2\`. Apply same pattern to CLI and TUI.

## 🔧 SCOPE FIX #2: Remove Config File (bv-xbar.10)

The presets task originally included \`~/.config/bv/search.json\` support, but:
1. bv doesn't have a config file system
2. CLI flags + env vars are sufficient for v1
3. Adds unnecessary complexity

**Revised scope:** Only implement presets, env vars, and CLI flags. Defer config file to future task if needed.

## ⚠️ EDGE CASE #3: Zero Text Weight

If user sets \`text=0\`, results are ranked purely by graph metrics, ignoring the search query. This is valid but may surprise users.

**Recommendation:** Add warning (not error) in Weights.Validate() if text < 0.1.

## 🔗 PARITY CHECK #4: Go/JS Preset Sync

JavaScript presets in hybrid_scorer.js MUST match Go presets exactly. Add a unit test that:
1. Reads JS preset values from the file
2. Compares against Go GetPreset() values
3. Fails if any preset drifts

## 💭 FUTURE CONSIDERATION: Status Normalization

Current mapping (open=1.0, in_progress=0.8, blocked=0.5, closed=0.1) is a reasonable default, but different use cases might want different interpretations:
- Sprint planning: open > blocked > in_progress
- Bottleneck analysis: blocked issues MORE important

For v1, single normalization is fine. Consider per-preset status weights in v2.

## Success Criteria

This task is complete when implementers have read and acknowledged these notes. It can be closed immediately after review.

title: Implement MetricsCache for search-time metric access
description:
## Objective

Create a cache layer that provides graph metrics (PageRank, status, priority, blocker count, updated_at) for search-time hybrid score computation.

## Background

Graph metrics are computed by bv's analysis engine (--robot-insights) but aren't easily accessible during search. The MetricsCache bridges this gap by:
1. Loading metrics on demand (lazy initialization)
2. Caching for repeated lookups within a search session
3. Invalidating when data_hash changes

## Deliverables

### MetricsCache Interface (pkg/search/metrics_cache.go)

```go
// IssueMetrics contains the graph-derived metrics for hybrid scoring.
type IssueMetrics struct {
    IssueID      string    `json:"issue_id"`
    PageRank     float64   `json:"pagerank"`      // 0.0-1.0, from graph analysis
    Status       string    `json:"status"`        // open|in_progress|blocked|closed
    Priority     int       `json:"priority"`      // 0-4 (P0=0, P4=4)
    BlockerCount int       `json:"blocker_count"` // How many issues this blocks
    UpdatedAt    time.Time `json:"updated_at"`    // For recency calculation
}

// MetricsCache provides fast access to issue metrics for hybrid scoring.
type MetricsCache interface {
    // Get returns metrics for an issue, computing/loading if needed.
    Get(issueID string) (IssueMetrics, bool)
    
    // GetBatch returns metrics for multiple issues efficiently.
    GetBatch(issueIDs []string) map[string]IssueMetrics
    
    // Refresh recomputes the cache from source data.
    Refresh() error
    
    // DataHash returns the hash of source data for cache validation.
    DataHash() string
    
    // MaxBlockerCount returns the maximum blocker count for normalization.
    MaxBlockerCount() int
}
```

### Implementation (pkg/search/metrics_cache_impl.go)

```go
type metricsCache struct {
    mu              sync.RWMutex
    metrics         map[string]IssueMetrics
    dataHash        string
    maxBlockerCount int
    loader          MetricsLoader
}

// MetricsLoader abstracts the source of metrics (graph analysis or direct DB).
type MetricsLoader interface {
    LoadMetrics() (map[string]IssueMetrics, error)
    ComputeDataHash() (string, error)
}
```

## Data Sources

Metrics come from existing bv computations:
- **PageRank**: Already computed in pkg/graph/analysis.go
- **Status/Priority**: Directly from issue model
- **BlockerCount**: From dependency graph (out-degree in blocks relation)
- **UpdatedAt**: Directly from issue model

## Lazy Loading Strategy

1. First search call triggers cache initialization
2. Cache stores data_hash to detect stale data
3. On subsequent calls, check data_hash; refresh if changed
4. Use sync.RWMutex for concurrent read access

## Graceful Degradation

If metrics unavailable (e.g., no graph computed):
- Return default metrics with neutral values
- PageRank: 0.5 (neutral)
- BlockerCount: 0
- Don't fail the search

## Success Criteria

- [ ] MetricsCache interface defined
- [ ] Implementation loads from graph analysis
- [ ] Lazy initialization on first access
- [ ] Cache invalidation on data_hash change
- [ ] GetBatch() for efficient bulk lookups
- [ ] Thread-safe with RWMutex
- [ ] Unit tests for cache behavior
- [ ] Graceful handling of missing metrics

## Files to Create

- pkg/search/metrics_cache.go (interface)
- pkg/search/metrics_cache_impl.go (implementation)
- pkg/search/metrics_cache_test.go (unit tests)

## Dependencies

- Depends on: bv-xbar.1 (Design HybridScorer interface)
- Blocked by: None

title: Implement HybridScorer with configurable weights
description:
## 📝 FUTURE: Preset-specific Status Weights

Current values (open=1.0, in_progress=0.8, blocked=0.5, closed=0.1) are for general actionability.

Future enhancement: Allow presets to override status weights:
- sprint-planning: blocked=0.2 (deprioritize blocked during sprint)
- bug-hunting: status weights unchanged (focus on priority/impact)

Keep simple for v1; expose as configuration option later if needed.

---

## Objective

Implement the core HybridScorer that combines text relevance with graph metrics using configurable weights.

## Background

This is the heart of hybrid search ranking. Given a text score and issue metrics, compute a weighted sum that balances relevance with graph importance.

## Deliverables

### HybridScorer Implementation (pkg/search/hybrid_scorer_impl.go)

```go
type hybridScorer struct {
    weights Weights
    cache   MetricsCache
}

// NewHybridScorer creates a scorer with the given weights and metrics cache.
func NewHybridScorer(weights Weights, cache MetricsCache) HybridScorer

func (s *hybridScorer) Score(issueID string, textScore float64) (HybridScore, error) {
    metrics, found := s.cache.Get(issueID)
    if !found {
        // Graceful degradation: return text-only score
        return HybridScore{
            IssueID:    issueID,
            FinalScore: textScore,
            TextScore:  textScore,
        }, nil
    }
    
    // Compute normalized component scores
    statusScore := normalizeStatus(metrics.Status)
    priorityScore := normalizePriority(metrics.Priority)
    impactScore := normalizeImpact(metrics.BlockerCount, s.cache.MaxBlockerCount())
    recencyScore := normalizeRecency(metrics.UpdatedAt)
    
    // Weighted sum
    final := s.weights.TextRelevance * textScore +
             s.weights.PageRank * metrics.PageRank +
             s.weights.Status * statusScore +
             s.weights.Impact * impactScore +
             s.weights.Priority * priorityScore +
             s.weights.Recency * recencyScore
    
    return HybridScore{
        IssueID:    issueID,
        FinalScore: final,
        TextScore:  textScore,
        ComponentScores: map[string]float64{
            "pagerank": metrics.PageRank,
            "status":   statusScore,
            "impact":   impactScore,
            "priority": priorityScore,
            "recency":  recencyScore,
        },
    }, nil
}
```

### Normalization Functions (pkg/search/normalizers.go)

```go
// normalizeStatus maps status to [0,1] range favoring actionable states.
func normalizeStatus(status string) float64 {
    switch status {
    case "open":        return 1.0
    case "in_progress": return 0.8
    case "blocked":     return 0.5
    case "closed":      return 0.1
    default:            return 0.5
    }
}

// normalizePriority maps P0-P4 to [0.2, 1.0] range.
func normalizePriority(priority int) float64 {
    switch priority {
    case 0: return 1.0  // P0 Critical
    case 1: return 0.8  // P1 High
    case 2: return 0.6  // P2 Medium
    case 3: return 0.4  // P3 Low
    case 4: return 0.2  // P4 Lowest
    default: return 0.5
    }
}

// normalizeImpact normalizes blocker count to [0,1].
func normalizeImpact(blockerCount, maxBlockerCount int) float64 {
    if maxBlockerCount == 0 {
        return 0.5 // Neutral when no blockers exist
    }
    return float64(blockerCount) / float64(maxBlockerCount)
}

// normalizeRecency applies exponential decay (half-life ~30 days).
func normalizeRecency(updatedAt time.Time) float64 {
    daysSinceUpdate := time.Since(updatedAt).Hours() / 24
    return math.Exp(-daysSinceUpdate / 30)
}
```

## Design Decisions

1. **Component scores always computed**: Even when weight is 0, compute for transparency
2. **Graceful degradation**: Missing metrics → text-only score (no error)
3. **Normalization to [0,1]**: All factors normalized before weighting
4. **Weights must sum to ~1.0**: Enforced by Weights.Validate()

## Success Criteria

- [ ] HybridScorer implementation computes correct weighted scores
- [ ] All 4 normalizer functions implemented with tests
- [ ] Component breakdown included in HybridScore
- [ ] Graceful handling of missing metrics
- [ ] Unit tests with known inputs → expected outputs
- [ ] Benchmark showing <1ms per score computation

## Files to Create

- pkg/search/hybrid_scorer_impl.go
- pkg/search/normalizers.go
- pkg/search/normalizers_test.go
- pkg/search/hybrid_scorer_test.go

## Dependencies

- Depends on: bv-xbar.1 (interface), bv-xbar.2 (MetricsCache)

Depends on (3):
  → bv-xbar: [EPIC] Graph-Aware Hybrid Search Ranking [P1]
  → bv-xbar.1: Design HybridScorer interface and weight configuration [P1]
  → bv-xbar.2: Implement MetricsCache for search-time metric access [P1]

Blocks (5):
  ← bv-xbar.11: Unit tests for HybridScorer and MetricsCache [P1]
  ← bv-xbar.5: CLI integration: --robot-search hybrid mode [P1]
  ← bv-xbar.4: Add field boosting for title/labels/description [P2]
  ← bv-xbar.6: TUI integration: hybrid search toggle [P2]
  ← bv-xbar.13: Performance benchmarks for hybrid search [P3]

title: Add field boosting for title/labels/description
description:
## Objective

Enhance text relevance scoring by weighting matches differently based on which field they occur in.

## Background

Currently, all text matches are weighted equally regardless of where they occur. A title match should rank higher than a description match because titles are more semantically dense.

## Proposed Field Weights

- **ID exact match**: ×3.0 (user knows exactly what they want)
- **Title match**: ×2.0 (most important semantic content)
- **Labels match**: ×1.5 (categorization is valuable)
- **Description match**: ×1.0 (baseline)

## Implementation Approaches

### Option A: Modify IssueDocument() (simplest)

Repeat important fields in the document:
```go
func IssueDocument(issue model.Issue) string {
    // Repeat title twice for implicit 2x weight
    title := strings.TrimSpace(issue.Title)
    labels := strings.Join(issue.Labels, " ")
    desc := strings.TrimSpace(issue.Description)
    
    return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s %s %s", 
        title, title,  // title appears twice (2x weight)
        labels,        // labels once
        desc)          // description once
}
```

### Option B: Multi-field scoring (more precise)

Score each field separately and combine:
```go
func ScoreWithFieldBoost(query, title, labels, desc string) float64 {
    titleScore := embedAndScore(query, title) * 2.0
    labelScore := embedAndScore(query, labels) * 1.5
    descScore := embedAndScore(query, desc) * 1.0
    return max(titleScore, labelScore, descScore)
}
```

### Option C: BM25F (for FTS5)

SQLite FTS5 supports column weights:
```sql
-- Create FTS with column weights
SELECT bm25(issues_fts, 3.0, 2.0, 1.5, 1.0) -- id, title, labels, desc
FROM issues_fts WHERE issues_fts MATCH ?
```

## Recommendation

- For vector search (TUI/CLI): Use Option A (document repetition) - simplest
- For FTS5 search (Web): Use Option C (BM25F weights)

## ID Exact Match Detection

If query looks like an issue ID (matches prefix pattern), check for exact match first:
```go
func IsLikelyIssueID(query string) bool {
    // Match patterns like "bv-abc", "BV-123", etc.
    matched, _ := regexp.MatchString(`^[a-zA-Z]+-[a-zA-Z0-9]+$`, query)
    return matched
}
```

## Success Criteria

- [ ] IssueDocument() repeats title for implicit boosting
- [ ] FTS5 query uses column weights
- [ ] ID exact match ranks first
- [ ] Unit tests verify field boosting effect
- [ ] A/B comparison showing title matches rank higher

## Files to Modify

- pkg/search/documents.go (modify IssueDocument)
- pkg/export/sqlite_schema.go (FTS5 column weights)
- pkg/export/viewer_assets/viewer.js (BM25F in query)

## Dependencies

- Depends on: bv-xbar.3 (HybridScorer)
- Can be done in parallel with integration tasks

title: CLI integration: --robot-search hybrid mode
description:
## ⚠️ CRITICAL: Over-fetch Strategy Required

**BUG:** Getting top-K by text score, then re-ranking misses high-graph-score issues with mediocre text scores.

**FIX:** Over-fetch 3x candidates before hybrid scoring:
```go
fetchLimit := limit * 3  // Over-fetch for re-ranking
textResults, _ := idx.SearchTopK(queryVec, fetchLimit)
// Apply hybrid scoring, re-sort, trim to requested limit
```

---

## Objective

Add hybrid search mode to the CLI --robot-search command, allowing AI agents to leverage graph-aware ranking.

## Background

Currently --robot-search returns results ranked purely by vector similarity. This task adds:
- --search-mode flag to switch between text and hybrid
- --search-preset flag to use named weight configurations
- Extended JSON output with component scores

## New CLI Flags

```
--search-mode text|hybrid    Mode for ranking (default: text)
--search-preset <name>       Weight preset: default, bug-hunting, sprint-planning, 
                             impact-first, text-only
--search-weights <json>      Custom weights JSON (advanced, overrides preset)
```

## Implementation

### Flag Registration (cmd/bv/main.go)

```go
searchCmd.Flags().StringVar(&searchMode, "search-mode", "text", 
    "Search ranking mode: text (pure text), hybrid (graph-aware)")
searchCmd.Flags().StringVar(&searchPreset, "search-preset", "",
    "Weight preset for hybrid mode: default, bug-hunting, sprint-planning, impact-first, text-only")
searchCmd.Flags().StringVar(&searchWeightsJSON, "search-weights", "",
    "Custom weights JSON (overrides preset)")
```

### Handler Logic

```go
func handleRobotSearch() {
    // 1. Get text search results
    textResults, _ := idx.SearchTopK(queryVec, limit)
    
    // 2. If hybrid mode, apply HybridScorer
    if searchMode == "hybrid" {
        weights := getWeights(searchPreset, searchWeightsJSON)
        scorer := search.NewHybridScorer(weights, metricsCache)
        
        var hybridResults []search.HybridScore
        for _, r := range textResults {
            score, _ := scorer.Score(r.IssueID, r.Score)
            hybridResults = append(hybridResults, score)
        }
        
        // Re-sort by hybrid score
        sort.Slice(hybridResults, func(i, j int) bool {
            return hybridResults[i].FinalScore > hybridResults[j].FinalScore
        })
        
        outputHybridJSON(hybridResults, weights)
    } else {
        outputTextJSON(textResults)
    }
}
```

## JSON Output Format

### Text Mode (existing, unchanged)
```json
{
  "generated_at": "2025-01-15T...",
  "data_hash": "abc123",
  "query": "authentication",
  "mode": "text",
  "results": [
    {"issue_id": "bv-abc", "score": 0.85, "title": "..."}
  ]
}
```

### Hybrid Mode (new)

title: TUI integration: hybrid search toggle
description:
## Objective

Add hybrid search mode to the TUI with a keyboard toggle, allowing users to switch between text-only and graph-aware ranking.

## Background

TUI semantic search (pkg/ui/semantic_search.go) currently uses pure vector similarity. This task adds:
- 'H' key to toggle hybrid mode (consistent with heatmap toggle in graph view)
- Status bar indicator showing current mode
- Hybrid scores displayed in results

## UI Changes

### Keyboard Shortcut

Add 'H' to toggle hybrid mode in search results:
```
Press 'H' for hybrid ranking (currently: text)
```

### Status Bar

Show current mode in footer:
```
[Search: hybrid/default] | [42 results] | n/N: next/prev | H: toggle mode
```

### Result Display

Show hybrid score when in hybrid mode:
```
[0.87] bv-abc: Fix authentication timeout    [P1] [open]
       └── text: 0.85 | pagerank: 0.72 | impact: 0.45
```

## Implementation

### State Addition (pkg/ui/semantic_search.go)

```go
type SemanticFilter struct {
    // existing fields...
    hybridMode   bool
    hybridPreset search.PresetName
    scorer       search.HybridScorer
}

func (f *SemanticFilter) ToggleHybridMode() {
    f.hybridMode = !f.hybridMode
    f.recomputeResults()
}
```

### Modified ComputeSemanticResults

```go
func (f *SemanticFilter) ComputeSemanticResults(query string, issues []model.Issue) {
    textScores := computeTextScores(query, issues) // existing
    
    if f.hybridMode {
        for i, score := range textScores {
            hybrid, _ := f.scorer.Score(score.IssueID, score.Score)
            textScores[i].Score = hybrid.FinalScore
            textScores[i].ComponentScores = hybrid.ComponentScores
        }
        // Re-sort by hybrid score
        sort.Slice(textScores, func(i, j int) bool {
            return textScores[i].Score > textScores[j].Score
        })
    }
}
```

### Key Handler (pkg/ui/board.go or relevant file)

```go
case "H", "h":
    if m.semanticFilter != nil {
        m.semanticFilter.ToggleHybridMode()
        return m, tea.Batch(refreshCmd)
    }
```

## Preset Cycling

Allow cycling through presets with Shift+H:
- default → bug-hunting → sprint-planning → impact-first → text-only → default

## Success Criteria

- [ ] 'H' key toggles hybrid mode
- [ ] Status bar shows current mode
- [ ] Results re-ranked when mode toggled

title: Web export: Add graph metrics to SQLite export
description:
## Objective

Include graph metrics (PageRank, betweenness, blocker count) in the SQLite database exported for the web viewer, enabling client-side hybrid scoring.

## Background

Currently, graph metrics are computed by bv but not included in the --export-pages SQLite output. The web viewer can only do FTS5 text search.

This task extends the SQLite schema to include metrics, making hybrid search possible in the browser.

## Schema Changes

### Add Columns to issue_overview_mv

```sql
-- Extend the existing materialized view
CREATE TABLE issue_overview_mv (
    -- existing columns...
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    status TEXT,
    priority INTEGER,
    title TEXT,
    description TEXT,
    labels TEXT,  -- JSON array
    -- NEW: graph metrics
    pagerank REAL DEFAULT 0.5,
    betweenness REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
    blocker_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    dependent_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    critical_depth INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    in_cycle INTEGER DEFAULT 0  -- boolean as int
);
```

### Populate During Export

Modify sqlite_export.go to include metrics from graph_layout.json:

```go
func (e *SQLiteExporter) populateMetrics(tx *sql.Tx) error {
    // Load graph_layout.json
    layout, _ := e.loadGraphLayout()
    
    for issueID, metrics := range layout.Metrics {
        // metrics[0]=pagerank, [1]=betweenness, [2]=criticalDepth, 
        // [3]=blockerCount, [4]=inCycle
        _, err := tx.Exec(`
            UPDATE issue_overview_mv 
            SET pagerank = ?, betweenness = ?, blocker_count = ?, 
                critical_depth = ?, in_cycle = ?
            WHERE id = ?`,
            metrics[0], metrics[1], int(metrics[3]), 
            int(metrics[2]), int(metrics[4]), issueID)
    }
    return nil
}
```

## Data Flow

```
bv --export-pages
    │
    ├── Write issues to issue_overview_mv
    ├── Compute graph layout (graph_layout.json)
    │       └── Contains Metrics map[string][5]float64
    └── Populate metrics columns from graph_layout
```

## Metrics Mapping

From graph_layout.json Metrics array:
- [0] → pagerank (REAL)
- [1] → betweenness (REAL)
- [2] → criticalDepth (INTEGER)
- [3] → blockerCount (INTEGER)
- [4] → inCycle (INTEGER, 0/1)

## Backward Compatibility

- New columns have DEFAULT values
- Older exports without metrics still work (neutral values)
- No breaking changes to existing queries

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Schema includes new metric columns
- [ ] Export populates metrics from graph analysis
- [ ] Default values for missing metrics
- [ ] Existing export tests pass
- [ ] New test verifies metrics present
- [ ] No performance regression in export

## Files to Modify

- pkg/export/sqlite_schema.go (schema definition)
- pkg/export/sqlite_export.go (populate metrics)
- tests/e2e/export_pages_test.go (verify metrics)

## Dependencies

- Depends on: bv-xbar.1 (interface design for consistency)
- Blocked by: None (can start immediately)
- Blocks: bv-xbar.8 (JS hybrid scorer needs this data)

title: [RC-S5 proof] Prove action routing for live, historical and workspace sources
description:
## Independent proof target
handleRobotNext emits br update <display ID> --status=in_progress. Workspace loader rewrites local safe to api-safe, so a workspace root with no tracker receives an unusable or misdirected command. --as-of HEAD --robot-next emits a mutation command from a historical snapshot too. Source paths in envelopes are not consulted for action construction. --robot-triage has independent claim_top helpers. Ordinary next correctly refuses missing direct blockers, but that does not establish a live mutation target.

## Behavior that must be established
Preserve original issue ID and resolved repository identity before namespacing. Build action metadata centrally using source authority and readiness, covering triage/next/brief/exports and emitted scripts. Historical sources, arbitrary read-only files and ambiguous routes remain useful analyses but emit no live mutation command unless revalidated against the actual live target. For validated live workspace items include working directory, local ID and safely quoted argv-derived command. Support current br/bd identity deliberately; never strip a prefix heuristically. This task changes suggestions only and does not auto-claim any issue.

## Required unit/integration/E2E coverage
Isolated real trackers in two repos with colliding local IDs and different namespace prefixes; run only generated show/read-only commands automatically, use an argv-recording executable for mutation suggestion checks. Cover historical item now closed, custom --db, BEADS_DIR/BEADS_DB, redirects/worktrees, missing metadata, partial source and shell metacharacters/spaces. Assert no command targets the audit/user repository or historical display ID.

## Test workmanship and closure
Extend existing test files and harnesses. Test public behavior with a deliberately broken case/old-code negative control; do not merely mirror the implementation or assert keys exist. Log fixture/seed, source revision, argv, relevant nonsecret environment, expected and observed IDs/state, stdout/stderr and exit code on failures. Preserve artifacts for diagnosis. Run focused tests plus existing affected-package suite; use race tests for shared state and real platform/browser execution only where this task requires it. Never count a skipped prerequisite or missing runner as passed. This proof task depends on bv-xbvo.9; it can be designed beforehand but closes only after the real implementation and evidence succeed.
design: Ambition rounds: recommendations do not reserve work. Where supported, route an atomic br update <original-id> --claim suggestion to the real repository and let the tracker revalidate at execution. No static snapshot can guarantee future claim success. Preserve origin identity rather than stripping arbitrary prefixes. Historical/ambiguous/incomplete inputs get analysis but no mutation helpers, including nested triage.commands and generated scripts. Quote using an argv-based representation; do not interpolate issue IDs into shell text.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Independently verify: Valid live suggestions use original ID and verified target directory, never a namespace-stripped guess.
- [x] Independently verify: Historical, unknown-route and incomplete sources emit no nested or top-level mutation helper.
- [ ] Independently verify: Special characters remain literal argv values; concurrent claims require authoritative tracker revalidation.
- [x] Capture positive and negative control evidence with source revision, fixture, argv, expected/observed values and failure artifacts.
- [ ] Required real-service/platform/browser runs are completed where specified; no skipped prerequisite is marked passed.
notes: Refinement 4: bound the claim-routing contract to the installed br/bd capability, not a guessed future flag. Test live status changing after snapshot as an expected rejected claim by the tracker, not a bv guarantee. Inspect all nested command fields and emitted scripts; issue_id, source_repo and source_path labels alone are not proof of the correct mutable target.

title: [RC-S1 proof] Prove empty label scopes never widen the result set

At a90029b8 cmd/bv/main.go:2704 computes a label subgraph but assigns it only when IssueCount>0. Closed predecessor bv-3n9s.2 did not test an empty intersection.

## Required behavior
Always apply the selected empty set. Define label matching consistently with the existing documented matching policy and keep empty label input distinct from a nonempty unmatched label. Preserve requested scope and source metadata in empty output, with zero counts, empty lists, and no claim helpers. Apply combined repo/label/recipe filters without falling back to the full project. Extend existing main/registry paths rather than introduce an alternate dispatcher.

## Verification and acceptance

Assert actual result IDs and counts, scope metadata and absence of all mutation helpers. Negative control: the current six-issue fixture must fail because absent-label returns two tasks.

## Delivery constraints

title: [RC-S2] Make robot search honor scope and use the shared provenance envelope
description:
## Observed gap and background
cmd/bv/main.go sets issuesForSearch before --label and --recipe are applied and indexes that earlier slice. Search output is built separately and omits source_path/source_kind/scope. On the six-record Authentication fixture, --robot-search --recipe actionable returns all six, including api-closed and api-defer; --label backend also returns unrelated web-9 and ops-1. Both source binary and verified published v0.23.0 reproduce this. Predecessors bv-3n9s.1/.2 are closed; scoping E2E explicitly skips search.

## Required implementation
Use the shared selected-result IDs and authoritative dependency context from S3. Enforce scope before final ranking/limit so excluded high scorers cannot consume the result budget. Choose a scoped index or full index plus eligible-candidate filtering deliberately; preserve an unscoped cache and avoid destructive index churn between scopes. Build text and hybrid payloads from RobotContext.Envelope and bind their reported hashes/configuration to the intended source and candidate set. Keep exact-ID promotion, lexical boost, presets, custom weights and CLI-over-env precedence.

## Verification and acceptance
Text and hybrid modes; each filter and combined/absent filters; top-k with excluded leaders; score threshold; exact IDs; cache warm/cold and alternating scopes; --as-of; reordered input. Assert correct IDs, component scores, full envelope, and no contamination from out-of-scope index rows. Negative control reproduces all-six scoped results and missing envelope.

## Delivery constraints
Work in existing implementation/test files where sensible. Do not delete files, rewrite unrelated work, create compatibility shims, or run browser-opening product actions. Build, vet, first-party formatting and relevant tests must pass after implementation. Retain concise failing-before/passing-after evidence with source revision, fixture identity, command, exit code and observed-versus-expected results. The companion test bead is required for completion of this gap.
design: Ambition rounds: selected candidates and full dependency authority are distinct. Apply candidate eligibility before top-k and score threshold, including exact-ID promotion. Alternate scopes against the same cache without losing unscoped documents. Include source, scope and effective ranking configuration in identity; fixes must preserve existing text/hybrid relevance behavior for unscoped runs.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Text and hybrid search exclude api-closed/api-defer under actionable scope and unrelated records under label scope.
- [ ] Eligible lower-ranked records fill top-k even when excluded records score higher.
- [ ] Alternating scopes preserve index correctness; source/scope/hash metadata is present.
- [ ] A focused regression fails before this change and passes afterward; affected build/vet/format/tests pass.
notes: Refinement 4: source_hash, scope identity and selected-result hash are different concepts. Keep existing data_hash semantics explicit and use a distinct field if effective-set identity is needed. Test malformed stored index and scoped cache re-use without overwriting the unscoped corpus; exact-ID promotion cannot bypass scope.

title: [RC-S2 proof] Prove scoped search results, limits, caching and provenance
description:
## Independent proof target
cmd/bv/main.go sets issuesForSearch before --label and --recipe are applied and indexes that earlier slice. Search output is built separately and omits source_path/source_kind/scope. On the six-record Authentication fixture, --robot-search --recipe actionable returns all six, including api-closed and api-defer; --label backend also returns unrelated web-9 and ops-1. Both source binary and verified published v0.23.0 reproduce this. Predecessors bv-3n9s.1/.2 are closed; scoping E2E explicitly skips search.

## Behavior that must be established
Use the shared selected-result IDs and authoritative dependency context from S3. Enforce scope before final ranking/limit so excluded high scorers cannot consume the result budget. Choose a scoped index or full index plus eligible-candidate filtering deliberately; preserve an unscoped cache and avoid destructive index churn between scopes. Build text and hybrid payloads from RobotContext.Envelope and bind their reported hashes/configuration to the intended source and candidate set. Keep exact-ID promotion, lexical boost, presets, custom weights and CLI-over-env precedence.

## Required unit/integration/E2E coverage
Text and hybrid modes; each filter and combined/absent filters; top-k with excluded leaders; score threshold; exact IDs; cache warm/cold and alternating scopes; --as-of; reordered input. Assert correct IDs, component scores, full envelope, and no contamination from out-of-scope index rows. Negative control reproduces all-six scoped results and missing envelope.

## Test workmanship and closure
Extend existing test files and harnesses. Test public behavior with a deliberately broken case/old-code negative control; do not merely mirror the implementation or assert keys exist. Log fixture/seed, source revision, argv, relevant nonsecret environment, expected and observed IDs/state, stdout/stderr and exit code on failures. Preserve artifacts for diagnosis. Run focused tests plus existing affected-package suite; use race tests for shared state and real platform/browser execution only where this task requires it. Never count a skipped prerequisite or missing runner as passed. This proof task depends on bv-xbvo.3; it can be designed beforehand but closes only after the real implementation and evidence succeed.
design: Ambition rounds: selected candidates and full dependency authority are distinct. Apply candidate eligibility before top-k and score threshold, including exact-ID promotion. Alternate scopes against the same cache without losing unscoped documents. Include source, scope and effective ranking configuration in identity; fixes must preserve existing text/hybrid relevance behavior for unscoped runs.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Independently verify: Text and hybrid search exclude api-closed/api-defer under actionable scope and unrelated records under label scope.
- [ ] Independently verify: Eligible lower-ranked records fill top-k even when excluded records score higher.
- [ ] Independently verify: Alternating scopes preserve index correctness; source/scope/hash metadata is present.
- [ ] Capture positive and negative control evidence with source revision, fixture, argv, expected/observed values and failure artifacts.
- [ ] Required real-service/platform/browser runs are completed where specified; no skipped prerequisite is marked passed.
notes: Refinement 4: source_hash, scope identity and selected-result hash are different concepts. Keep existing data_hash semantics explicit and use a distinct field if effective-set identity is needed. Test malformed stored index and scoped cache re-use without overwriting the unscoped corpus; exact-ID promotion cannot bypass scope.

title: [RC-S3] Preserve dependency truth while filtering plans, triage, recipes and TUI
description:
## Observed gap and background
pkg/analysis/plan.go:isBlockedAfterCompletions ignores blocking references absent from issueMap. CLI --repo removes blockers before analysis; ComputeLabelSubgraph retains only one context hop. For api-1/backend -> web-1/frontend -> ops-1/ops, --repo api promotes api-1 and --label backend promotes web-1, though both are blocked. Triage marks api-1 claimable, while robot-next's separate direct-blocker guard refuses it. recipe.Filter only checks direct open blockers. All existing tests pass; closed bv-3n9s.2 and bv-9hti.1 do not cover this composition.

## Required implementation
Represent authoritative loaded issues separately from selected output IDs and any display-context nodes. Compute readiness from full dependency authority, then project candidates into requested scope. Consolidate ready/blocked/claimable predicates used by analysis, triage, next, recipes and TUI; distinguish in-progress work from newly claimable open/unassigned tasks. Preserve parent-child inherited blocking, tombstones, deferral, epic exclusions and closed blockers. Unknown required dependencies must yield unknown/blocked eligibility with a reason, never become satisfied through filtering. Keep scoped metrics explicit about their graph; do not require full expensive graph metrics merely to decide readiness.

## Verification and acceptance
Deterministic independent graph oracle over chains, diamonds, cycles, missing IDs, parent chains/cycles/depth boundary, mixed edge types, closed/tombstoned blockers, assigned/in-progress/epic/deferred tasks and defer_until clock boundary. E2E compare claimability across plan, triage, next and actionable recipe before/after scopes. Regression counterexample above must fail old code. Preserve valid cross-label context for exploration without recommending those nodes as in-scope work.

## Delivery constraints
Work in existing implementation/test files where sensible. Do not delete files, rewrite unrelated work, create compatibility shims, or run browser-opening product actions. Build, vet, first-party formatting and relevant tests must pass after implementation. Retain concise failing-before/passing-after evidence with source revision, fixture identity, command, exit code and observed-versus-expected results. The companion test bead is required for completion of this gap.
design: Ambition rounds: dependency state is satisfied/unsatisfied/unknown. Unknown records or truncated parent traversal never become satisfied. For fixed authority and clock, ready(scope) is a subset of ready(all) intersect selected IDs. Verify with an independent small-graph oracle plus permutations. Context-only graph nodes never become scope-selected candidates. Build forward/reverse adjacency once per snapshot. Keep dependency-ready, open/unassigned/nondeferred, scope eligibility, source completeness and ranking readiness separate; avoid parallel implementations drifting again.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] api-1 and web-1 remain dependency-blocked after repo/label projection.
- [x] Independent oracle agrees across missing references, parents, cycles, status, assignee and deferral boundaries.
- [x] Plan/triage/next/actionable recipe/TUI share readiness semantics without dropping exploratory context.
- [x] A focused regression fails before this change and passes afterward; affected build/vet/format/tests pass.
notes: Refinement 4: do not force identical result lists across distinct APIs. Preserve dependency-ready planning (including ongoing work where documented) separately from open/unassigned/non-epic claim candidates. Shared predicates must agree on each fact, and fields/docs must identify which set a count represents. On the new tracker, bv plan counts 11 dependency-ready records including 3 epics while br ready lists 8 tasks; this distinction must be explicit and must not silently remove useful planning records. Also test ready candidates beyond the top three so a rejected leader cannot hide every valid next action.

title: [RC-S3 proof] Prove readiness invariants across filters and all consumers
description:
## Independent proof target
pkg/analysis/plan.go:isBlockedAfterCompletions ignores blocking references absent from issueMap. CLI --repo removes blockers before analysis; ComputeLabelSubgraph retains only one context hop. For api-1/backend -> web-1/frontend -> ops-1/ops, --repo api promotes api-1 and --label backend promotes web-1, though both are blocked. Triage marks api-1 claimable, while robot-next's separate direct-blocker guard refuses it. recipe.Filter only checks direct open blockers. All existing tests pass; closed bv-3n9s.2 and bv-9hti.1 do not cover this composition.

## Behavior that must be established
Represent authoritative loaded issues separately from selected output IDs and any display-context nodes. Compute readiness from full dependency authority, then project candidates into requested scope. Consolidate ready/blocked/claimable predicates used by analysis, triage, next, recipes and TUI; distinguish in-progress work from newly claimable open/unassigned tasks. Preserve parent-child inherited blocking, tombstones, deferral, epic exclusions and closed blockers. Unknown required dependencies must yield unknown/blocked eligibility with a reason, never become satisfied through filtering. Keep scoped metrics explicit about their graph; do not require full expensive graph metrics merely to decide readiness.

## Required unit/integration/E2E coverage
Deterministic independent graph oracle over chains, diamonds, cycles, missing IDs, parent chains/cycles/depth boundary, mixed edge types, closed/tombstoned blockers, assigned/in-progress/epic/deferred tasks and defer_until clock boundary. E2E compare claimability across plan, triage, next and actionable recipe before/after scopes. Regression counterexample above must fail old code. Preserve valid cross-label context for exploration without recommending those nodes as in-scope work.

## Test workmanship and closure
Extend existing test files and harnesses. Test public behavior with a deliberately broken case/old-code negative control; do not merely mirror the implementation or assert keys exist. Log fixture/seed, source revision, argv, relevant nonsecret environment, expected and observed IDs/state, stdout/stderr and exit code on failures. Preserve artifacts for diagnosis. Run focused tests plus existing affected-package suite; use race tests for shared state and real platform/browser execution only where this task requires it. Never count a skipped prerequisite or missing runner as passed. This proof task depends on bv-xbvo.5; it can be designed beforehand but closes only after the real implementation and evidence succeed.
design: Ambition rounds: dependency state is satisfied/unsatisfied/unknown. Unknown records or truncated parent traversal never become satisfied. For fixed authority and clock, ready(scope) is a subset of ready(all) intersect selected IDs. Verify with an independent small-graph oracle plus permutations. Context-only graph nodes never become scope-selected candidates. Build forward/reverse adjacency once per snapshot. Keep dependency-ready, open/unassigned/nondeferred, scope eligibility, source completeness and ranking readiness separate; avoid parallel implementations drifting again.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Independently verify: api-1 and web-1 remain dependency-blocked after repo/label projection.
- [x] Independently verify: Independent oracle agrees across missing references, parents, cycles, status, assignee and deferral boundaries.
- [x] Independently verify: Plan/triage/next/actionable recipe/TUI share readiness semantics without dropping exploratory context.
- [x] Capture positive and negative control evidence with source revision, fixture, argv, expected/observed values and failure artifacts.
- [x] Required real-service/platform/browser runs are completed where specified; no skipped prerequisite is marked passed.
notes: Refinement 4: do not force identical result lists across distinct APIs. Preserve dependency-ready planning (including ongoing work where documented) separately from open/unassigned/non-epic claim candidates. Shared predicates must agree on each fact, and fields/docs must identify which set a count represents. On the new tracker, bv plan counts 11 dependency-ready records including 3 epics while br ready lists 8 tasks; this distinction must be explicit and must not silently remove useful planning records. Also test ready candidates beyond the top three so a rejected leader cannot hide every valid next action.

title: Unit test: suggestions.go - Core suggestion types and interfaces
description:
Create comprehensive unit tests for pkg/analysis/suggestions.go

## File Overview
suggestions.go defines the core types and interfaces for the suggestion system:
- SuggestionType enum (dependency, duplicate, label, cycle)
- Suggestion struct with confidence scoring
- SuggestionResult aggregation

## Test Cases to Implement
1. **Type Tests**
   - Verify SuggestionType string representations
   - Test confidence score normalization (0.0-1.0 bounds)
   - Validate priority ordering

2. **Suggestion Creation**
   - Create suggestions with all field combinations
   - Test empty/nil field handling
   - Validate ID generation if applicable

title: History: Adaptive Three-Pane Layout
description:
# History: Adaptive Three-Pane Layout

## Problem Statement
The current History view uses a fixed 40%/60% split regardless of terminal width. On modern wide screens (150+ columns), this wastes valuable space. Users with wide terminals should see more information at once.

## Design

### Responsive Breakpoints
\`\`\`
< 100 cols:  Two-pane (current behavior, optimized)
100-150 cols: Three-pane standard
> 150 cols:  Three-pane wide with timeline
\`\`\`

### Layout Configurations

#### Narrow (< 100 cols)
\`\`\`
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BEADS            │ COMMITS              │
│                  │                      │
│ 45%              │ 55%                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

#### Standard (100-150 cols)
\`\`\`
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BEADS         │ COMMITS           │ DETAILS                  │
│               │                   │                          │
│ 30%           │ 35%               │ 35%                      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

#### Wide (> 150 cols)
\`\`\`
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BEADS        │ TIMELINE         │ COMMITS          │ DETAILS              │
│              │                  │                  │                      │
│ 20%          │ 25%              │ 25%              │ 30%                  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

### Implementation

\`\`\`go
type historyLayout int

const (
    layoutNarrow   historyLayout = iota // < 100 cols
    layoutStandard                      // 100-150 cols
    layoutWide                          // > 150 cols
)

func (h *HistoryModel) determineLayout() historyLayout {
    if h.width < 100 {
        return layoutNarrow
    } else if h.width < 150 {
        return layoutStandard
    }
    return layoutWide
}

func (h *HistoryModel) View() string {
    layout := h.determineLayout()
    
    switch layout {
    case layoutNarrow:
        return h.renderTwoPaneView()
    case layoutStandard:
        return h.renderThreePaneView()
    case layoutWide:
        return h.renderWidePaneView() // With timeline
    }
}
\`\`\`

### Pane Focus Management
With three panes, Tab cycles through:
1. Primary list (beads or commits)
2. Secondary list (commits or beads)
3. Details panel

Visual indicator shows which pane is focused (border color).

### Responsive Details
- Narrow: Truncate aggressively, show essentials
- Standard: Show full commit messages, file counts
- Wide: Show file list inline, full timestamps

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Layout adapts based on terminal width
- [ ] Breakpoints at 100 and 150 columns
- [ ] Tab cycles through all visible panes
- [ ] Focus indicator (border color) accurate
- [ ] Content adjusts to available width
- [ ] No layout jumps on small width changes (hysteresis)

## Technical Notes
- Consider caching layout calculation (avoid recomputing on every render)
- Test with various terminal widths: 80, 100, 120, 150, 200
- Handle terminal resize gracefully
close_reason: Implemented adaptive three-pane layout with breakpoints at 100/150 cols

title: Viewport: Validate performance benchmarks
description:
## Task: Validate Performance Benchmarks

### Background

After implementing viewport scrolling, we need to verify the performance improvements meet our targets. The benchmarks in `tree_bench_test.go` should show significant improvement.

### Current benchmark results (before viewport)

```
BenchmarkTreeRender/50_visible_80x24:   ~1.8ms
BenchmarkTreeRender/100_visible_120x40: ~9.9ms
BenchmarkTreeRender/200_visible_160x50: ~38ms  <- EXCEEDS TARGET
BenchmarkTreeRender100:                 ~6.6ms
```

### Target results (after viewport)

```
BenchmarkTreeRender/50_visible_80x24:   < 1ms
BenchmarkTreeRender/100_visible_120x40: < 2ms
BenchmarkTreeRender/200_visible_160x50: < 5ms  <- Now within target
BenchmarkTreeRender100:                 < 2ms
```

The key insight: with viewport scrolling, render time should be O(viewport height), not O(total nodes). So 200 nodes with viewport of 50 should render as fast as 50 nodes.

### Validation steps

1. **Run benchmarks before changes** (baseline)
   ```bash
   go test -bench=BenchmarkTreeRender -benchmem ./pkg/ui/... > bench_before.txt
   ```

2. **Run benchmarks after changes**
   ```bash
   go test -bench=BenchmarkTreeRender -benchmem ./pkg/ui/... > bench_after.txt
   ```

3. **Compare results**
   ```bash
   benchstat bench_before.txt bench_after.txt
   ```

### Expected improvements

| Benchmark | Before | After | Improvement |
|-----------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Render 50 nodes | ~1.8ms | ~0.5ms | 3.6x |
| Render 100 nodes | ~9.9ms | ~1ms | 10x |
| Render 200 nodes | ~38ms | ~2ms | 19x |

### Memory allocation improvements

With viewport rendering:
- String builder allocates only for visible lines
- No style computation for non-visible nodes
- Expected: 50-80% reduction in allocations

### Test to add

```go
// BenchmarkTreeRenderLargeWithViewport specifically tests viewport impact
func BenchmarkTreeRenderLargeWithViewport(b *testing.B) {
    theme := DefaultTheme(lipgloss.NewRenderer(nil))
    issues := generateHierarchyIssues(100, 4, 4) // ~1000 issues
    
    tree := NewTreeModel(theme)
    tree.Build(issues)
    tree.SetSize(120, 40) // Viewport of 40 lines
    tree.ExpandAll()
    
    // Scroll to middle
    tree.cursor = tree.NodeCount() / 2
    tree.ensureCursorVisible()
    
    b.ReportAllocs()
    b.ResetTimer()
    
    for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
        _ = tree.View()
    }
    
    // Target: < 5ms for 1000 issues with 40-line viewport
}
```

### Files to modify
- `pkg/ui/tree_bench_test.go` - Add new benchmarks, update existing if needed

### Success Criteria
- [ ] All render benchmarks meet targets (< 5ms for visible viewport)
- [ ] Memory allocations reduced by > 50%
- [ ] No performance regression for small trees
- [ ] benchstat shows statistically significant improvement

### Dependencies
- bv-db02 (windowed rendering) - must be complete to measure

### Notes
- Run benchmarks multiple times for statistical significance
- Use `-count=10` for benchstat comparison
- Document results in commit message
